"avant" points to a past situation, so the imparfait is used, and "Tu" takes the ending -ais: "habitais".
Describing how he was at school calls for the imparfait of être, and "Il" takes the form "était".

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (avoir) un chien quand nous étions jeunes.
questions.explanation: The subject "nous" takes the imperfect ending -ions, and "quand nous étions jeunes" signals a past state, so "avions" is right.
questions.meaning: we had, we used to have

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (aller) souvent à la plage en été.
questions.explanation: The subject "vous" takes the imperfect ending -iez, and "souvent" signals a past habit, so "alliez" is right.
questions.meaning: you used to go, you were going

questions.explanation: The subject "elles" is plural third person, which takes -aient, and "toujours ... le dimanche" shows a habit, so "mangeaient" is right.
questions.meaning: they used to eat, they were eating

questions.prompt: Je ___ (faire) du vélo tous les jours.
questions.explanation: The subject "je" takes the imperfect ending -ais, and "tous les jours" signals a repeated past habit, so "faisais" is right.
questions.meaning: I used to do, I was doing

questions.explanation: The subject "tu" takes the imperfect ending -ais, and "chaque été" signals a repeated past habit, so "venais" is right.
questions.meaning: you used to come, you were coming

questions.explanation: The subject "il" takes the imperfect ending -ait, and the sentence describes how he used to speak, so "parlait" is right.
questions.meaning: he used to speak, he was speaking

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (finir) toujours nos devoirs avant le dîner.
questions.explanation: The subject "nous" takes -ions, and the imperfect stem of finir is "finiss-", so with "toujours" (a past habit) "finissions" is right.
questions.meaning: we used to finish, we were finishing

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (savoir) déjà nager à cet âge.
questions.explanation: The subject "vous" takes the imperfect ending -iez, and the sentence describes a past ability, so "saviez" is right.
questions.meaning: you knew, you used to know

questions.explanation: The subject "elles" is plural third person, which takes -aient, and "toujours" shows a past habit, so "voulaient" is right.
questions.meaning: they wanted, they used to want

questions.prompt: Quand il pleuvait, nous ___ (rester) à la maison.
questions.explanation: The subject "nous" takes -ions, and "quand il pleuvait" sets up a repeated past situation, so "restions" is right.
questions.meaning: we stayed, we used to stay

questions.explanation: The subject "elle" takes the imperfect ending -ait, and "autrefois" signals a past habit, so "chantait" is right.
questions.meaning: she used to sing, she was singing

questions.prompt: Il ___ (croire) encore au père Noël à six ans.
questions.explanation: The subject "il" takes the imperfect ending -ait (croire becomes "croy-"), and "à six ans" describes a past state, so "croyait" is right.
questions.meaning: he believed, he used to believe

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (vivre) à la campagne à cette époque.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nous" takes the imperfect ending -ions, and "à cette époque" signals a past habit or state, so "vivions" fits.
questions.meaning: we lived, we used to live

questions.prompt: Tu ___ (lire) beaucoup quand tu étais jeune.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tu" takes the imperfect ending -ais, and "quand tu étais jeune" points to a past habit, so "lisais" is right.
questions.meaning: you used to read, you were reading

questions.explanation: The plural subject "Elles" takes the imperfect ending -aient, and "toujours" shows a repeated past habit, so "dormaient" is correct.
questions.meaning: they used to sleep, they were sleeping

questions.prompt: Je ___ (prendre) le bus tous les matins.
questions.explanation: The subject "Je" takes the imperfect ending -ais, and "tous les matins" describes a repeated past habit, so "prenais" is correct.
questions.meaning: I used to take, I was taking

questions.prompt: Il ___ (écrire) des lettres à ses amis.
questions.explanation: The singular subject "Il" takes the imperfect ending -ait, and writing letters to friends is a habitual past action, so "écrivait" fits.
questions.meaning: he/she used to write, was writing

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (boire) du lait chaud avant de dormir.
questions.explanation: The subject "Vous" takes the imperfect ending -iez, and drinking warm milk before bed is a past routine, so "buviez" is correct.
questions.meaning: you used to drink, you were drinking

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (attendre) le bus ensemble chaque jour.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nous" takes the imperfect ending -ions, and "chaque jour" shows a repeated past action, so "attendions" is right.
questions.meaning: we used to wait, we were waiting

questions.explanation: The singular subject "Elle" takes the imperfect ending -ait, and "à cette époque" sets a past background, so "riait" is correct.
questions.meaning: she used to laugh, was laughing

questions.explanation: The plural subject "Ils" takes the imperfect ending -aient, and knowing a neighbourhood is a past state, so "connaissaient" is correct.
questions.meaning: they knew, they used to know

questions.prompt: La vie ___ (sembler) plus simple à cette époque.
questions.explanation: The singular subject "La vie" takes the imperfect ending -ait, and "à cette époque" describes how things seemed in the past, so "semblait" is correct.

units.title: Conditionnel Présent
units.description: Being polite and hypothetical — Present conditional for polite requests and hypotheticals.

questions.prompt: Je ___ (vouloir) un café, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: With "Je", the conditional of vouloir ends in -ais, and "s'il vous plaît" calls for a polite request, so "voudrais" (I would like) is right.
The subject "Tu" takes the conditional ending -ais, and the question is a polite invitation, so "aimerais" (would you like) is correct.
questions.meaning: you would like, you would love

questions.explanation: The subject "Il" takes the third-person singular conditional ending -ait on the future stem pourr-, giving "pourrait"; "pourraient" is plural and "pourrais" goes with je/tu.
questions.meaning: he could, he would be able to

questions.explanation: With "Nous" the conditional ends in -ions, so devoir becomes "devrions" (stem devr- + -ions); "devriez" is for vous.
"Vous" takes the conditional ending -iez on the irregular stem saur-, giving "sauriez"; "savriez" wrongly uses the infinitive stem.
The plural subject "Elles" needs the ending -aient on the stem viendr-, giving "viendraient"; "viendrait" is singular.
After "Je" the conditional ends in -ais: prendre drops its final e to give the stem prendr- and so "prendrais", meaning 'I would have a dessert'.
questions.meaning: I would take, I would have

questions.explanation: "Tu" takes the ending -ais on the irregular stem fer- (faire), giving "ferais"; "ferait" is for il/elle and "feraient" for ils/elles.
Être has the irregular conditional stem ser-, and "Il" takes -ait, so the answer is "serait"; "seraient" is plural.
Avoir has the irregular stem aur-, and "Nous" takes -ions, giving "aurions"; "auriez" belongs to vous.
The polite request addresses someone with "Vous", which takes -iez on the stem pourr-, giving "pourriez".
questions.meaning: you could, would you be able to

questions.explanation: Plural "Elles" needs -aient on the irregular stem voudr-, giving "voudraient"; "voudrait" would be singular.

questions.prompt: J'___ (aller) bien si j'avais le temps.
questions.explanation: With "j'" (je) the conditional of aller uses the irregular stem ir- plus -ais, giving "irais", which matches the 'si + imparfait' hypothesis.
questions.example: J'irais bien si j'avais le temps.

questions.explanation: "Tu" takes the ending -ais on the stem dir- (dire), giving "dirais"; "dirait" is for il/elle.
The subject "Il" is third person singular, so the conditional ending is -ait: "verrait". The stem verr- is irregular for voir.
"Nous" takes the conditional ending -ions, and venir has the irregular stem viendr-, giving "viendrions".
"Vous" takes the conditional ending -iez, so aimer becomes "aimeriez"; the polite question means 'would you like'.
"Elles" is third person plural, so the ending is -aient, on the irregular stem saur- of savoir: "sauraient".
"Je" takes the conditional ending -ais, so préférer becomes "préférerais".
"Tu" takes the ending -ais, and devoir has the irregular stem devr-, giving "devrais" ('you should').
The impersonal "Il" with falloir is always singular, and the verb has the irregular stem faudr-, giving "faudrait".
questions.meaning: it would be necessary, we should

questions.explanation: "Nous" takes the conditional ending -ions, so souhaiter becomes "souhaiterions", a polite way to say 'we would like'.
"Vous" takes the ending -iez, and être has the irregular stem ser-, giving "seriez".
"Elles" is third person plural, so the conditional ending is -aient: "adoreraient".
"Je" takes the ending -ais, and boire has the irregular stem boir-, giving "boirais".

units.title: Relative Pronouns
units.description: Qui, que, où, dont — Relative pronouns linking two ideas into one sentence.

questions.prompt: Voici la femme ___ habite à côté.
questions.explanation: The blank is the subject of "habite", so the subject relative pronoun "qui" is needed. "Qu'" would be an object, and "dont" and "où" do not fit.

questions.prompt: C'est le livre ___ je lis en ce moment.
questions.explanation: "que" is right because "le livre" is the direct object of "je lis" (je lis le livre), and "que" replaces a direct object.

questions.prompt: C'est la ville ___ je suis né.
questions.explanation: "où" is right because "la ville" is a place (je suis né dans la ville), and "où" replaces a place.
"dont" is right because the verb is "parler de" (je t'ai parlé de cet homme), and "dont" replaces "de + noun".

questions.prompt: La personne ___ m'a aidé est partie.
questions.explanation: "qui" is right because it is the subject of "m'a aidé" (la personne m'a aidé), and "qui" replaces a subject.

questions.prompt: Le film ___ nous avons vu était génial.
questions.explanation: "que" is right because "le film" is the direct object of "nous avons vu", and the subject "nous" already follows the blank.

questions.prompt: C'est le jour ___ tout a changé.
questions.explanation: "où" is right because "le jour" is a time expression (le jour où tout a changé), and "où" can replace a time.
questions.meaning: when, on which (relative pronoun for time)

questions.prompt: C'est le sujet ___ elle a peur.
questions.explanation: "dont" is right because the expression is "avoir peur de" (elle a peur de ce sujet), and "dont" replaces "de + noun".

questions.prompt: Le chien ___ aboie appartient au voisin.
questions.explanation: "qui" is right because it is the subject of "aboie" (le chien aboie), and "qui" replaces a subject.

questions.prompt: La voiture ___ il a achetée est rouge.
questions.explanation: "qu'" is right because "la voiture" is the direct object of "a achetée", so "que" is needed, and it elides before the vowel in "il".
questions.example: La voiture qu'il a achetée est rouge.

questions.prompt: C'est la raison pour ___ il est parti.
questions.explanation: "laquelle" is right because it follows the preposition "pour" and agrees with the feminine noun "la raison".

questions.prompt: Voici les amis ___ je passe mes vacances.
questions.explanation: "avec qui" is right because the verb needs "avec" (je passe mes vacances avec les amis), and "qui" refers to people after a preposition.

questions.prompt: C'est le restaurant ___ nous avons dîné.
questions.explanation: "où" is right because "le restaurant" is a place (nous avons dîné dans le restaurant), and "où" replaces a place.

questions.prompt: Le livre ___ la couverture est bleue est à moi.
questions.explanation: "dont" replaces de + noun: it is the cover of the book (la couverture du livre), so "dont" means 'whose'.

questions.prompt: La fille ___ chante est ma sœur.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of "chante" (the girl is the one singing), so French uses "qui".
The verb is rêver de (to dream of), so the relative pronoun replacing de + the holidays is "dont".
questions.meaning: of which, about which (replaces de + noun)

questions.prompt: C'est quelque chose ___ je ne comprends pas.
questions.explanation: "quelque chose" is the direct object of "je ne comprends pas" (I don't understand something), so the object pronoun "que" is needed.
questions.meaning: that, which (direct object of the clause)

questions.explanation: "le quartier" is a place where the speaker lives (j'habite dans ce quartier), so the place relative "où" is used.

questions.prompt: La personne à ___ j'ai parlé était gentille.
questions.explanation: After the preposition à, a relative pronoun referring to a person is "qui" (à qui = to whom).
questions.meaning: whom, after a preposition (à qui = to whom)

questions.prompt: C'est un projet ___ nous sommes fiers.
questions.explanation: The expression is fier de (proud of), so de + the project becomes "dont".

questions.prompt: Voilà la maison ___ appartient à mes grands-parents.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of "appartient" (the house belongs to my grandparents), so "qui" is used.
questions.meaning: which, that, who (subject of the clause)

questions.prompt: Le sac ___ tu cherches est sous la table.
questions.explanation: "Le sac" is the direct object of "tu cherches" (you are looking for the bag), and "tu" is the subject, so "que" is used.
questions.meaning: that, which (direct object of the clause)

questions.prompt: C'est l'année ___ nous nous sommes rencontrés.
questions.explanation: After a time noun like "l'année", French uses "où" to mean 'when' (the year when we met).
questions.meaning: when (relative pronoun after a time word)

questions.prompt: Le collègue ___ le bureau est là-bas m'a aidé.
questions.explanation: The office belongs to the colleague (le bureau du collègue), so "dont" expresses 'whose'.

questions.prompt: C'est une histoire ___ je me souviens bien.
questions.explanation: The verb is se souvenir de (to remember), so de + the story becomes "dont".

units.title: Object Pronouns
units.description: Le, la, les, lui, leur — Direct and indirect object pronouns.

questions.prompt: Je ___ vois tous les jours (mon frère).
questions.explanation: "le" replaces "mon frère", a masculine direct object of "voir" (you see someone, no "à"), so the direct pronoun "le" is needed.

questions.prompt: Je ___ vois tous les jours (ma sœur).
questions.explanation: "la" replaces "ma sœur", a feminine direct object of "voir", so you need the feminine direct pronoun "la", not the indirect "lui".
"les" replaces "mes amis", a plural direct object of "voir", so the plural direct pronoun "les" is needed; "leur" is only for indirect objects.
"parler à" takes an indirect object, and "à moi" means 'to me', so the pronoun is "me"; "lui" would mean to him or her.
"à toi" is 'to you' (informal), so the indirect pronoun before "parle" is "te"; "lui" and "leur" refer to third persons.
"parler à son collègue" has a singular indirect object, so it becomes "lui" (to him or her); "leur" is plural and "le" is a direct pronoun.

questions.prompt: Il ___ parle souvent (à ma sœur et moi).
questions.explanation: "à ma sœur et moi" means 'to my sister and me', which is 'to us', so the first-person plural pronoun "nous" is used before the verb.
"à eux/elles" is a plural indirect object after "parler à", so it is replaced by "leur"; "les" would be a direct object.
"ce livre" is a direct object of "aimer", and "le" elides before the vowel in "aime", giving "l'"; "les" is plural and "lui" is indirect.
questions.example: Je l'aime beaucoup.

questions.explanation: "mes parents" is a plural direct object of "voir" (note the agreement in "vus"), so you need "les"; "leur" is indirect and "l'" is singular.
questions.example: Je les ai vus hier.

questions.prompt: Tu ___ as dit la vérité (à moi) ?
questions.explanation: "dire quelque chose à quelqu'un" takes an indirect object, and "à moi" is 'to me', so "me" elides to "m'" before the vowel in "as".
questions.example: Tu m'as dit la vérité ?

questions.prompt: Nous ___ avons offert un cadeau (à elle).
questions.explanation: "offrir à quelqu'un" takes an indirect object, and "à elle" is singular, so it becomes "lui"; "leur" would be plural.

questions.prompt: Vous ___ avez appelées (ma sœur et moi) hier.
questions.explanation: The bracket says the callers called "ma sœur et moi", so the direct object is us, which is "nous"; the participle "appelées" agrees with it (feminine plural).
questions.example: Vous nous avez appelés hier.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ a envoyé une lettre (à eux).
questions.explanation: Envoyer takes "à" + person, so the pronoun is indirect, and "à eux" is plural, giving "leur" ("lui" would be singular).
"ce pull" is a masculine singular direct object of acheter, so it is replaced by "l'" (elided before the vowel in acheter); "les" is plural and "lui" is indirect.
questions.example: Je vais l'acheter.

questions.explanation: Inviter takes a direct object, and "ses amis" is plural, so it becomes "les" placed before the infinitive.
The bracket says the person to help is "moi", so the pronoun is "m'" (me), elided before the vowel of aider.
questions.example: Peux-tu m'aider ?

questions.prompt: Je ___ ai donné mon numéro (à toi).
questions.explanation: The bracket "à toi" means the number is given to you, so the pronoun is "t'" (te, elided before ai).
questions.example: Je t'ai donné mon numéro.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ a présenté son projet (à mes collègues et moi).
questions.explanation: The bracket "à mes collègues et moi" includes the speaker, so the indirect object is us: "nous" ("leur" would exclude the speaker).
The bracket says the people thanked "moi", so the pronoun is first-person "m'", elided before the vowel of ont.
"ce sujet" is a masculine singular direct object, so the pronoun is "le" ("la" is feminine, "les" plural, "lui" indirect).
The bracket "elle" gives a feminine singular direct object (rencontrer takes no "à"), so "l'" fits, and the participle "rencontrée" agrees with it.
questions.example: Nous l'avons rencontrée hier.

questions.explanation: Écrire takes "à" + person, and "à eux" is plural, so the indirect pronoun is "leur".

questions.prompt: Il ___ a expliqué la situation (à elle).
questions.explanation: Expliquer takes "à" + person, and "à elle" is singular, so the indirect pronoun is "lui" ("leur" would be plural).
"le" is right because "connaître" takes a direct object and "cet homme" is masculine singular, so it is replaced by "le"; "lui" is indirect and "la"/"les" do not match.

units.title: Y and En
units.description: Two small but essential pronouns — The pronouns y (place/idea) and en (quantity/of it).

questions.prompt: Tu vas à Paris ? Oui, j'___ vais demain.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces a place introduced by "à", here "à Paris", so it means "there" in "j'y vais".

questions.prompt: Il pense à son avenir ? Oui, il ___ pense souvent.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces "à" plus a thing or idea ("à son avenir"), as "penser à" requires; "lui" is only for people.

questions.prompt: Elle a des enfants ? Oui, elle ___ a deux.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "des enfants" and stays when a number is given, so "elle en a deux" means "she has two of them".

questions.prompt: Tu veux du café ? Oui, j'___ veux bien.
questions.explanation: "en" is correct here. The pronouns y (place/idea) and en (quantity/of it).

questions.prompt: Vous allez à la fête ? Oui, nous ___ allons.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces the place "à la fête" after "aller", so "nous y allons" means "we are going there".

questions.prompt: Il parle de son travail ? Oui, il ___ parle beaucoup.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "de son travail" after "parler de", so "il en parle" means "he talks about it".

questions.prompt: Tu crois à cette histoire ? Oui, j'___ crois.
questions.explanation: "y" is correct here. The pronouns y (place/idea) and en (quantity/of it).

questions.prompt: Elle a besoin d'aide ? Oui, elle ___ a besoin.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "d'aide" after "avoir besoin de", so "elle en a besoin" means "she needs it".

questions.prompt: Nous répondons à la question ? Oui, nous ___ répondons.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces "à la question", a thing after "répondre à", so "nous y répondons"; "lui" would be for a person.

questions.prompt: Ils ont peur des araignées ? Oui, ils ___ ont peur.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "des araignées" after "avoir peur de", so "ils en ont peur" means "they are afraid of them".

questions.prompt: Tu penses souvent à elle ? Oui, j'___ pense souvent.
questions.explanation: "y" is correct here. The pronouns y (place/idea) and en (quantity/of it).
questions.example: Tu penses souvent à ton examen ? Oui, j'y pense souvent.

questions.prompt: Vous voulez des fruits ? Oui, nous ___ voulons.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "des fruits", a noun introduced by the indefinite article "des" (some fruit), and it goes before the verb: "nous en voulons".

questions.prompt: Il habite à Lyon ? Oui, il ___ habite.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces the place "à Lyon" (a location introduced by "à"), so the answer is "il y habite".

questions.prompt: Elle revient de vacances ? Oui, elle ___ revient.
questions.explanation: "revenir de" takes "en", which replaces "de vacances" (coming back from somewhere): "elle en revient".

questions.prompt: Vous vous intéressez à l'art ? Oui, nous nous ___ intéressons.
questions.explanation: S'intéresser takes à, and "y" replaces à + a thing (à l'art); it goes after the reflexive "nous" and before the verb.

questions.prompt: Tu as combien de livres ? J'___ ai dix.
questions.explanation: "en" stands for the counted noun "livres" and stays in the sentence when the number is given: "j'en ai dix".
questions.meaning: of them (stands for the counted noun)

questions.prompt: Il va souvent au cinéma ? Oui, il ___ va souvent.
questions.explanation: "y" replaces the place "au cinéma", and "aller" is not reflexive, so "il y va" with no "s'".

questions.prompt: Vous avez assez de temps ? Oui, nous ___ avons assez.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "de temps" (the quantity after "assez de"), so "nous en avons assez".

questions.prompt: Elle s'habitue à sa nouvelle vie ? Oui, elle ___ habitue.
questions.explanation: "s'habituer à" is reflexive and "à sa nouvelle vie" becomes "y", so the pronoun "s'y" combines both: "elle s'y habitue".

questions.prompt: Tu te souviens de ce jour ? Oui, je m'___ souviens.
questions.explanation: "se souvenir de" takes "en" for "de ce jour", and "en" elides after "me" before the verb: "je m'en souviens".

questions.prompt: Il tient à son travail ? Oui, il ___ tient beaucoup.
questions.explanation: "tenir à" takes "y" to replace "à son travail", and "tenir" is not reflexive, so "il y tient" without "s'".

questions.prompt: Nous avons besoin de conseils ? Oui, nous ___ avons besoin.
questions.explanation: "avoir besoin de" takes "en" to replace "de conseils": "nous en avons besoin".
questions.example: Il a besoin de conseils ? Oui, il en a besoin.

questions.prompt: Elle réfléchit à la question ? Oui, elle ___ réfléchit.
questions.explanation: "réfléchir à" takes "y" to replace "à la question", and the verb is not reflexive: "elle y réfléchit".

questions.prompt: Tu manges des légumes ? Oui, j'___ mange tous les jours.
questions.explanation: "en" replaces "des légumes" (a quantity of something introduced by de/des), so it goes before the verb: "j'en mange".

questions.prompt: Il croit encore au succès ? Oui, il ___ croit toujours.
questions.explanation: The verb is "croire au succès" (croire à + thing), and "y" replaces an à + noun phrase, so it goes before the verb: "il y croit".

units.title: Environment & Nature
units.description: Talking about the natural world — Nature and environment vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "la nature" is spelled like the English word but is feminine, so it takes la.
"la forêt" means forest; it is feminine and keeps the circumflex on the ê.
"la montagne" means mountain; it is feminine, so it takes la.
"la rivière" is the everyday word for river; le lac is a lake, not a river.
"le lac" means lake; despite ending in -ac, it is masculine.
"la mer" means sea and is feminine; do not confuse it with la mère (mother), which sounds the same.
"l'océan" means ocean; it is masculine (un océan), and le becomes l' before the vowel.
"le ciel" means sky; le soleil is the sun in the sky, not the sky itself.
"le soleil" means sun; it is masculine, so you say le soleil and un soleil.
moon → la lune. Nature and environment vocabulary.
"l'étoile" means star; it is feminine (une étoile), and la becomes l' before the vowel.
"l'arbre" means tree; it is masculine (un arbre), and le becomes l' before the vowel.
"la fleur" means flower and is feminine, even though most nouns ending in -eur are masculine.
"l'herbe" means grass; it is feminine, and the h is silent, so la becomes l'.
"la pierre" is the feminine noun for stone, a piece of rock; "le sable" is sand and "le ciel" is the sky.
"le sable" is the masculine noun for sand, as on a beach; "la forêt" is a forest and "le soleil" is the sun.
"la terre" means earth, both the ground or soil and, with a capital, the planet; "la mer" is the sea and "la fleur" is a flower.
"l'air" is the masculine noun for the air we breathe, written with l' because it starts with a vowel; "le vent" is the wind.
pollution → la pollution. Nature and environment vocabulary.
"le recyclage" is the masculine noun for recycling; like most nouns ending in -age, it takes le.
"l'environnement" means the environment; note the French spelling with two n's in the middle and the masculine article shortened to l'.
"le climat" means climate and is masculine; the final t is silent.
"l'énergie" is the feminine noun for energy, written with l' before the vowel; "le soleil" is the sun, not energy itself.
"renouvelable" means renewable, as in une énergie renouvelable; "durable" means sustainable and "polluant" means polluting.
"durable" means sustainable, as in le développement durable; "renouvelable" means renewable, which is a different idea.

units.title: Technology & the Internet
units.description: Talking about being online — Internet and computing vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "le réseau" is the masculine noun for a network, as in un réseau Wi-Fi or les réseaux sociaux; "les données" means data.
"la connexion" means connection, as in "une connexion Internet"; note the French spelling with -xion, not -ction.
"le logiciel" means software, the programs that run on a computer; "le serveur" and "l'écran" are machines or hardware.
"le matériel" is the physical equipment of a computer (hardware), as opposed to "le logiciel", the software.
"le fichier" is any file stored on a computer; "la pièce jointe" is only a file attached to an email.
"le dossier" is the folder where you group files on a computer, as in "ouvrir un dossier".
"les données" means data and is normally plural in French, as in "les données personnelles".
"le nuage" literally means a cloud in the sky and is also used for cloud storage ("stocker dans le nuage"); many people also just say "le cloud".
"le serveur" is the computer that stores data and sends websites to other machines, just like "server" in English.
"le navigateur" is the program you use to browse websites, such as Firefox or Chrome; it comes from "naviguer", to browse.

questions.prompt: The French word for "search engine" is…
questions.explanation: "le moteur de recherche" (literally "search motor") is the tool you use to search the web, such as Google.

questions.prompt: The French word for "social media" is… ___
questions.explanation: "les réseaux sociaux" (literally "social networks") is the usual French for social media and is used in the plural.
"le compte" is the account you create on a website or service ("créer un compte"); "le profil" is only the page that shows your details.
"le profil" is your personal page on a website or social network, with your photo and details. It is masculine, so it takes "le".
"la mise à jour" is an update to software or an app; literally it means 'a putting up to date' (mettre à jour = to update).
"la notification" is the alert an app or phone sends you. Like most nouns ending in -tion, it is feminine.
"le lien" is a clickable link on a web page or in a message; "la connexion" is your internet connection, not a link.
"la pièce jointe" is a file attached to an email; literally it means 'joined piece', from joindre (to attach).

questions.prompt: The French word for "computer virus" is…
questions.explanation: "le virus" is the same word as in English and is used for computer viruses too; note that it is masculine and the final s is pronounced.
"la sécurité" means security or safety, online or offline. Nouns ending in -té are usually feminine, so it takes "la".
"la sauvegarde" is a saved copy of your data, from sauvegarder (to save or back up). It is feminine.
"l'appareil" means any device, such as a phone or tablet. It is masculine, and "le" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
"l'écran" is the display of a phone, computer or TV. It is masculine, and "le" becomes "l'" before the vowel.

questions.prompt: The French word for "app" (on a phone) is…
questions.explanation: "l'application" is an app on a phone or tablet (people also say "l'appli"); "le logiciel" is software in general.
"le paramètre" is an option you can change on a device or in an app; the settings menu is usually called "les paramètres".

units.title: Emotions & Feelings, In Depth
units.description: Describing subtler feelings — More nuanced emotion vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "le soulagement" is the feeling you get when a worry or pain ends. The other options mean admiration, satisfaction and serenity.
"la gratitude" is the feeling of being thankful. It looks like the English word but is feminine, so it takes "la".
"le regret" is the feeling of wishing you had acted differently. It is spelled like the English word and is masculine, so it takes "le".
"l'espoir" means hope. It is a masculine noun, and "le" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
"le désespoir" means despair, the loss of all hope. It is built from "espoir" (hope) with the prefix dé-.
"l'enthousiasme" means enthusiasm. The h is silent, so the article is elided to "l'". It is a masculine noun.
"l'anxiété" means anxiety, a strong feeling of worry. It is feminine, and "la" becomes "l'" before the vowel.
"la satisfaction" is spelled like the English word and means the same thing. Like most nouns ending in -tion, it is feminine.
"la déception" means disappointment, not deception (deception is "la tromperie"). It is a classic false friend.
"la fierté" means pride. It is a feminine noun formed from the adjective "fier" (proud).
"la honte" means shame, the opposite of "la fierté" (pride). Its h is aspirated, so there is no elision: "la honte", never "l'honte".
"la culpabilité" means guilt, the feeling of having done wrong. It is related to the adjective "coupable" (guilty).

questions.prompt: The French word for "the feeling of sharing someone's pain and wanting to help" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la compassion" is the feminine noun for sharing someone's suffering and wanting to help; it is spelled exactly like the English word "compassion".
"l'envie" is the feminine noun for envy, and it can also mean a wish or craving; the article elides to l' before the vowel.

questions.prompt: The French word for "a feeling of great respect and approval for someone" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'admiration" is the feminine noun for great respect and approval; it is spelled like English and takes l' before the vowel.
"la confiance" is the feminine noun for trust, as in "avoir confiance en quelqu'un" (to trust someone).
"le doute" is the masculine noun for doubt, as in "j'ai un doute" (I have a doubt); note it ends in -oute with no b.
"le courage" is the masculine noun for bravery; it is spelled like the English word "courage" but takes the masculine article le.

questions.prompt: The French word for "the ability to wait calmly without getting annoyed" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la patience" is the feminine noun for calmly waiting without getting annoyed, as in "Il faut de la patience".
"la tendresse" is the feminine noun for tenderness or gentle affection, formed from the adjective "tendre" (tender).
"la nostalgie" is the feminine noun for a longing for the past; English -ia becomes French -ie.
"la sérénité" is the feminine noun for calm peace of mind; English -ity becomes French -ité, and words ending in -ité are feminine.
"l'irritation" is the feminine noun for annoyance; it is spelled like English and takes l' before the vowel.
"la mélancolie" is the feminine noun for a gentle, lingering sadness; note the é and the -ie ending where English has -y.
"le contentement" is the masculine noun for a calm, quiet satisfaction, built from the adjective "content" (pleased). Don't confuse it with "le désespoir" (despair) or "la culpabilité" (guilt).

units.title: Media & News
units.description: Talking about the press — Media and journalism vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "les nouvelles" is a plural noun meaning the news, as in "les nouvelles du jour". On TV and radio the French also say "les informations" ("les infos").
"le journal" is the newspaper you read every day. "le gros titre" is a headline, "le reportage" is a news report and "l'abonnement" is a subscription.
"le magazine" is masculine in French even though it ends in -e, so you say "un magazine". "le direct" means a live broadcast and "la radio" is the radio.
"l'article" is a masculine noun ("un article") for a piece of writing in a newspaper or magazine. "la source" is where the information comes from.
"le journaliste" is the person who gathers and reports the news. "le lecteur" is the reader, and "la rumeur" is a rumour.
"le titre" is the title printed above an article, so it is the headline. A big front-page headline is "le gros titre", and "le journal" is the newspaper itself.
"le reportage" is a news report or feature made by a journalist on the spot. "le titre" is a headline and "l'abonnement" is a subscription.
"l'interview" is a question-and-answer session with a journalist, and it is usually feminine: "une interview". "le reportage" is a report and "le direct" means live.
"la diffusion" is the act of broadcasting a programme on TV or radio, from the verb "diffuser". A single programme is "une émission".
"la chaîne" is a TV or radio channel, as in une chaîne de télévision; the same word also means chain.
"la radio" is feminine in French: you say "écouter la radio". "le public" is the audience and "la source" is where information comes from.
"le podcast" is a borrowed English word and is masculine in French: "écouter un podcast". "l'interview" is an interview and "l'opinion" is an opinion.
"la publicité" means an advert or advertising in general (informally "la pub"); "la presse" is the press and "la diffusion" is broadcasting.
"l'abonnement" means subscription and comes from s'abonner (to subscribe); it is masculine: un abonnement.
"le public" is the audience of a show or media outlet; it is masculine singular even though it refers to many people.
"le rédacteur" is the person who writes and edits articles for a newspaper; the chief editor is "le rédacteur en chef".
"la presse" means the press, meaning newspapers and journalists as a whole; it is feminine.

questions.prompt: The French word for "latest news" is… ___
questions.explanation: "les dernières nouvelles" literally means "the last news", the most recent news; "le gros titre" is a headline.
"l'opinion" is the same word as in English and is feminine (une opinion, l'opinion publique).
"la censure" is the act of banning or cutting information; note it is feminine and ends in -ure, not -ship.

questions.prompt: The French word for "freedom of speech" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la liberté d'expression" literally means freedom of expression and is the usual French term for freedom of speech.
"la source" is spelled as in English but is feminine; journalists protect "leurs sources".
"la rumeur" is unconfirmed information that spreads; it is feminine despite ending in -eur.
"le gros titre" is the big headline on the front page, literally "the big title".

questions.prompt: The French word for "live broadcast" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le direct" is a live broadcast; the adverb form is "en direct" (live), as in « une émission en direct ».

units.title: Education System
units.description: Talking about school and university — Education vocabulary from school to university.

questions.explanation: "l'école" is the general word for school (and for primary school); "l'enseignant" is the teacher.

questions.prompt: The French word for "high school" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le lycée" is the French high school for ages 15–18, after "le collège" (middle school).
"l'université" means university; it is feminine (une université), and la becomes l' before the vowel.
"le diplôme" is the general word for a degree or diploma; specific university degrees are "la licence" or "le master".

questions.prompt: The French word for "course" (a class you attend) is…
questions.explanation: "le cours" is a class or lesson you attend, as in "un cours de maths"; "le programme" is the syllabus or curriculum, not the class itself.
A school subject is "la matière" (Quelle est ta matière préférée ?); le sujet means a topic, not a school subject.

questions.prompt: The French word for "grade" (a mark on a test) is…
questions.explanation: "la note" is the mark a teacher gives your work, as in "J'ai eu une bonne note"; "le cours" is the lesson itself, not the mark.

questions.prompt: The French word for "exam (education system)" is… ___
questions.explanation: exam (education system) → l'examen. Education vocabulary from school to university.

questions.prompt: The French word for "homework (education system)" is…
questions.explanation: homework (education system) → les devoirs. Education vocabulary from school to university.

questions.prompt: The French word for "teacher (in the education system)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'enseignant" is the general word for a teacher at any level, from the verb enseigner (to teach). A female teacher is l'enseignante.
"l'étudiant" is a student at university or in higher education. A school pupil is un élève.

questions.prompt: The French word for "classroom (education system)" is…
questions.explanation: "la salle de classe" literally means 'the room of class', the room where lessons take place. Le lycée is the whole high school, not one room.
"la bourse" is money given to a student to pay for their studies, as in obtenir une bourse (to get a scholarship).
"le programme" is the set of subjects and content taught in a course or school year, so it is the French word for curriculum.
"le semestre" is one half of the academic year. Notice that it is masculine even though it ends in -e.
"le cours magistral" is a university lecture given by a professor to a large audience. Beware: une lecture in French means 'a reading'.
"les frais de scolarité" means the fees paid for schooling, which is tuition. Frais is always plural.
"la remise des diplômes" literally means 'the handing out of degrees', the graduation ceremony. Le diplôme is the degree itself.

questions.prompt: The French word for "library (education system)" is… ___
questions.explanation: library (education system) → la bibliothèque. Education vocabulary from school to university.
"la recherche" is academic research, from the verb rechercher (to search for). Faire de la recherche means to do research.
"la thèse" is the long research work written for a doctorate, just like an English thesis. Note the grave accent on the è.
"l'alphabétisation" means learning to read and write, as in le taux d'alphabétisation (the literacy rate).
"la maternelle" (short for l'école maternelle) is the French nursery school for ages 3 to 6, the stage before primary school.

questions.prompt: The French word for "principal" (head of a school) is… ___
questions.explanation: "le directeur" is the head of a school ("la directrice" for a woman); in a French lycée the head is also called "le proviseur".

questions.prompt: The French word for "report card" is…
questions.explanation: "le bulletin" is the school report with a pupil's grades, sent home each term; "la remise des diplômes" is a graduation ceremony.

units.title: Health & Wellness
units.description: Talking about staying healthy — Health and wellness vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "la santé" means health in general, as in "être en bonne santé"; "la guérison" is recovery from an illness.
"le bien-être" (literally 'well-being') is the general state of feeling good in body and mind; the other options name specific things such as stress or a symptom.
"l'exercice" is physical exercise, as in "faire de l'exercice"; note the French spelling with -ice and the elided article l'.

questions.prompt: The French word for "diet" (as in going on a diet) is…
questions.explanation: "le régime" is a controlled way of eating, as in "suivre un régime"; what you eat every day in general is "l'alimentation".
"le sommeil" is the noun for sleep, as in "manquer de sommeil"; the verb 'to sleep' is "dormir".
"le stress" is borrowed from English and keeps the same spelling, but it is masculine and pronounced the French way.
"la relaxation" is the act of relaxing and is feminine, like most nouns ending in -tion; "le bilan de santé" is a health check-up.
"la nutrition" is the direct French equivalent of nutrition, a feminine noun like most words ending in -tion. "Une alimentation équilibrée" means a balanced diet, which is a different idea.
Vitamin is "la vitamine" in French. It is feminine and adds a final -e that English doesn't have.

questions.prompt: The French word for "immune system" is…
questions.explanation: Immune system is "le système immunitaire". Système is masculine despite its -e ending, and the adjective is immunitaire, placed after the noun.

questions.prompt: The French word for "mental health" is…
questions.explanation: Mental health is "la santé mentale". Santé is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine form mentale and comes after the noun.
Therapy is "la thérapie". English -y often becomes -ie in French, and these nouns are usually feminine.
Meditation is "la méditation". It is feminine like most -tion nouns and takes an accent on the first é.
"la forme physique" means physical fitness, as in être en bonne forme physique (to be fit); le régime is a diet, not fitness.

questions.prompt: The French word for "balanced diet" is…
questions.explanation: "une alimentation équilibrée" is the usual phrase for a balanced diet: alimentation means the food you eat, and équilibrée agrees with this feminine noun.
Hydration is "l'hydratation", with an extra -at- compared with English. The article elides to l' because the h is silent.
"la guérison" is recovery from an illness, from the verb guérir (to heal, to get better).
Prevention is "la prévention". It is feminine like most -tion nouns and takes an accent on the é.
"le bilan de santé" is a medical checkup: un bilan is an overall assessment, here of your health.
Symptom is "le symptôme". It is masculine despite the final -e and has a circumflex on the ô.
Treatment is "le traitement", from the verb traiter (to treat). Nouns ending in -ment are masculine.
Vaccine is "le vaccin". It is masculine and, unlike the English word, has no final -e.
"la dépendance" is the everyday word for addiction, as in la dépendance au tabac (nicotine addiction).
Habit is "l'habitude", a feminine noun with the article elided before a silent h. Be careful: French un habit means a piece of clothing, not a habit.
"le mode de vie" literally means 'way of life', which is what 'lifestyle' means; "le bien-être" means 'well-being', not lifestyle.

units.title: Housing & Renting
units.description: Finding a place to live — Renting and housing vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "le loyer" is the rent you pay each month; la caution is the deposit and le locataire is the tenant.
"le bail" is the lease, the rental contract you sign with the landlord; le préavis is the notice period.
"le propriétaire" is the owner, so for a rented flat it is the landlord who receives the rent.
"le locataire" is the person who rents and pays the rent; the owner who rents the place out is "le propriétaire".
"la caution" is the sum you pay the landlord at the start and get back when you leave, which is the deposit; "le bail" is the lease.
"les charges" are the costs paid on top of the rent, such as water, heating and building upkeep, which is what 'utilities' refers to; "le loyer" is the rent itself.
"meublé" describes a flat that is rented with its furniture, which is what 'furnished' means; "spacieux" means spacious.
"non meublé" adds 'non' (not) to "meublé" (furnished), so it means a flat rented without furniture.

questions.prompt: The French word for "studio apartment" is…
questions.explanation: "le studio" is a one-room flat with its own kitchen corner and bathroom, the same word as in English.
"le colocataire" is 'co-' plus "locataire" (tenant): a person you share a rented flat with, a roommate or flatmate.

questions.prompt: The French word for "to move (relocate)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "déménager" means to leave your home and move to another one; "louer" means to rent and "rénover" means to renovate.
"le quartier" is the part of a town where you live, the neighbourhood; "l'immeuble" is only the building.

questions.prompt: The French word for "real estate agency" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'agence immobilière" is the business that rents and sells flats and houses for owners, a real estate agency; "immobilier" means property.
"le prêt immobilier" is a loan ("prêt") from a bank to buy property ("immobilier"), which is a mortgage; "le bail" is a rental lease.
"l'assurance" is insurance; for example, a tenant in France must take out home insurance ("l'assurance habitation").
"l'entretien" is the maintenance or upkeep of a home, as in "les frais d'entretien"; "le loyer" is the rent.
"la rénovation" is the work done to renovate a home, as in "des travaux de rénovation"; "le rangement" means storage or tidying.
"le balcon" is the small outdoor platform attached to a flat, as in "un appartement avec balcon".
"l'ascenseur" is the lift (elevator) that takes you between floors; it takes l' because ascenseur starts with a vowel.
"l'étage" is a floor or level of a building, as in "au troisième étage" (on the third floor).

questions.prompt: The French word for "lease agreement" is…
questions.explanation: "le contrat de location" is the written lease signed by the tenant and the landlord ("le propriétaire").

questions.prompt: The French word for "notice (to vacate)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le préavis" is the notice a tenant gives before moving out, as in "donner son préavis"; "le bail" is the lease itself.
"la propriété" is a property you own, such as a house with its land; "la caution" is the deposit and "le préavis" is the notice period.

questions.prompt: The French word for "square meter" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le mètre carré" (m²) is the unit French housing ads use for floor area, as in « un appartement de 45 mètres carrés ».
"le rangement" is the housing word for storage space, as in « un appartement avec beaucoup de rangements ».

units.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de)
units.description: Verbs that need à or de — Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.

lessons.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de) 1
lessons.subtitle: Verbs that need à or de

questions.explanation: "à" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
"de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
The verb « hésiter » is followed by "à" before an infinitive: hésiter à faire quelque chose.
"de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
The verb « réussir » is followed by "à" before an infinitive: réussir à faire quelque chose.

lessons.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de) 2
lessons.subtitle: Verbs that need à or de

questions.prompt: Vous avez oublié ___ fermer la porte.
questions.explanation: "de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.

questions.prompt: Ils réussissent ___ finir dans les délais.
questions.explanation: "à" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
questions.meaning: réussir à: to succeed in, manage to

questions.explanation: "de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
"à" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
"de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.

lessons.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de) 3
lessons.subtitle: Verbs that need à or de

questions.explanation: "à" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
questions.meaning: s'intéresser à: to be interested in

questions.explanation: "de" is correct here. Common verbs requiring à or de before an infinitive or noun.
The verb s'habituer takes "à" before a noun: s'habituer à quelque chose, so "à ce nouveau rythme".
The verb essayer is followed by "de" before an infinitive when it means to try to: essayer de comprendre.
The verb hésiter takes "à" before an infinitive: hésiter à accepter means to hesitate to accept.

lessons.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de) 4
lessons.subtitle: Verbs that need à or de

questions.explanation: Arrêter takes "de" before an infinitive when it means to stop doing something: arrêter de fumer.
Chercher followed by an infinitive means to try to and takes "à": chercher à résoudre le problème.
questions.meaning: chercher à: to try to, seek to

questions.explanation: Remercier quelqu'un takes "de" (or pour) before the thing you are thankful for: je te remercie "de" ton aide.
The expression se mettre "à" + infinitive means to start doing something: elle s'est mise à pleurer.

questions.prompt: Nous avons envie ___ sortir ce soir.
questions.explanation: The expression avoir envie "de" is always followed by de before an infinitive: nous avons envie de sortir.

lessons.title: Verbs + Prepositions (à/de) 5
lessons.subtitle: Verbs that need à or de

questions.explanation: Refuser takes "de" before an infinitive: refuser de répondre means to refuse to answer.
Tenir "à" + noun means to care about or be attached to something: tu tiens à ce projet.
questions.meaning: tenir à: to care about, be attached to

questions.explanation: Choisir takes "de" before an infinitive: elle a choisi de rester means she chose to stay.
Inviter quelqu'un takes "à" before an infinitive or noun: inviter ses amis à dîner.
The adjective "fier" is followed by "de" to introduce what you are proud of: "fiers de leur travail".

units.title: Passive Voice
units.description: Être + past participle — The passive voice with être and a past participle.

questions.explanation: The subject "la lettre" is feminine singular, so the passive uses singular "est" and the participle takes a feminine -e: "est écrite".
"L'année dernière" signals the past, and "le livre" is masculine singular, so the passive perfect is "a été publié" with no extra -e or -s.
"La maison" is feminine singular and "en 1990" points to the past, so the passive perfect needs a feminine participle: "a été construite".
"Les fenêtres" is feminine plural and "hier" puts the action in the past, so you need "ont été nettoyées" with plural "ont" and a feminine plural participle.

questions.prompt: Le film ___ (réaliser) par un jeune cinéaste.
questions.explanation: "Le film" is masculine singular, so the passive perfect is "a été réalisé"; the infinitive "réaliser" is never used after "été".
"Cette chanson" is feminine singular, so the present passive takes "est" and a feminine participle: "est chantée".
"Le pont" is masculine singular and "le mois dernier" signals the past, so the passive perfect is "a été réparé", not the feminine "réparée".
"Les documents" is masculine plural and "ce matin" points to the past, so you need plural "ont été" and a participle with -s: "ont été signés".
"La décision" is feminine singular and "hier soir" is past, so the participle agrees with it: "a été prise" (not masculine "pris").
"Le repas" is masculine singular and there is no past marker, so the present passive is "est préparé" with no feminine or plural ending.
"Demain" calls for the future, and "les résultats" is masculine plural, so the passive is "seront annoncés" with plural "seront" and -s on the participle.
"a été fondée" is feminine singular to agree with "La ville", and the passé composé of être shows a completed past event (au Moyen Âge).
"Le projet" is masculine singular, so the participle is "a été approuvé" with no feminine or plural ending.
"Les invités" is plural, so the verb is "ont été accueillis" with plural "ont" and a masculine plural participle.

questions.prompt: Le tableau ___ (peindre) par un artiste célèbre.
questions.explanation: "Le tableau" is masculine singular, so the passive is "a été peint"; the participle of peindre agrees and takes no -e.

questions.prompt: La réunion ___ (annuler) à cause de la pluie.
questions.explanation: "La réunion" is feminine singular, so the participle takes -e: "a été annulée".
"Ce roman" is masculine singular, so the passive is "a été traduit" with no extra ending.
"Les billets" is masculine plural, so the verb is "ont été vendus" with plural "ont" and -s on the participle.
"Le prix" is masculine singular, so the passive is "a été remis", with no -e and no plural.

questions.prompt: Cette règle ___ (respecter) par tout le monde.
questions.explanation: "Cette règle" is feminine singular and the action is a present state, so the passive is "est respectée" with -e on the participle.
"Le colis" is masculine singular and the delivery happened yesterday, so the passive is "a été livré".
"Les enfants" is plural and the action is in the present, so the passive is "sont surveillés" with plural "sont" and -s on the participle.
"Le budget" is masculine singular and the action is finished (cette année), so the passive is "a été réduit".
"a été confirmée" is right because the subject "La nouvelle" is feminine singular, so the past participle takes -e after "a été" (passive voice, passé composé).
"a été rénové" agrees with "Ce quartier", which is masculine singular, so the participle has no extra ending.

units.title: Time Expressions
units.description: Depuis, pendant, il y a — Depuis, pendant, and il y a for talking about time.

questions.explanation: "depuis" is used with a present-tense verb for an action that began in the past and is still going on: "J'habite ici depuis cinq ans" (I still live here).

questions.prompt: Nous avons voyagé ___ deux semaines. (duration: for two weeks)
questions.explanation: "pendant" gives the length of a finished action; the trip is over and the verb is in the passé composé, so "depuis" does not fit.

questions.prompt: Il est parti ___ une heure. (point in the past: an hour ago)
questions.explanation: "il y a" means 'ago' and places a past event at a moment back from now, so "Il est parti il y a une heure" means he left an hour ago.
"depuis" goes with a starting point ("2020") and a present-tense verb: she began studying in 2020 and still does.
"pendant" expresses the duration of a completed action in the passé composé: the waiting lasted one whole hour and is over.

questions.prompt: Ils se sont mariés ___ dix ans.
questions.explanation: "il y a" means 'ago': "Ils se sont mariés il y a dix ans" puts the wedding ten years before now.

questions.prompt: Je travaille ici ___ le mois de mars.
questions.explanation: "depuis" marks the starting point ("le mois de mars") of a situation that continues now, with the verb in the present.

questions.prompt: Nous avons vécu à Paris ___ trois ans, de 2015 à 2018.
questions.explanation: "pendant" gives the length of a finished stay: they lived in Paris for three years and no longer do, so "depuis" does not fit.
"il y a" means 'ago' and fits a single completed event: she moved six months ago.

questions.prompt: Tu apprends l'espagnol ___ combien de temps ?
questions.explanation: "depuis" is correct here. Depuis, pendant, and il y a for talking about time.

questions.prompt: Il a plu ___ toute la journée.
questions.explanation: "pendant" fits because "toute la journée" gives a finished stretch of time during which it rained.
"il y a" means 'ago': the film was seen at a point in the past, so "il y a longtemps" means 'a long time ago'.
"depuis" marks the starting point ("l'université") of a situation that is still true now: we have known each other since then.
"pendant" gives the length of a completed action: she slept for ten hours, and that sleep is over.
"il y a" plus a duration says how long ago a past event happened: they moved two years ago.

questions.prompt: Je fais du sport ___ un an maintenant.
questions.explanation: "depuis" is used with the present tense for an action that began in the past and continues now ("maintenant"): I have been exercising for a year.

questions.prompt: Hier soir, nous avons discuté ___ des heures.
questions.explanation: "pendant" expresses how long a finished action lasted: last night they talked for hours, and the conversation ended.
"il y a" with a past tense ("a appelé") tells how long ago the call happened: five minutes ago.
"depuis" is correct here. Depuis, pendant, and il y a for talking about time.
"pendant" covers a completed period: you worked throughout "tout l'été", and it is over (passé composé).

questions.prompt: J'ai fini mes études ___ deux ans.
questions.explanation: "il y a" means 'ago': finishing studies was a past event, so "il y a deux ans" means 'two years ago'.
"depuis" marks the starting point ("notre mariage") of something still going on: we have lived here since our wedding.

questions.prompt: Il a couru ___ une heure sans s'arrêter.
questions.explanation: "pendant" gives the duration of a completed action (he ran for an hour). "depuis" needs an action still going on, and "il y a" means 'ago'.

questions.prompt: Elle a quitté son emploi ___ un mois.
questions.explanation: "il y a" means 'ago' and points back to a past moment: she left her job a month ago. "pendant" gives a duration and "depuis" needs an ongoing situation.
"depuis" with a present tense (je le connais) shows something that began in the past and still continues: I have known him since childhood.

units.title: Making Suggestions & Giving Advice
units.description: Recommending and advising — Common structures for suggestions and advice.

questions.explanation: The subject is "tu", so the conditional of devoir takes the -ais ending: "devrais" gives the polite advice 'you should'.
After "Si j'étais toi" (imperfect) the result clause takes the conditional, and "je" requires the -ais ending: "partirais".

questions.prompt: On ___ (pouvoir) aller au cinéma ce soir.
questions.explanation: The subject "on" takes third-person singular, so the conditional of pouvoir is "pourrait": 'we could go to the cinema'.

questions.prompt: Pourquoi ne pas ___ (to take) un peu de repos ?
questions.explanation: "prendre" is correct here. Common structures for suggestions and advice.
"Il vaudrait mieux" is followed by an infinitive, and "partir" matches the clue 'to leave' (sortir would mean 'go out').

questions.prompt: Je te conseille de ___ (to stay) prudent.
questions.explanation: "Je te conseille de" is followed by an infinitive, and "rester" prudent means 'stay careful', matching the clue.
"Consulter un médecin" is the usual French way to say 'see a doctor', and it follows "tu devrais" as an infinitive: "consulter".

questions.prompt: Ça vaudrait la peine d'___ (to try).
questions.explanation: "essayer" is correct here. Common structures for suggestions and advice.

questions.prompt: À ta place, je ne ___ (dire) rien.
questions.explanation: "À ta place, je..." sets up advice with the conditional, and "je" takes -ais: "dirais" ('I would say').

questions.prompt: Il serait sage de ___ des économies. (to save money)
questions.explanation: "faire" is correct because the fixed expression for saving money is "faire des économies", and "il serait sage de" must be followed by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Tu ferais mieux de ___ (to sleep) tôt ce soir.
questions.explanation: "dormir" is correct because the clue says "to sleep", and "tu ferais mieux de" is followed by an infinitive meaning to sleep early tonight.

questions.prompt: Je te suggère de ___ (to take) quelques jours de vacances.
questions.explanation: "prendre" is correct because "prendre des vacances" is the standard way to say take time off, and "je te suggère de" needs an infinitive.
"essayait" is correct because "et si" for a suggestion takes the imperfect, and "on" takes the third-person singular ending.
"être" is correct because the clue says "to be" and "être plus attentif" means to be more attentive, after "il faudrait" plus an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Tu devrais vraiment ___ (to read) ce livre.
questions.explanation: "lire" is correct because the clue says "to read", which is what you do with a book, and "tu devrais" is followed by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Pourquoi ne pas ___ (to leave) un peu plus tôt ?
questions.explanation: "partir" is correct because the clue says "to leave", and "partir plus tôt" means to set off earlier; "pourquoi ne pas" takes an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Je te recommande de ___ (to try) ce restaurant.
questions.explanation: "essayer" is correct because the clue says "to try", and "essayer ce restaurant" means to try out that restaurant; "je te recommande de" takes an infinitive.
questions.example: Je te recommande d'essayer ce restaurant.

questions.prompt: Il serait préférable de ___ (to wait until) demain.
questions.explanation: "attendre" is correct because the clue says "to wait until" tomorrow, and "il serait préférable de" is followed by an infinitive.
questions.example: Il serait préférable d'attendre demain.

questions.prompt: On devrait ___ (to make) une décision rapidement.
questions.explanation: "prendre" is correct because French says "prendre une décision" for make a decision; "faire une décision" is an English calque.
questions.meaning: to take (prendre une décision: to make a decision)

questions.prompt: Ça serait une bonne idée de ___ (to make) un plan.
questions.explanation: "faire" is correct because "faire un plan" is the usual way to say make a plan, and "une bonne idée de" is followed by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Tu pourrais ___ (to ask) à quelqu'un d'autre.
questions.explanation: "demander" is correct because the clue says "to ask", and "demander à quelqu'un" means to ask someone, after "tu pourrais" plus an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Si j'étais à ta place, je ___ (accepter) cette offre.
questions.explanation: After "Si j'étais..." the main clause takes the conditional, and the subject "je" needs the first-person ending, so "accepterais" is right.
questions.example: Si j'étais à ta place, j'accepterais cette offre.

questions.prompt: Il vaut mieux ___ (to prevent) que guérir.
questions.explanation: This is the set proverb "Il vaut mieux prévenir que guérir" (prevention is better than cure), so "prévenir" is the verb that pairs with "guérir".

questions.prompt: Je te conseille vivement de ___ (to take) ce cours.
questions.explanation: In French you "suivre un cours" to take a class, so "suivre" is the verb that matches "to take" here.

questions.prompt: Tu devrais peut-être ___ (to take) un peu de repos.
questions.explanation: The set phrase is "prendre du repos" (to take some rest), so "prendre" is the verb that follows "Tu devrais peut-être".

units.title: Say It Your Way
units.description: Write the idea in French — Opinions and plans, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say you think the meeting went well.
acceptableAnswers: Je pense que la réunion s'est bien passée.
À mon avis, la réunion était réussie.
Je trouve que la réunion s'est bien déroulée.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je pense que la réunion s'est bien passée." Se passer bien means 'to go well', and passée agrees with la réunion because it is an être verb.

acceptableAnswers: Je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord.
Je vois les choses différemment.
Permettez-moi de ne pas être d'accord.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je ne suis pas tout à fait d'accord." Adding 'pas tout à fait' (not quite) softens the disagreement and makes it polite.

questions.prompt: Say you would like to change your reservation.
acceptableAnswers: Je voudrais modifier ma réservation.
J'aimerais changer ma réservation.
Serait-il possible de modifier ma réservation ?
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je voudrais modifier ma réservation." Je voudrais is the polite conditional for 'I would like', and modifier is the usual verb for changing a booking.

questions.prompt: Explain why you are learning French.
acceptableAnswers: J'apprends le français pour voyager.
J'apprends le français parce que je veux voyager.
C'est pour le travail que j'apprends le français.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'apprends le français pour voyager." Use 'pour' + infinitive or 'parce que' + clause to give your reason.

questions.prompt: Say you would help if you had more time.

J'aimerais aider, mais le temps me manque.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je t'aiderais si j'avais plus de temps." An imaginary condition uses 'si' + imperfect ('j'avais') with the conditional in the main clause ('aiderais').

questions.prompt: Ask for someone's opinion on a decision.
acceptableAnswers: Qu'en penses-tu ?
Quel est ton avis là-dessus ?
Qu'est-ce que tu en penses ?
Qu'en pensez-vous ?
Qu'est-ce que vous en pensez ?
questions.explanation: "Qu'en penses-tu ?" uses en to stand for the decision (penser de quelque chose becomes en penser). With a stranger or a group, say "Qu'en pensez-vous ?"

questions.prompt: Say you regret not calling earlier.
acceptableAnswers: Je regrette de ne pas avoir appelé plus tôt.
J'aurais dû appeler plus tôt.
Je m'en veux de ne pas avoir téléphoné avant.
questions.explanation: "Je regrette de ne pas avoir appelé plus tôt." uses regretter de + a past infinitive, with both ne and pas placed before avoir. "J'aurais dû appeler plus tôt" says the same thing with the past conditional of devoir.

acceptableAnswers: Et si on trouvait un compromis ?

questions.explanation: "Et si on trouvait un compromis ?" uses Et si + imperfect, a friendly way to suggest something. "Un terrain d'entente" means common ground.

questions.prompt: Say you are worried about the exam.

questions.explanation: "Je suis inquiet pour l'examen." uses inquiet pour to say what worries you; a woman writes inquiète.

questions.prompt: Explain that you need more information before deciding.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai besoin de plus d'informations avant de décider.

questions.explanation: "J'ai besoin de plus d'informations avant de décider." uses avoir besoin de for 'need' and avant de + infinitive for 'before deciding'.

questions.prompt: Say you are proud of your progress.

questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je suis fier de mes progrès." 'Être fier de' means to be proud of, and a woman writes 'fière'.

acceptableAnswers: On pourrait reporter la réunion.

questions.explanation: "On pourrait reporter la réunion." softens the suggestion with the conditional. Reporter and repousser both mean to postpone.

questions.prompt: Say you would rather stay home tonight.

questions.explanation: "Je préférerais rester à la maison ce soir." uses the conditional of préférer for 'would rather'. J'aimerais mieux means the same thing.

questions.prompt: Express that a decision was difficult.
acceptableAnswers: Cette décision a été difficile à prendre.

questions.explanation: "Cette décision a été difficile à prendre." uses difficile à + infinitive. In French you say prendre une décision (literally 'take a decision'), not 'make' one.

questions.prompt: Say you are considering a career change.

questions.explanation: "J'envisage de changer de carrière." uses envisager de + infinitive for 'to be considering'. Note that changer de takes no article.

questions.prompt: Ask someone for their honest opinion.

acceptableAnswers: La situation s'est améliorée.

questions.explanation: "La situation s'est améliorée." S'améliorer takes être in the passé composé, so améliorée agrees with la situation.

questions.prompt: Explain you missed the deadline because of an emergency.

questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'ai raté la date limite à cause d'une urgence." 'À cause de' + noun gives the cause, and the passé composé 'j'ai raté' tells a finished past event.

questions.prompt: Say you would travel more if you had the money.

acceptableAnswers: Je doute que ce plan fonctionne.

questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je vais y réfléchir." "Réfléchir à quelque chose" becomes "y réfléchir", because "y" replaces "à + thing".

questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Peux-tu préciser ce que tu veux dire ?" "Préciser" means to spell out more exactly, and "ce que tu veux dire" means "what you mean".

acceptableAnswers: J'apprécie les retours honnêtes.

questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'apprécie les retours honnêtes." "Un retour" is the usual word for feedback, and "apprécier" takes a direct object, so no preposition is needed.

questions.answer: Cette solution est meilleure que la précédente.
questions.explanation: "Cette solution est meilleure que la précédente." uses "meilleure", the irregular comparative of "bonne", to say one solution is better than the previous one. It agrees with the feminine "solution", and you never say "plus bonne".

questions.answer: Je préfère le café au thé.
questions.explanation: "Je préfère le café au thé." shows the pattern "préférer A à B" (to prefer A to B). Here "à + le" contracts to "au" before "thé".
"Il vaut mieux partir tôt." uses "il vaut mieux" + infinitive to give advice: it's better to leave early.
"Selon moi, c'est trop cher." opens with "selon moi" (in my opinion) to introduce a personal view. In "c'est", the "ce" is shortened before "est".

questions.answer: Je trouve que ce livre est ennuyeux.

"Elle a probablement raison." uses "avoir raison" (to be right), not "être". The adverb "probablement" goes right after the verb "a".
"C'est important de bien manger." uses "c'est" + adjective + "de" + infinitive to say that an action is important. This is the usual spoken pattern.

questions.answer: Il est nécessaire de réserver à l'avance.
questions.explanation: "Il est nécessaire de réserver à l'avance." uses "il est" + adjective + "de" + infinitive, a slightly more formal way to say something is necessary. "À l'avance" means in advance.

questions.answer: Je suis content de mes résultats.

"Ce n'est pas si simple." uses "pas si" + adjective (not that / not so) to soften a disagreement. "Ne" becomes "n'" before "est".

units.title: Subjunctive Mood
units.description: Expressing necessity, doubt, and wish — Present subjunctive after common triggers like "il faut que".

questions.prompt: Il faut que je ___ (faire) mes devoirs.
questions.explanation: "Il faut que" requires the subjunctive, and the subject "je" takes the form "fasse" (not the nous, vous or ils forms).

questions.prompt: Il faut que tu ___ (être) à l'heure.
questions.explanation: "Il faut que" requires the subjunctive, and "tu" takes "sois", the subjunctive of être; "es" is the indicative.

questions.prompt: Il faut qu'il ___ (avoir) de la patience.
questions.explanation: "Il faut que" takes the subjunctive, and the subjunctive of avoir for "il" is irregular: "ait" (not "a", which is the indicative).

questions.prompt: Il faut que nous ___ (aller) au rendez-vous.
questions.explanation: After "il faut que" you need the subjunctive, and for "nous" the form of aller is "allions"; "aille", "ailles" and "aillent" belong to other subjects.

questions.explanation: "Je veux que" (a wish) takes the subjunctive, and for "tu" comprendre ends in -es: "comprennes" (with the double n).

questions.explanation: "Il est important que" takes the subjunctive, and for "nous" prendre has the -ions form: "prenions".

units.title: Idiomatic Expressions
units.description: Meaning match — Common French idioms beyond literal translation.

choices: to put the cart before the horse
questions.explanation: "Avoir le cafard" literally means 'to have the cockroach', but it is used to mean "to feel down or depressed", like having the blues.

questions.prompt: The idiom "poser un lapin à quelqu'un" means… ___
bank: to call a spade a spade
questions.explanation: "Poser un lapin à quelqu'un" literally means 'to put a rabbit on someone' and is used to mean "to stand someone up", that is, to not turn up to a meeting.

questions.prompt: The idiom "coûter les yeux de la tête" means…
choices: to have other things to worry about
questions.explanation: "Coûter les yeux de la tête" literally means 'to cost the eyes from your head', so something is so costly it would take what you value most: "to be very expensive".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un chat dans la gorge" means… ___
bank: to kill two birds with one stone
to have a frog in one's throat
questions.answer: to have a frog in one's throat
questions.explanation: French says 'a cat in the throat' where English says "to have a frog in one's throat": both describe a hoarse, croaky voice.

questions.prompt: The idiom "tomber dans les pommes" means…
choices: to be exhausted, at the end of one's rope
questions.explanation: "Tomber dans les pommes" literally means 'to fall into the apples', but the fixed idiom simply means "to faint".

questions.prompt: The idiom "casser les pieds à quelqu'un" means… ___
bank: to have a frog in one's throat
questions.explanation: "Casser les pieds à quelqu'un" literally means 'to break someone's feet' and is used informally to mean "to annoy someone".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le coup de foudre" means…
choices: to fall in love at first sight
questions.explanation: A "coup de foudre" is a lightning strike: love that hits you suddenly, so the idiom means "to fall in love at first sight".

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre la charrue avant les bœufs" means… ___
bank: to put the cart before the horse
to have other things to worry about
questions.answer: to put the cart before the horse
questions.explanation: "Mettre la charrue avant les bœufs" literally means putting the plough before the oxen, which is doing things in the wrong order: "to put the cart before the horse".

questions.prompt: The idiom "appeler un chat un chat" means…
choices: to call a spade a spade
questions.explanation: "Appeler un chat un chat" literally means 'to call a cat a cat', that is, to name things plainly without softening them, so it means "to call a spade a spade".

questions.prompt: The idiom "être dans la lune" means… ___
bank: to call a spade a spade
to have other things to worry about
questions.explanation: "Être dans la lune" literally means 'to be in the moon': your mind is far away from what is happening, so it means "to be daydreaming".

bank: to have a frog in one's throat
questions.explanation: "Avoir la pêche" literally means 'to have the peach'; in everyday French it describes someone full of energy and good spirits, so it means "to feel great and energetic".

questions.prompt: The idiom "faire la grasse matinée" means…
choices: to put the cart before the horse
questions.explanation: "Faire la grasse matinée" literally means 'to make the fat morning', a long, lazy morning spent in bed, so it means "to sleep in".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un poil dans la main" means… ___
bank: to have other things to worry about
questions.explanation: "Avoir un poil dans la main" literally means 'to have a hair in your hand', as if you never use your hand to work, so it means "to be very lazy".

choices: to tell tall tales or lies
to be exhausted, at the end of one's rope
questions.explanation: "Raconter des salades" literally means 'to tell salads', a mixed-up story served up to fool someone, so it means "to tell tall tales or lies".

questions.prompt: The idiom "c'est la fin des haricots" means… ___
bank: to put the cart before the horse
questions.explanation: "C'est la fin des haricots" literally means 'it's the end of the beans'. Beans were the last cheap food left, so running out of them means "it's all over, hopeless".

questions.prompt: The idiom "donner sa langue au chat" means…
questions.explanation: "Donner sa langue au chat" literally means 'to give your tongue to the cat'. You say it when you stop trying to find an answer and ask to be told, so it means "to give up guessing".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir d'autres chats à fouetter" means… ___
bank: to have other things to worry about
to kill two birds with one stone
questions.answer: to have other things to worry about
questions.explanation: "Avoir d'autres chats à fouetter" literally means 'to have other cats to whip': you have more important business than this, so it means "to have other things to worry about".

questions.prompt: The idiom "être au bout du rouleau" means…
choices: to tell tall tales or lies
to fall in love at first sight
to be exhausted, at the end of one's rope
questions.explanation: "Être au bout du rouleau" literally means 'to be at the end of the roll': like a roll that is used up, you have nothing left, so it means "to be exhausted, at the end of one's rope".

questions.prompt: The idiom "prendre ses jambes à son cou" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Prendre ses jambes à son cou" literally means 'to take your legs to your neck', that is, to run off as fast as you can, so it means "to run away quickly".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la tête dans les nuages" means…
choices: to call a spade a spade
questions.explanation: "Avoir la tête dans les nuages" literally means 'to have your head in the clouds': your thoughts are elsewhere, so it means "to be absent-minded".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le bras long" means…
questions.explanation: "Avoir le bras long" literally means "to have a long arm": your reach goes far through the people you know, so it means "to have influence or connections".

questions.prompt: The idiom "tourner autour du pot" means… ___

units.title: Business & Formal French
units.description: Professional written French — Formal phrases for business correspondence and meetings.

questions.prompt: Je vous prie de bien vouloir ___ ma demande.
questions.explanation: After "Je vous prie de bien vouloir" a verb must be an infinitive, so "considérer" fits; the other forms are a participle or conjugated.
questions.meaning: to consider, to give thought to

questions.explanation: "Mon" is masculine, so only "CV" fits; "lettre" and "candidature" are feminine, and a "facture" is not something you attach to an application.

questions.prompt: Nous avons le plaisir de vous ___ à la réunion.
questions.explanation: "Avoir le plaisir de" must be followed by an infinitive, so "inviter" is right; "invité", "invitez" and "inviterons" are other forms.

questions.prompt: Je me permets de vous ___ concernant notre projet.
