questions.explanation: After "Je me permets de vous" the verb must be an infinitive, so "contacter" is right; "contacté", "contactez" and "contacte" are the wrong forms here.
questions.meaning: to contact, to get in touch with

questions.prompt: Dans l'attente de votre ___, je vous prie d'agréer mes salutations.
questions.explanation: After "votre" you need a singular noun, and "dans l'attente de votre réponse" is the standard closing phrase, so "réponse" fits; the plural "réponses" does not agree with "votre".
A meeting "a lieu" (takes place): the fixed expression is "avoir lieu", so "lieu" is right, while "place", "endroit" and "site" cannot be used in this expression.
questions.meaning: place; "avoir lieu" means to take place

questions.prompt: Nous devons ___ le budget avant vendredi.
questions.explanation: After the modal "devons" the verb stays in the infinitive, so "finaliser" is right; "finalisé", "finalisons" and "finalise" are the wrong forms.

questions.prompt: Le contrat a été ___ par les deux parties.
questions.explanation: The passive "a été" needs a past participle agreeing with the masculine singular "contrat", so "signé" is right; "signée" and "signés" do not agree and "signer" is an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Il est nécessaire de ___ les objectifs de l'équipe.
questions.explanation: After "Il est nécessaire de" the verb takes the infinitive, so "clarifier" is right; "clarifié", "clarifiez" and "clarifiait" are conjugated or participle forms that do not fit.

questions.prompt: Nous cherchons à ___ nos parts de marché.
questions.explanation: After the preposition "à" in "Nous cherchons à" the verb is an infinitive, so "augmenter" is right; "augmenté", "augmentons" and "augmentez" are the wrong forms.

questions.prompt: Veuillez ___ un rendez-vous avec le directeur.
questions.explanation: "Veuillez" is followed by an infinitive, so "fixer" is right ("fixer un rendez-vous" means to set an appointment); "fixé", "fixez" and "fixons" are the wrong forms.
The future passive "sera ___" needs a past participle agreeing with the feminine singular "décision", so "prise" is right; "pris" and "prises" do not agree and "prendre" is an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Nous devons ___ nos priorités ce trimestre.
questions.explanation: "Revoir ses priorités" is the set phrase for reassessing priorities, and "devons" needs an infinitive, so "revoir" is right.

questions.prompt: L'entreprise a connu une forte ___ cette année.
questions.explanation: "Une forte" requires a feminine noun, and "croissance" is the feminine word meaning growth; "développement", "essor" and "succès" are masculine and cannot follow "une forte".

questions.prompt: Le rapport doit être ___ avant la fin du mois.
questions.explanation: "Doit être" is followed by a past participle agreeing with the masculine singular "rapport", so "soumis" is right; "soumise" and "soumises" do not agree and "soumettre" is an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Nous sommes ___ de vous informer de ce changement.
questions.explanation: After "Nous sommes" you need an adjective agreeing with the plural subject, and "ravis" (delighted) is the plural masculine form. The other options are infinitive or verb forms ("ravir", "ravissons", "ravit").

questions.prompt: Merci de bien vouloir ___ cette information à toute l'équipe.
questions.explanation: After "bien vouloir" the next verb stays in the infinitive, so "diffuser" is right; "diffusé", "diffusez" and "diffusiez" are a participle and conjugated forms.

questions.prompt: Le projet a été ___ en raison du budget.
questions.explanation: In the passive "a été ___" the past participle agrees with the subject "Le projet", which is masculine singular, so "annulé" is correct. "annulée" and "annulés" do not match the subject.
questions.example: Le projet a été annulé en raison de restrictions budgétaires.

questions.prompt: Notre équipe a ___ un excellent travail.
questions.explanation: After "a" the passé composé needs a past participle, and "accompli" (from accomplir) stays unchanged because the object "un excellent travail" comes after the verb. "accomplie" would wrongly agree, and "accomplir" or "accomplit" are not participles.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ les risques avant de décider.
questions.explanation: "Il faut" is followed by an infinitive, so "évaluer" (to assess) is correct. "évaluez", "évalué" and "évaluant" are not infinitives.

questions.prompt: Le client a exprimé sa ___ envers nos services.
questions.explanation: "sa" is feminine, and a client expressing a positive view of our services fits "satisfaction" (feminine). "mécontentement" and "enthousiasme" are masculine, and "intérêt" is masculine too, so none agree with "sa".

questions.prompt: Nous devons ___ les coûts de production.
questions.explanation: The modal "devons" is followed by an infinitive, so "réduire" (to cut) is correct. "réduit", "réduisons" and "réduisant" are not infinitives.

questions.prompt: La proposition a été ___ à l'unanimité.
questions.explanation: In the passive "a été ___" the participle agrees with the subject "La proposition", which is feminine singular, so "acceptée" is correct. The other forms are masculine or plural.
After the possessive "votre" a noun is needed, and "collaboration" is the noun meaning cooperation. "collaborer", "collaboré" and "collaborons" are verb forms.
"Veuillez" is followed by an infinitive, so "consulter" (to look at) is correct. "consultez", "consulté" and "consultant" cannot follow it.

units.title: Comparatives & Superlatives
units.description: Comparing people and things — Comparative and superlative structures.

questions.prompt: Elle est plus ___ que son frère.
questions.explanation: The adjective after "Elle est plus" agrees with the feminine singular subject "Elle", so "grande" is correct. "grand", "grands" and "grandes" have the wrong gender or number.
After "Il est aussi" you need an adjective agreeing with masculine singular "Il", so "intelligent" is correct. "intelligente" and "intelligents" do not agree, and "intelligemment" is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Cette voiture est moins ___ que l'autre.
questions.explanation: "chère" must agree with the feminine singular noun "voiture" after "est moins", so the feminine singular form is needed.

questions.prompt: C'est le meilleur ___ de la ville.
questions.explanation: "meilleur" is masculine, so it needs a masculine noun, and "restaurant" is the only masculine option; the other three are feminine and would require "meilleure".

questions.prompt: C'est la pire journée de ma ___.
questions.explanation: "la pire journée de ma vie" is the fixed expression for the worst day ever, and feminine "ma" requires a feminine noun like "vie".

questions.prompt: Il court plus ___ que son ami.
questions.explanation: After the verb "court" you need an adverb, and "plus vite" is the regular comparative of "vite"; "bien" would change to "mieux" and "bon"/"meilleur" are adjectives.

questions.prompt: Elle chante aussi ___ que sa sœur.
questions.explanation: "chante" is a verb, so it takes the adverb "bien", and "aussi bien que" expresses equality; "mieux" is only used with "plus".

questions.prompt: Ce livre est moins ___ que le film.
questions.explanation: "intéressant" agrees with the masculine singular noun "livre" after "est moins", so no feminine or plural ending is added.

questions.prompt: C'est le plus haut ___ de Paris.
questions.explanation: "le plus haut" is masculine, so the noun must be masculine, and "bâtiment" is the only one; "tour", "église" and "cathédrale" are feminine and would need "la plus haute".

questions.prompt: Cette solution est la meilleure de ___.
questions.explanation: "la meilleure de toutes" is the set phrase meaning the best of all, and "toutes" agrees with the feminine "solution".

questions.prompt: Il travaille plus ___ que les autres.
questions.explanation: In "travailler dur" the word "dur" works as an invariable adverb, so it takes no feminine or plural ending even though "les autres" is plural.

questions.prompt: Ma maison est aussi ___ que la tienne.
questions.explanation: After "aussi ... que" you need an adjective that agrees with the subject; "maison" is feminine, so the feminine form "spacieuse" is needed.

questions.prompt: Ce plat est moins ___ que je ne le pensais.
questions.explanation: "Plat" is masculine, so the adjective after "moins ... que" takes the masculine form "épicé", which describes how a dish tastes.

questions.prompt: C'est le film le plus ___ que j'aie vu.
questions.explanation: "triste" is an adjective that stays the same for masculine and feminine and agrees with the singular "film"; "tristes" is plural, "tristement" an adverb and "tristesse" a noun.

questions.prompt: Elle est la meilleure de la ___.
questions.explanation: After the superlative "la meilleure", the group being compared needs a noun, and "classe" (feminine, so "de la") is the natural one for a student ranked best among her classmates.

questions.prompt: Il est aussi ___ que le champion.
questions.explanation: After "être" in "aussi ... que" you need an adjective, so "rapide" is right; "vite" is an adverb and cannot follow "est" here.

questions.prompt: Ce quartier est moins ___ que le centre-ville.
questions.explanation: "Ce quartier" is masculine singular, so the adjective after "moins ... que" must be masculine singular: "cher". "Chère", "chers" and "chères" have the wrong gender or number.
"La pire" is feminine singular, so the noun must be feminine: "nouvelle". "Jour", "moment" and "film" are masculine and would need "le pire".
"Parle" is a verb, so it is modified by an adverb in "plus ... que moi": "couramment" (fluently). "Courant", "courante" and "courantes" are adjective forms.

questions.prompt: Cette région est la plus ___ du pays.
questions.explanation: In "la plus ... du pays" the adjective agrees with "région", which is feminine, so you need "belle" and not the masculine "beau".

questions.prompt: Elle est moins ___ que son collègue.
questions.explanation: The subject "Elle" is feminine singular, so the adjective after "moins" takes feminine singular agreement: "patiente". "Patient" is masculine, and "patients" and "patientes" are plural.

questions.prompt: C'est le pire résultat de tous les ___.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression "de tous les temps" means "of all time", so the superlative "le pire résultat de tous les temps" takes "temps". "Heures", "années" and "saisons" do not form this expression.

questions.prompt: Ce trajet est plus ___ que prévu.
questions.explanation: "Trajet" is masculine, so the adjective after "plus" takes the masculine form "long" (plus + adjective + que = more … than).
questions.meaning: long, taking a lot of time

questions.prompt: Il est le meilleur ___ de l'équipe.
questions.explanation: "Il" and "le meilleur" are masculine singular, so the noun must be masculine singular: "joueur". "Joueuse" is feminine, and "joueurs" and "joueuses" are plural.

questions.prompt: Cette histoire est plus ___ que l'autre.
questions.explanation: "Histoire" is feminine singular, and "drôle" has the same form in the feminine, so "plus drôle que l'autre" is correct. "Amusant" is masculine, and "drôles" and "amusants" are plural.

units.title: Reported Speech
units.description: Le discours indirect — Reported speech with tense and pronoun shifts.

questions.explanation: After the past tense "a dit", reported speech shifts the present "est" to the imperfect, and "il" takes the third-person singular ending: "était". "Étais", "étaient" and "étiez" do not agree with "il".
After the past tense "a dit", a future plan ("viendra demain") shifts to the conditional, and "elle" takes the third-person singular ending: "viendrait". The other forms do not agree with "elle".

questions.prompt: Il a expliqué qu'il ___ (avoir) besoin d'aide.
questions.explanation: After the past-tense verb "a expliqué", the reported verb shifts to the imperfect, and the subject "il" takes the third-person singular ending: "avait".
The announcement was made in the past, so the future "partira" becomes the conditional (future in the past). With "elle" it is "partirait".

questions.prompt: Il m'a dit qu'il ___ (finir) le travail hier.
questions.explanation: "Hier" shows the finishing happened before he spoke, so reported speech uses the pluperfect: "avait fini".

questions.prompt: Elle a demandé si je ___ (pouvoir) l'aider.
questions.explanation: The present "peux" shifts to the imperfect after "a demandé", and "je" takes the ending -ais: "pouvais".
questions.meaning: I could, I was able to

questions.prompt: Il a répondu qu'il ne ___ (savoir) pas.
questions.explanation: After "a répondu", the present "sait" shifts to the imperfect, and the subject "il" takes -ait: "savait".

questions.prompt: Elle a expliqué qu'elle ___ (aller) au marché.
questions.explanation: Reported after the past "a expliqué", "elle va" becomes the imperfect, and "elle" takes -ait: "allait".

questions.prompt: Il a dit qu'il ___ (vouloir) partir tôt.
questions.explanation: After "a dit", the present "veut" shifts to the imperfect, and "il" takes -ait: "voulait".
After "m'a demandé", the present "habites" shifts to the imperfect, and "j'" (je) takes -ais: "habitais".

questions.prompt: Il a affirmé qu'il ___ (dire) la vérité.
questions.explanation: After the past "a affirmé", the present "dit" shifts to the imperfect, and "il" takes -ait: "disait".

questions.prompt: Elle a précisé qu'elle ___ (manger) une heure plus tôt.
questions.explanation: "Une heure plus tôt" places the eating before the moment of speaking, so reported speech uses the pluperfect: "avait mangé".
questions.example: Elle a précisé qu'elle avait mangé avant de partir.

questions.explanation: The question "quand arriverez-vous ?" is reported in the past, so the future becomes the conditional, and "nous" takes -ions: "arriverions".

questions.prompt: Elle a dit qu'elle ___ (être) très contente du résultat.
questions.explanation: After the past verb "a dit", her present "je suis" shifts to the imperfect "était" in reported speech; "très" is already in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Il a expliqué pourquoi il ___ toujours en retard.
questions.explanation: After the past verb "a expliqué", the present "est" shifts to the imperfect "était" in reported speech; "toujours" is already in the sentence.

questions.prompt: Elle a promis qu'elle ___ (appeler) plus tard.
questions.explanation: After a past-tense verb of reporting ("a promis"), a future in the original speech becomes the conditional, and "elle" takes the -ait ending: "appellerait".

questions.prompt: Il a affirmé que le projet ___ (être) enfin terminé.
questions.explanation: "était enfin" is correct here. Reported speech with tense and pronoun shifts.
questions.example: Il a affirmé que le projet était enfin terminé.

questions.prompt: Elle a demandé si nous ___ (avoir) fini.
questions.explanation: After "a demandé si", the reported verb shifts to the imperfect, and the subject "nous" requires the ending -ions: "avions".

questions.prompt: Il a dit qu'il ___ (faire) beau la veille.
questions.explanation: "La veille" (the day before) places the weather before the moment of reporting, so the past-tense reporting verb takes the pluperfect: "avait fait".
questions.example: Il a dit qu'il avait fait ses devoirs la veille.

questions.explanation: "Bientôt" points to a future event seen from the past, so the conditional is needed; with "elle" it is "reviendrait".

questions.prompt: Il a expliqué que la réunion ___ (commencer) à midi.
questions.explanation: After "a expliqué que" in the past, the present "commence" becomes the imperfect, and "la réunion" (3rd person singular) gives "commençait".

questions.prompt: Elle a dit qu'elle ne ___ (comprendre) pas.
questions.explanation: After "a dit que", the present "je ne comprends pas" shifts to the imperfect, and "elle" takes the ending -ait: "comprenait".
The question "combien ça coûte ?" shifts to the imperfect after "a demandé", and the singular subject "cela" requires "coûtait", not the plural "coûtaient".
After "a affirmé que", the present "j'ai toujours raison" shifts to the imperfect, giving "avait toujours". The expression is "avoir raison", so a form of "être" cannot be used.
questions.example: Elle a affirmé qu'elle avait toujours raison.

questions.prompt: Il a dit qu'il ___ (essayer) de son mieux.
questions.explanation: After "a dit que" in the past, the present "j'essaie" shifts to the imperfect, and "il" takes the ending -ait: "essayait".
questions.example: Il a dit qu'il essayait de faire de son mieux.

units.title: Plus-que-parfait
units.description: The pluperfect — What had already happened before another past action.

questions.explanation: His leaving happened before "je suis arrivé", so the pluperfect is needed. "Partir" takes "être", and the masculine singular agreement gives "était déjà parti".
questions.example: Quand je suis arrivé, il était déjà parti.

questions.explanation: Finishing "avant midi" is completed before another past point, so the pluperfect is used. "Finir" takes "avoir", and "elle" gives "avait fini" with no agreement.
Eating "avant leur arrivée" happened before another past moment, so the pluperfect is used. "Manger" takes "avoir", and "nous" gives "avions mangé".
With "tu" the pluperfect needs "avais", and "voir" takes avoir, so it is "avais vu". The action happened before "moi", so a past-before-past tense is needed.

questions.prompt: Ils ___ (arriver) quand le film a commencé.
questions.explanation: "arriver" takes être, and the participle agrees with the plural subject "Ils", giving "étaient déjà arrivés". The arriving came before the film started, hence the pluperfect.
questions.example: Ils étaient déjà arrivés quand le film a commencé.

questions.explanation: "J'" is first person, so the auxiliary is "avais", and "oublier" takes avoir with an invariable participle: "avais oublié". "Mon parapluie" comes after the verb, so there is no agreement.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (perdre) ses clés avant de partir.
questions.explanation: "perdre" takes avoir, and with "Elle" the auxiliary is "avait", so it is "avait perdu". "Ses clés" follows the verb, so the participle stays unchanged.

questions.prompt: Quand Paul a proposé d'aller au musée Rodin, nous ___ (visiter) ce musée.
questions.explanation: With "nous" the pluperfect of "visiter" (avoir verb) is "avions déjà visité". The visit happened before Paul made his suggestion, so a past-before-past tense is needed.
questions.example: Nous avions déjà visité ce musée.

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (terminer) vos études avant de déménager.
questions.explanation: With "Vous" the auxiliary is "aviez", and "terminer" takes avoir with the past participle "terminé", not the infinitive: "aviez terminé". The studies were finished before moving.

questions.prompt: Il ___ (préparer) le dîner avant que nous arrivions.
questions.explanation: "Il" is singular, so the auxiliary is "avait", and "préparer" takes avoir: "avait préparé". The dinner was prepared before "nous arrivions".
"J'" needs "avais" and "lire" takes avoir, so it is "avais lu". "Ce livre" comes after the verb, so the participle does not agree.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (partir) avant que je puisse la remercier.
questions.explanation: "partir" takes être, so the participle agrees with feminine "Elle": "était partie". She left before the speaker could thank her.

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (ne jamais voir) une telle chose.
questions.explanation: The negation wraps the auxiliary: "ne" becomes "n'" before "avions" and "jamais" follows it, giving "n'avions jamais vu". "Nous" requires "avions".
questions.example: Nous n'avions jamais vu une telle chose.

questions.explanation: "Ils" needs "avaient", and "décider" takes avoir. "Déjà" goes between auxiliary and participle: "avaient déjà décidé".
questions.example: Ils avaient déjà décidé avant la réunion.

questions.prompt: Tu ___ (comprendre) la leçon avant le cours suivant.
questions.explanation: "Tu" takes "avais", and "comprendre" has the irregular participle "compris": "avais compris". The understanding came before the next class.

questions.prompt: Il ___ (écrire) la lettre avant de partir.
questions.explanation: The subject "Il" needs the imperfect of avoir plus the participle, giving "avait écrit". The participle stays "écrit" because "la lettre" comes after the verb, so there is no agreement.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (déjà manger) quand nous sommes arrivés.
questions.explanation: "Elle" takes "avait" (not "avais"), and manger uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "avait déjà mangé". The adverb "déjà" sits between the auxiliary and the participle.
questions.example: Elle avait déjà mangé quand nous sommes arrivés.

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (finir) nos devoirs avant le dîner.
questions.explanation: "Nous" needs "avions" (imperfect of avoir) plus the participle, giving "avions fini". The participle stays "fini" because "nos devoirs" follows the verb.
"J'" (je) takes "avais", and appeler uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "avais appelé". The participle of appeler is spelled "appelé" with one l.

questions.prompt: Ils ___ (vendre) la maison avant de déménager.
questions.explanation: "Ils" needs "avaient", and vendre uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "avaient vendu". The participle stays "vendu" because "la maison" comes after the verb.

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (faire) une erreur sans le savoir.
questions.explanation: "Vous" takes "aviez", and faire uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "aviez fait". The participle stays "fait" because "une erreur" follows the verb.
questions.meaning: you had made, you had done

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (retourner) chez elle avant la tempête.
questions.explanation: Retourner (to go back) is conjugated with être, and the participle agrees with the feminine subject "Elle", giving "était retournée".
questions.meaning: she had gone back, she had returned

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (choisir) ce restaurant avant de réserver.
questions.explanation: "Nous" takes "avions", and choisir uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "avions choisi". The participle stays "choisi" because "ce restaurant" follows the verb.
questions.example: Nous avions choisi ce restaurant avant de partir.

questions.prompt: Il ___ (dire) la vérité dès le début.
questions.explanation: "Il" takes "avait", and dire uses avoir with the irregular participle "dit", giving "avait dit".

questions.prompt: J'___ (finir) mon travail avant la pause.
questions.explanation: "J'" (je) takes "avais", and finir uses avoir, so the pluperfect is "avais fini". The participle stays "fini" because "mon travail" follows the verb.

units.title: Conditionnel passé
units.description: The past conditional — What would have happened.

questions.prompt: Si j'avais su, je ___ (venir) plus tôt.
questions.explanation: After "si" plus the pluperfect, the result clause takes the past conditional. Venir uses être, so "je" gives "serais venu".

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (partir) si elle avait eu le temps.
questions.explanation: The "si" clause is in the pluperfect, so the result takes the past conditional. Partir uses être and the participle agrees with feminine "Elle", giving "serait partie".

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (aider) si tu nous avais demandé.
questions.explanation: The si-clause is in the pluperfect ("si tu nous avais demandé"), so the main clause takes the past conditional, and "aurions aidé" matches "nous" with avoir as the auxiliary.
questions.example: Nous aurions aidé si tu nous l'avais demandé.

questions.explanation: "aurais réussi" is the "tu" form of avoir (aurais) plus the participle; réussir takes avoir, not être, and "aurait" would be the il/elle form.
Venir takes être, and the participle agrees with the plural subject "ils", giving "seraient venus"; "auraient venu" uses the wrong auxiliary.

questions.prompt: J'___ (aimer) le voir avant son départ.
questions.explanation: The elided "J'" is the first-person singular, so the past conditional of aimer is "aurais aimé"; "aurait" and "aurions" are other persons, and aimer takes avoir.
With "Elle" (third person singular), the past conditional of devoir is "aurait dû", expressing a reproach about the past: she should have warned us earlier.
The subject "Nous" needs the form aurions, and the participle of pouvoir is the invariable "pu" (never "pus"), so "aurions pu"; pouvoir takes avoir.

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (dire) la même chose à ma place.
questions.explanation: The subject "Vous" requires the ending -iez, and dire takes avoir, so the past conditional is "auriez dit".
"Il" takes the third person singular auxiliary, and choisir uses avoir, so the past conditional is "aurait choisi"; "serait choisi" would be a passive.
"J'" is first person singular, so the past conditional of vouloir is "aurais voulu", a polite way to express a past wish or regret.
Rester takes être, and the participle agrees with the feminine singular subject "Elle", giving "serait restée".
"Nous" takes aurions, and faire uses avoir with no agreement here since "un autre choix" follows the verb, so "aurions fait".
The subject "Tu" takes the auxiliary form aurais, and devoir uses avoir, so "aurais dû" expresses a past reproach: you should have listened.

questions.prompt: Ils ___ (arriver) à l'heure sans la panne.
questions.explanation: Arriver forms its past conditional with être, so the participle agrees with the masculine plural "Ils": "seraient arrivés". "auraient arrivé" uses the wrong auxiliary, and the other options lack the plural masculine agreement.
The subject "J'" (je) takes the conditional of avoir in the first person singular, "aurais", plus the participle: "aurais préféré". The forms in -ait, -ions and -iez belong to il, nous and vous.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (pouvoir) réussir avec un peu de chance.
questions.explanation: "Elle" is third person singular, so avoir takes the ending -ait: "aurait pu". Pouvoir uses avoir, not être, so "serait pu" is wrong.
The subject "Nous" requires the -ions ending of avoir in the conditional: "aurions aimé". The other options are the forms for je, il and vous.
The subject "Vous" requires the -iez ending of avoir in the conditional: "auriez accepté". Accepter takes avoir, so "seriez accepté" is wrong.

Partir takes être in compound tenses, and "Il" is masculine singular, so no extra agreement is needed: "serait parti". "aurait parti" uses the wrong auxiliary, while "serait partie" and "seraient partis" do not agree with "Il".

"J'" calls for the first person "aurais", and faire takes avoir with no agreement here, since "la même erreur" follows the verb: "aurais fait". "aurais faite" wrongly agrees with an object that comes after.
"Elle" is third person singular, so avoir takes -ait in the past conditional: "aurait voulu". The other options are the forms for je, ils and nous.
"Nous" takes "aurions", and devoir uses avoir, so the past conditional is "aurions dû" (we should have). "serions dû" wrongly uses être.
questions.meaning: we should have, we ought to have

questions.explanation: "Ils" is third person plural, so avoir takes -aient: "auraient pu". "aurait" is singular and "seraient pu" uses the wrong auxiliary.
questions.meaning: they could have, they might have

questions.explanation: Être itself takes avoir in compound tenses, and "Tu" needs the -ais ending: "aurais été". "serais été" is impossible because être never uses être as its auxiliary.

units.title: Gerund & Present Participle
units.description: En + -ant for simultaneous actions — Use the gerund (en + present participle) to show two things happening at once.

questions.explanation: Two actions happening at once are expressed with en + present participle (the gerund): "en regardant". After "en" the verb cannot be an infinitive, a past participle or a conjugated form.
"en faisant" is the gerund of faire: "en" plus the present participle (nous faisons gives faisant) shows she sings while doing the dishes. The spelling is faisant, not "fesant".

questions.prompt: J'ai appris le français ___ (voyager) en France.
questions.explanation: The gerund "en voyageant" says how I learned French: by travelling. Verbs in -ger keep the e before -ant (voyageant) to keep the soft g sound.
Talking and walking happen at the same time, so French uses the gerund "en marchant" (en + stem of nous marchons + -ant). The infinitive or past participle cannot follow "en" here.
The gerund "en lisant" expresses the means: you learn a lot by reading. It is built on the nous form (lisons), giving lisant, not on the infinitive lire.

questions.prompt: Il s'est blessé ___ (courir) dans la rue.
questions.explanation: He hurt himself while running, so the gerund "en courant" is needed. The present participle of courir is courant with a single r, from the nous form courons.

questions.prompt: Elle a trouvé du travail ___ (chercher) sur internet.
questions.explanation: The gerund "en cherchant" gives the means by which she found work: by searching online. It is formed with en + the present participle (cherch- + -ant).

questions.prompt: Nous économisons de l'argent ___ (cuisiner) à la maison.
questions.explanation: The gerund "en cuisinant" states how they save money: by cooking at home. Only en + present participle (cuisin- + -ant) expresses this manner or means.
Listening to music and working happen at the same time, so you need the gerund "en travaillant". It is en + the present participle (nous travaillons gives travaillant).
The gerund "en persévérant" tells how he succeeded: by persevering. Verbs in -er form it by replacing -ons of the nous form with -ant.
She fell asleep during the film, so the gerund "en regardant" shows two simultaneous actions. It is en + regardant, the present participle of regarder.
They talked while waiting for the bus, so the gerund "en attendant" is used. For -re verbs the participle comes from the nous form (attendons gives attendant).
The gerund "en voyageant" says you learn a lot by travelling. Verbs in -ger keep the e before -ant (voyageant) to keep the soft g sound.

questions.prompt: Il a perdu du poids ___ (faire) plus de sport.
questions.explanation: After "en", French needs the present participle (faire becomes "faisant"), which shows how he lost weight: by doing more sport. The infinitive, the 'fait' form and the misspelling 'fesant' are not valid after "en". Answer: "en faisant".

questions.prompt: Elle a amélioré son français ___ (pratiquer) tous les jours.
questions.explanation: To say how she improved, use "en" plus the present participle: pratiquer becomes "pratiquant" (stem of 'nous pratiquons' + -ant). The infinitive, past participle and present-tense forms cannot follow "en". Answer: "en pratiquant".

questions.prompt: Nous avons économisé du temps ___ (planifier) à l'avance.
questions.explanation: The gerund "en planifiant" (planifier becomes planifi- + -ant) expresses the means by which time was saved: by planning ahead. Infinitive, past participle and present-tense forms are not used after "en".
questions.example: Nous avons gagné du temps en planifiant à l'avance.

questions.prompt: J'ai rencontré mon ami ___ (étudier) à l'université.
questions.explanation: "en étudiant" is the gerund of étudier and shows the two actions happened together: he met his friend while studying at university. Only the present participle can follow "en".

questions.prompt: Il s'est amusé ___ (jouer) avec ses amis.
questions.explanation: "en jouant" is the gerund of jouer (nous jouons becomes jou- + -ant) and says he had fun while playing with his friends. After "en" you cannot use the infinitive, past participle or present tense.
"en posant" is the gerund of poser and states the means: she understood by asking questions. The other forms (posé, poser, pose) are not present participles, so they cannot follow "en".

With a reflexive verb the pronoun stays in the gerund and agrees with the subject: the subject is "nous", so "en nous entraînant". 'en s'entraînant' and 'en vous entraînant' have the wrong pronoun, and 'en entraînant' drops it.
The future 'réussiras' is followed by the means of succeeding: "en essayant" (gerund of essayer), meaning by trying again. The infinitive, past participle and imperfect cannot follow "en".

questions.prompt: Il a tout perdu ___ (jouer) au casino.
questions.explanation: "en jouant" is the gerund of jouer and shows how he lost everything: by gambling at the casino. Only a present participle can follow "en"; 'jouer', 'joué' and 'jouait' are not valid there.

questions.prompt: Elle s'est fait des amis ___ (participer) au club.
questions.explanation: "en participant" is the gerund of participer and gives the means: she made friends by taking part in the club. The infinitive, past participle and imperfect are not gerunds and cannot follow "en".
"en achetant" is the gerund of acheter and tells how we saved money: by buying in bulk. After "en" you need the -ant form, not the infinitive, past participle or imperfect.

questions.prompt: J'ai découvert cette recette ___ (chercher) sur internet.
questions.explanation: "en cherchant" is the gerund of chercher and shows how I found the recipe: while searching online. Only the present participle can follow "en"; 'chercher', 'cherché' and 'cherchait' do not fit.

units.title: Concession & Contrast Connectors
units.description: Signalling contrast — Connectors for concession and contrast.

questions.prompt: Il est gentil, ___ un peu têtu.
questions.explanation: "mais" (but) joins two contrasting qualities: kind, but a bit stubborn. "Malgré" needs a noun and "quand même" cannot link the two ideas here.
"cependant" means "however": it introduces a statement that contrasts with the previous one, for example "Il pleut ; cependant, nous sortons."
"néanmoins" means "nevertheless": it admits a point and then states something that still holds, for example "C'est cher ; néanmoins, je l'achète."
"bien que" means "although" and is followed by the subjunctive, for example "bien qu'il pleuve".

questions.prompt: The French connector for "even though" is ___.
questions.explanation: "même si" means "even though / even if" and, unlike "bien que", is followed by the indicative, for example "même s'il pleut".
"malgré" means "despite" and is followed by a noun, not a clause, for example "malgré la pluie".

questions.prompt: The French connector for "on the other hand" is ___.
questions.explanation: "en revanche" means "on the other hand" and starts a new sentence that presents a contrasting point, for example "Il est timide ; en revanche, sa sœur parle à tout le monde."
"alors que" means "whereas" and links two contrasting clauses, for example "Il aime la mer, alors que je préfère la montagne."
"pourtant" means "yet" and introduces a surprising contrast, for example "Il est riche, et pourtant il se plaint."

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "in spite of"?
questions.explanation: "malgré" means "in spite of" and is followed by a noun, for example "malgré le froid".

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "on the contrary"?
questions.explanation: "au contraire" means "on the contrary": it rejects the previous statement outright, whereas "en revanche" only adds a contrasting point.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "while" (contrasting two facts)? ___
questions.explanation: "tandis que" means "while/whereas" and links two contrasting clauses in the indicative: Il travaille tandis qu'elle se repose.
"quand même" means "still, anyway" despite what was just said: Il pleuvait, mais on est sortis quand même.
"tout de même" means "even so, all the same": it keeps a statement true despite an obstacle, as in C'est cher, mais je l'achète tout de même.

questions.prompt: Which French expression means "regardless" (= no matter what)?
questions.explanation: "peu importe" means "regardless, no matter" (peu importe le prix), while "quand même" means "still, anyway".
"inversement" means "conversely": it presents the reverse of the previous statement, while "en revanche" means "on the other hand".
"par contraste" means "by contrast" and sets two things side by side; "au contraire" means "on the contrary" and contradicts what was just said.
"nonobstant" is a formal, legal-style word for "notwithstanding, despite", used before a noun: nonobstant les difficultés.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "all the same"?
questions.explanation: "tout de même" means "all the same, nevertheless": the fact stays true despite what came before.

questions.prompt: Which French expression means "in contrast to" (followed by a noun)? ___
questions.explanation: "contrairement à" means "in contrast to, unlike" and is followed by a noun (contrairement à son frère), while "tandis que" introduces a whole clause.
"quoique" means "though, although" and takes the subjunctive (quoiqu'il soit tard), while "même si" means "even if" and takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "despite the fact that"?
questions.explanation: "bien que" means "although, despite the fact that" and is followed by the subjunctive: bien qu'il soit malade.

questions.prompt: Which French expression means "however that may be"? ___
questions.explanation: "quoi qu'il en soit" means "however that may be, in any case" and closes a point to move on, while "pourtant" means "yet".

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "be that as it may"?
questions.explanation: "quoi qu'il en soit" means "be that as it may" or "in any case": it sets aside what was just said and moves on. "Pourtant" and "cependant" mean "yet/however", and "inversement" means "conversely".
"à la différence de" means "unlike" and is followed by a noun to contrast two things. "Pourtant" and "cependant" mean "however", and "inversement" means "conversely".

units.title: Cause & Consequence Connectors
units.description: Explaining why and what follows — Connectors for cause and consequence.

questions.prompt: The French connector meaning "because", followed by a full clause, is… ___
questions.explanation: "parce que" means "because" and is followed by a clause with a verb, while "en raison de" means "because of" and takes a noun.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "since" (giving a cause)?
questions.explanation: "puisque" means "since" in the sense of "given that", and it introduces a cause the listener already accepts. "Ainsi" and "par conséquent" introduce a result, not a cause.

questions.prompt: The French connector meaning "as", giving a cause at the start of a sentence, is… ___
questions.explanation: "comme" at the start of a sentence means "as" or "since" and gives the cause, as in "Comme il pleuvait, je suis resté."

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "so" (introducing a consequence)?
questions.explanation: "donc" means "so" and introduces the consequence of what was just said. "Puisque" gives a cause, and "afin de" gives a purpose.
"ainsi" means "thus" and introduces a conclusion or result. "Puisque" gives a cause, "afin de" a purpose, and "grâce à" means "thanks to".
"par conséquent" means "therefore" and introduces a result. "Parce que", "en raison de" and "puisque" all introduce a cause instead.

questions.prompt: The French connector for "so that" is ___.
questions.explanation: "de sorte que" means "so that" and introduces the result or aim of an action; it takes the subjunctive when it expresses an aim. "De ce fait" and "en conséquence" mean "as a result", and "en raison de" means "due to".
"à cause de" means "because of" and is followed by a noun, often a negative cause. "Par conséquent", "c'est pourquoi" and "raison pour laquelle" introduce a result instead.

questions.prompt: The French connector for "due to" is ___.
questions.explanation: "en raison de" means "due to" and is a formal way to give a cause before a noun. The other options, such as "par conséquent" and "c'est pourquoi", introduce a result.
"grâce à" means "thanks to" and introduces a positive cause before a noun. "Ainsi" and "d'où" introduce a result, and "afin de" gives a purpose.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "as a result"?
questions.explanation: "de ce fait" means "as a result": it introduces a consequence of the fact just stated, e.g. "Il a plu, de ce fait le match est annulé."

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "consequently" is ___.
questions.explanation: "par conséquent" means "consequently" and introduces the logical result of what came before, e.g. "Il est malade, par conséquent il reste chez lui."
"d'où" means "hence" and is usually followed by a noun naming the result, e.g. "Il pleuvait, d'où son retard."

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "that's why" is ___.
questions.explanation: "c'est pourquoi" literally means "that is why" and introduces a consequence clause, e.g. "Il était malade, c'est pourquoi il est resté chez lui."
"étant donné que" means "given that": it introduces a cause presented as an accepted fact and is followed by a full clause.

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "for this reason" is ___.
questions.explanation: "pour cette raison" is the word-for-word equivalent of "for this reason" and refers back to a cause just mentioned.

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "as a consequence"?
questions.explanation: "en conséquence" means "as a consequence" and introduces an action or result that follows from what was just said.

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "owing to" is ___.
questions.explanation: "en raison de" means "owing to" and is followed by a noun, e.g. "en raison de la pluie".

questions.prompt: Which French connector means "so much so that"?
questions.explanation: "si bien que" means "so much so that": it introduces a result that follows from the situation just described, e.g. "Il a plu toute la nuit, si bien que la route est inondée."

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "in order to" is ___.
questions.explanation: "afin de" means "in order to" and expresses purpose; it is followed by an infinitive, e.g. "afin de réussir".

questions.prompt: The French connector that means "in order that" is ___.
questions.explanation: "afin que" means "in order that" and expresses purpose; it is followed by the subjunctive, e.g. "afin qu'il comprenne".
"menant à" means "leading to": it is the present participle of "mener" followed by "à" and a noun naming the result.

questions.prompt: The French connector for "resulting in" is… ___
questions.explanation: "entraînant" is the present participle of "entraîner" (to lead to), so it introduces a result directly, like 'resulting in'; "donc" and "de ce fait" mean 'so/therefore' and "en raison de" gives a cause.

questions.prompt: The French connector for "which is why" is…
questions.explanation: "raison pour laquelle" literally means 'reason for which', so it adds the consequence of what was just said, like 'which is why'; "étant donné que" gives a cause and "ainsi" means 'thus'.
"en conséquence" means 'as a result, accordingly' and starts a new clause stating the consequence; "de sorte que" means 'so that' and "étant donné que" gives a cause.

units.title: Politics & Society
units.description: Talking about current affairs — Politics and society vocabulary.

questions.explanation: government → le gouvernement. Politics and society vocabulary.
president → le président. Politics and society vocabulary.
"l'élection" is feminine (une élection), and the article elides to l' before the vowel é.
"le vote" is a direct cognate of 'vote' and is masculine, so it takes "le"; the other words mean president, immigration and politics.
"le citoyen" is masculine; a female citizen is la citoyenne. Note the spelling -oyen.
"la loi" is feminine and means a law passed by parliament, as in voter une loi.
"la démocratie" is feminine, like most nouns ending in -ie. The t is pronounced like an s, and the first e takes an accent (é).
"le parlement" is masculine and is spelled -lement, with no i as in English 'parliament'.
"le ministre" means a government minister; for a woman, la ministre is the standard form today.
"la politique" means both 'policy' (a government's plan of action) and 'politics', so context tells them apart; the other words mean president, protest and justice.
"la constitution" is the text setting out a state's fundamental laws; it is a feminine cognate of the English word, and in France it is often capitalised: la Constitution.
"les droits" is the plural of le droit (a right), as in les droits de l'homme (human rights).
"la justice" means both fairness and the legal system, exactly like English 'justice', and it is feminine.
"l'égalité" is feminine, like most nouns ending in -té. It appears in the French motto Liberté, égalité, fraternité.
"la liberté" is feminine, like most nouns ending in -té. It translates both 'freedom' and 'liberty'.
"la société" is feminine, like most nouns ending in -té. It can also mean a company.
"l'immigration" is spelled as in English; it is feminine, and "la" elides to "l'" before the vowel.
"la pauvreté" comes from pauvre (poor) and is feminine, like most nouns ending in -té.
"l'inégalité" is égalité with the prefix in-. It is feminine (une inégalité), and the article elides before the vowel.
"la manifestation" is the everyday word for a street protest or demonstration (informally "une manif"); the other options mean law, diplomacy and justice.
"la réforme" is the cognate of "reform" and is feminine; note the accent on the é. Example: la réforme des retraites (pension reform).
"l'impôt" is masculine (un impôt) and is often used in the plural: payer ses impôts (to pay your taxes). Watch the circumflex on the ô.

questions.prompt: The French word for "public opinion" is…
questions.explanation: "l'opinion publique" is feminine, so the adjective takes the feminine form publique. In French it follows the noun.
diplomacy → la diplomatie. Politics and society vocabulary.
"la souveraineté" is feminine, like most nouns ending in -té. Example: la souveraineté nationale (national sovereignty).

units.title: Environment & Climate Change
units.description: Talking about the planet — Climate and environmental vocabulary.

questions.prompt: The French word for "climate change" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le changement climatique" is masculine, and the adjective climatique comes after the noun, unlike in English. It is also called le réchauffement climatique when the focus is warming.

questions.prompt: The French word for "global warming" is…
questions.explanation: "le réchauffement climatique" is the standard term for global warming: "réchauffement" (warming) comes from "chaud" (hot) and "climatique" means 'of the climate'.

questions.prompt: The French word for "greenhouse gas" is… ___
bank: le gaz à effet de serre
questions.answer: le gaz à effet de serre
questions.explanation: "le gaz à effet de serre" literally means 'gas with a greenhouse effect' ("serre" = greenhouse), such as CO2 or methane.

questions.prompt: The French word for "carbon footprint" is…
questions.explanation: "l'empreinte carbone" uses "empreinte" (footprint, mark) followed by "carbone" with no preposition; the word is feminine, and the article elides to "l'" before the vowel.

bank: le gaz à effet de serre
questions.explanation: "la déforestation" is the loss of forests, built on "forêt"; like most nouns ending in -tion, it is feminine.
"la biodiversité" means the variety of living species; nouns ending in -ité are feminine, so it takes "la".
"l'écosystème" is a community of living things and their environment; it is masculine (un écosystème), even though "l'" hides the gender.

questions.prompt: The French word for "renewable energy" is…
questions.explanation: "l'énergie renouvelable" is energy from sources that renew themselves, like sun or wind; "énergie" is feminine, so the adjective "renouvelable" stays the same in the feminine.

questions.prompt: The French word for "solar panel" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le panneau solaire" is built from "panneau" (a panel, masculine) and "solaire" (of the sun), so it is the panel that turns sunlight into electricity.

questions.prompt: The French word for "wind turbine" is…
questions.explanation: "l'éolienne" is a wind turbine; the word comes from Éole, the Greek god of the winds, and it is feminine (une éolienne).
sustainability → la durabilité. Climate and environmental vocabulary.
"les émissions" means emissions, for example of CO2, and is normally plural in this sense, just like the English word.
"la sécheresse" is a drought, a long period without rain; it comes from "sec" (dry) and is feminine.
"l'inondation" is a flood; it comes from the verb "inonder" (to flood) and is feminine, like most nouns ending in -tion.
"l'extinction" is the total disappearance of a species; it is spelled like the English word but is feminine (une extinction).
"la conservation" is the protection of nature and wildlife, as in "la conservation de la nature"; it is feminine, like most nouns ending in -tion.
"le recyclage" is the masculine noun for collecting and reprocessing waste so it can be reused, as in "le recyclage du verre".

questions.prompt: The French word for "plastic waste" is… ___
questions.explanation: "les déchets plastiques" means plastic waste: "les déchets" (always plural here) is rubbish or waste, and "plastiques" says what kind.

questions.prompt: The French word for "endangered species" is…
questions.explanation: "l'espèce en voie de disparition" literally means 'the species on the way to disappearing'. Espèce is feminine; a close synonym is une espèce menacée.

questions.prompt: The French word for "natural resource" is… ___
bank: le gaz à effet de serre
questions.explanation: "la ressource naturelle" is feminine, so naturelle takes the feminine -le ending and follows the noun. It is often plural: les ressources naturelles.
pollution (climate) → la pollution. Climate and environmental vocabulary.
"l'écologie" (feminine, elided before a vowel) is the study of living things and their environment, and also the green political movement.

questions.prompt: The French word for "ozone layer" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la couche d'ozone" literally means "the layer of ozone": "la couche" is a layer, and "de" elides to "d'" before "ozone".

questions.prompt: The French word for "sea level" is…
questions.explanation: "le niveau de la mer" is literally 'the level of the sea'; French uses de rather than putting the nouns together as English does. Example: le niveau de la mer monte (sea level is rising).

questions.prompt: The French word for "carbon neutral" is… ___
questions.explanation: "neutre en carbone" is an adjective phrase meaning carbon neutral; it follows the noun, as in "une entreprise neutre en carbone".

units.title: Law & Justice
units.description: Talking about the legal system — Law and justice vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "la loi" is a feminine noun for a rule passed by parliament, as in "voter une loi"; "les droits" means rights, not law.
"le tribunal" is the court where trials take place; "l'avocat" is a person who works there, not the court itself.
"le juge" is the person who presides over a court. For a woman you can say la juge; don't confuse it with juger, the verb 'to judge'.

questions.prompt: The French word for "lawyer (in court)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'avocat" is the lawyer who defends or represents someone in court; the same word also means avocado, so rely on context.
"le procès" means a court trial, not a 'process', which in French is un processus. Example: le procès a duré trois semaines.
"le crime" is a masculine noun for a serious offence; "le témoin" is a witness and "la victime" the person harmed.
"le témoin" is a person who saw an event and testifies about it. It is traditionally masculine even for a woman, though la témoin is now also accepted.
"le jury" is spelled as in English but is masculine and pronounced the French way (zhu-ree). Example: le jury a rendu son verdict.
evidence → la preuve. Law and justice vocabulary.
"la peine" is the punishment a judge gives, as in "une peine de prison"; "le verdict" is only the decision of guilty or not guilty.
"la prison" is the place where convicted people are locked up; "la peine" is the sentence itself, not the place.
verdict → le verdict. Law and justice vocabulary.

questions.prompt: The French word for "trial (in court)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le procès" is a case heard before a court, so it translates "trial" (or lawsuit); it is masculine and written with a grave accent: è.
"le contrat" is a legally binding agreement between parties; unlike English contract, the French word has no c before the final t: contrat.
"les droits" (plural) are the legal entitlements a person has, as in les droits de l'homme; the singular le droit usually means "law" as a field.

questions.prompt: The French word for "the judicial system" is…
questions.explanation: "la justice" means the judicial system as a whole, as in saisir la justice (to take legal action); la loi and la législation are the laws themselves.
"coupable" means guilty, i.e. found responsible for a crime; its opposite is innocent.

questions.prompt: The French word for "not guilty" is…
questions.explanation: "innocent" describes someone who did not commit the crime, the opposite of coupable.
"l'appel" is the request for a higher court to review a judgment, as in faire appel; it elides because appel starts with a vowel.
"l'amende" is a sum of money you must pay as a penalty, as in une amende de 135 euros; it is feminine and elided because it starts with a vowel.

questions.prompt: The French word for "the force that keeps order and makes arrests" is…
questions.explanation: "la police" is the force that keeps public order and arrests suspects; in French it is feminine and singular.
"l'arrestation" is the act of the police taking someone into custody; the related verb is arrêter.

questions.prompt: The French word for "a person the police think committed a crime" is…
questions.explanation: "le suspect" is the person the police believe may have committed the crime, unlike le témoin, who only saw it.
"la victime" is the person harmed by a crime; the word is always feminine, even when it refers to a man.
"la législation" is the body of laws passed by a parliament. Like most nouns ending in -tion, it is feminine, so it takes "la".

units.title: Economy & Finance
units.description: Talking about money and markets — Economics and finance vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "l'économie" is the French word for a country's economy. It is feminine, and "la" becomes l' before the vowel.
"l'inflation" is the general rise in prices. It is feminine (a -tion noun), and "la" shortens to l' before the vowel.
"le marché" is the economic market where goods and money are traded. It is masculine, so it takes "le".
"l'investissement" is money put into something to earn a return. It is masculine (nouns in -ment usually are), with l' before the vowel.

questions.prompt: The French word for "stock (a share in a company)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'action" is one share in a company; the stock market is la Bourse. Don't confuse it with le stock, which means goods kept in reserve.
"le budget" is spelled the same as in English but is pronounced the French way, without the final t. It is masculine, so it takes "le".
"la dette" is money you owe to someone. It is feminine, so it takes "la".
"le revenu" is the money a person or household earns. It is masculine and is often used in the plural, les revenus.

questions.prompt: The French word for "tax (paid to the state)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'impôt" is a tax paid to the state; income tax is l'impôt sur le revenu. It is masculine, with l' before the vowel.
"la croissance" is the growth of an economy, from the verb croître (to grow). It is feminine, so it takes "la".
"la récession" is a period when the economy shrinks. It is feminine and has an accent on the first e (é), unlike English.
"le chômage" means unemployment, the state of having no job. "La croissance" is growth and "le marché" is the market.
"la devise" is a country's currency, as in an exchange rate (it can also mean a motto). "La dette" is debt and "les actions" are shares.
"le commerce" means trade, the buying and selling of goods. "Le revenu" is income and "le salaire" is wages.
"la banque" is the bank, the institution that keeps your money and lends it. "L'action" is a share and "le consommateur" is a consumer.
"le prêt" is a loan, money lent that must be paid back. "L'épargne" means savings and "le taux d'intérêt" is the interest rate.

questions.prompt: The French word for "interest rate" is…
questions.explanation: "le taux d'intérêt" is the interest rate, the percentage charged on a loan or paid on savings. "La croissance" means growth.
"le profit" is the money a business keeps after its costs (a synonym is "le bénéfice"). "L'investissement" is investment.
"le salaire" is the pay an employee gets for their work. "Le revenu" is broader: income from any source.
"le consommateur" is the consumer, the person who buys and uses goods and services. "L'inflation" is rising prices.

questions.prompt: The French word for "supply and demand" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'offre et la demande" is supply and demand: "l'offre" is what is offered for sale and "la demande" is what buyers want. "Les recettes et les dépenses" means income and spending.
"les actions" are shares in a company that you buy on the stock market; in finance the word does not mean deeds. "Le revenu" is income.
"le PIB" stands for produit intérieur brut, the French term for GDP. "Le SMIC" is the minimum wage.
"l'épargne" is money you put aside, your savings. "le budget" is a spending plan, "le PIB" is GDP and "la devise" is a currency.

questions.prompt: The French word for "stock market" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la bourse" is the stock market, where shares are bought and sold. "les actions" are the shares themselves, not the market.

units.title: Arts & Culture
units.description: Talking about the arts — Arts and culture vocabulary.

questions.explanation: "l'art" is art in general. "l'artiste" is the person who makes it, so it is not the word for "art".
"la peinture" means painting, both the art form and a painted picture. "l'art" is the broader word for art in general.
"la sculpture" is spelled exactly as in English but is feminine in French. Note the article "la".
"le musée" means museum. It ends in -ée but is masculine, so it takes "le".
"l'exposition" is an exhibition, a public display of works in a museum or gallery. In French it rarely means "exposition" in the English sense of explaining something.

questions.prompt: The French word for "artist (performing arts)" is… ___
questions.explanation: artist (performing arts) → l'artiste. Arts and culture vocabulary.
masterpiece → le chef-d'œuvre. Arts and culture vocabulary.
literature → la littérature. Arts and culture vocabulary.
"la poésie" is poetry, literature written in verse. "la pièce" is a play, a different genre.
"le roman" is a novel, a long work of prose fiction. Despite its look, it does not mean "romance".

questions.prompt: The French word for "theater (performing arts)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le théâtre" is the art of live stage performance, and also the building where plays are staged. Note the spelling with -tre and the accent.
"la pièce" (short for "la pièce de théâtre") is a play. In other contexts the same word can mean a room or a coin.
"le cinéma" is film as an art form, often called "le septième art". It is also the word for a movie theater.

questions.prompt: The French word for "film director" is…
questions.explanation: A film director is "le réalisateur" (from réaliser un film, to make a film); "le metteur en scène" is used more for theatre. "La pièce" is a play, and "l'exposition" is an exhibition.

questions.prompt: The French word for "music (as an art form)" is… ___
questions.explanation: The art of sound is "la musique", which is feminine like most nouns ending in -ique. "La danse" is dance, "l'artiste" is the artist, and "la représentation" is a performance.

A person who writes music is "le compositeur" (feminine: la compositrice), from composer, to compose. "Le romancier" writes novels, "le sculpteur" makes sculptures and "l'architecte" designs buildings.
Dance is "la danse", spelled with -se in French, not -ce as in English. The other options are other arts: la peinture (painting), la musique (music), la sculpture (sculpture).
Architecture is "l'architecture": the same word as in English, but feminine (une architecture), with the article elided to l' before the vowel.
Cultural heritage passed down through generations is "le patrimoine", as in le patrimoine mondial de l'UNESCO. The other options are a place (le musée, le théâtre) or an art form (l'architecture).
Tradition is "la tradition": the same word as in English, and feminine like all nouns ending in -tion.
Festival is "le festival", the same word as in English and masculine, as in le festival d'Avignon. Its plural is regular: les festivals.
An art gallery is "la galerie", spelled with one l and ending in -ie, unlike the English gallery. It is a place where artworks are shown and sold.
The person who reviews works is "le critique". With a feminine article, la critique usually means the review itself (or the profession of criticism).
A staged performance of a play or show is "la représentation", as in la représentation de ce soir. In French, la performance means an achievement or a piece of performance art.
Creativity is "la créativité": feminine like all nouns ending in -ité, with an acute accent on both e's.

units.title: Advanced Idioms II
units.description: Meaning match — More common French idioms.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le cœur sur la main" means… ___
bank: to badmouth someone behind their back
to make an effort, pitch in
questions.explanation: "Avoir le cœur sur la main" means "to be very generous": the person holds their heart out in their hand, ready to give to anyone.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre la clé sous la porte" means…
questions.explanation: "Mettre la clé sous la porte" means "to shut down (a business)": the owner leaves the key under the door and walks away for good.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir une araignée au plafond" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Avoir une araignée au plafond" means "to be a bit crazy": the ceiling stands for the head, and a spider living up there suggests odd ideas, like 'a screw loose'.

questions.prompt: The idiom "chercher midi à quatorze heures" means…
choices: to take a long weekend around a holiday
questions.explanation: "Chercher midi à quatorze heures" means "to overcomplicate things": looking for noon at two o'clock is searching for a difficulty where there is none.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un cœur d'artichaut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Avoir un cœur d'artichaut" means "to fall in love easily": like an artichoke giving away leaf after leaf, the heart is shared with one person after another.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le nez creux" means…
choices: to badmouth someone behind their back
questions.explanation: "Avoir le nez creux" means "to have good instincts": the person has a keen nose that sniffs out good opportunities before others do.
"Tomber des nues" means "to be utterly astonished": "nues" is an old word for clouds, so you are as shocked as if you had fallen from the sky.
"Avoir la frite" means "to feel great (informal)": it is casual slang for being full of energy, much like "avoir la pêche".

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre les pieds dans le plat" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Mettre les pieds dans le plat" means "to say something tactless": like stepping clumsily into the serving dish, you blunder straight into a delicate subject.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la main verte" means…
questions.explanation: "Avoir la main verte" means "to have a green thumb": a 'green hand' is good at gardening and makes plants grow well.

questions.prompt: The idiom "casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un" means…
choices: to badmouth someone behind their back
questions.explanation: "Casser du sucre sur le dos de quelqu'un" means "to badmouth someone behind their back": you criticise the person while they are not there to hear it.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre quelqu'un au pied du mur" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Mettre quelqu'un au pied du mur" means "to corner someone into deciding": with their back to the wall and no way out, they are forced to choose.
"Avoir le trac" means "to have stage fright": the nervousness you feel before performing or speaking in public, e.g. « J'ai toujours le trac avant un concert. »
"Faire la tête" means "to sulk": to stay in a bad mood with someone and refuse to talk, e.g. « Il fait la tête depuis notre dispute. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir des fourmis dans les jambes" means…
questions.explanation: "Avoir des fourmis dans les jambes" (literally 'ants in the legs') means "to have restless legs": you feel tingling and need to move, e.g. « Après deux heures de train, j'ai des fourmis dans les jambes. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre les bouchées doubles" means… ___
bank: to make an effort, pitch in
questions.explanation: "Mettre les bouchées doubles" (literally 'take double mouthfuls') means "to work twice as hard" to catch up or finish in time, e.g. « Il faut mettre les bouchées doubles pour finir à temps. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le cœur gros" means…
choices: to take a long weekend around a holiday
questions.explanation: "Avoir le cœur gros" (literally 'to have a big, swollen heart') means "to feel heavy-hearted", sad, often when leaving someone or somewhere, e.g. « J'ai le cœur gros de quitter Paris. »
"Tomber à l'eau" (literally 'to fall into the water') means "to fall through (a plan)": a project is cancelled, e.g. « Notre pique-nique est tombé à l'eau à cause de la pluie. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la tête sur les épaules" means…
choices: to badmouth someone behind their back
questions.explanation: "Avoir la tête sur les épaules" (literally 'to have your head on your shoulders') means "to be level-headed", sensible and calm, e.g. « Elle est jeune, mais elle a la tête sur les épaules. »

bank: to take a long weekend around a holiday
questions.answer: to take a long weekend around a holiday
questions.explanation: "Faire le pont" (literally 'to make the bridge') means "to take a long weekend around a holiday" by taking off the day between a public holiday and the weekend, e.g. « Le jeudi est férié, donc on fait le pont. »

bank: to make an effort, pitch in
to badmouth someone behind their back
questions.answer: to make an effort, pitch in
questions.explanation: "Mettre du sien" (literally 'to put in some of one's own') means "to make an effort, pitch in" so that things work, e.g. « Pour que ça marche, chacun doit mettre du sien. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la puce à l'oreille" means…
questions.explanation: "Avoir la puce à l'oreille" (literally 'to have a flea in your ear') means "to become suspicious" that something is wrong, e.g. « Son silence m'a mis la puce à l'oreille. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "être haut comme trois pommes" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Être haut comme trois pommes" (literally 'as tall as three apples') means "to be very small (a child)", e.g. « Je te connais depuis que tu es haut comme trois pommes. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un verre dans le nez" means…
choices: to take a long weekend around a holiday
questions.explanation: "Avoir un verre dans le nez" (literally 'to have a glass in your nose') is a colloquial way to say "to be a bit tipsy", e.g. « Après la fête, il avait un verre dans le nez. »

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre la puce à l'oreille de quelqu'un" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Mettre la puce à l'oreille de quelqu'un" literally means "to put a flea in someone's ear": a small detail starts to bother you. So it means "to make someone suspicious".

units.title: Emphatic Structures
units.description: C'est...qui/que — Emphasizing part of a sentence with c'est...qui/que.

questions.explanation: "C'est" is used because the stressed word is a singular name, Marie, and "qui" follows because Marie is the subject of "a téléphoné". "Ce sont" would need a plural.
questions.meaning: it is (stresses the word that follows)

questions.explanation: "que" is used because "ce livre" is the direct object of "je cherche". "Qui" would replace a subject, and "dont" would need "de".

questions.prompt: Ce sont mes amis ___ sont arrivés.
questions.explanation: "qui" is used because "mes amis" is the subject of "sont arrivés", and the verb comes straight after the blank. "Que" would need a subject before the verb.
"C'est" is used because the stressed phrase "à toi" is not a plural noun, so the singular form is needed, and "que" follows it. "Ce sont" is only for plural nouns or third-person plural pronouns.
"que" is used because the stressed word is a time expression ("demain"), and c'est...que is the pattern for adverbials. "Qui" is only for subjects, and "dont" would need "de".
"qui" is used because "eux" is the subject of "ont gagné", and the verb follows the blank directly. "Que" would need a subject after it.
"que" is used because the stressed phrase "à Paris" is a place complement, not a subject, so c'est...que is needed. "Qui" is only for subjects, and "dont" would need "de".
questions.meaning: that (follows a stressed place or time)

questions.explanation: "C'est" is used because the stressed word is the singular pronoun "lui", and "qui" follows because it is the subject of "a raison". "Ce sont" would need a plural.
questions.meaning: it is (stresses the word that follows)

questions.explanation: "que" is used because "ce film" is the direct object of "j'ai préféré", and "que" replaces an object. "Qui" would replace a subject, and "dont" would need "de".
"qui" is used because "ces documents" is the subject of "manquent", and the verb follows the blank directly. "Que" would need a separate subject.

questions.prompt: ___ elle qui a organisé la fête.
questions.explanation: "C'est" is used because the stressed word is the singular pronoun "elle", and "qui" follows because it is the subject of "a organisé". "Ce sont" is only for plural pronouns like "elles".
questions.meaning: it is (stresses the word that follows)

questions.prompt: C'est cette maison ___ nous voulons acheter.
questions.explanation: "que" is used because "cette maison" is the direct object of "nous voulons acheter", and a subject ("nous") already follows the blank. "Qui" would replace a subject, and "dont" would need "de".

questions.prompt: Ce sont ses parents ___ l'ont aidé.
questions.explanation: The blank is the subject of "l'ont aidé" (the parents helped him), so the subject relative pronoun "qui" is needed, not "que" or "dont".
The emphasized phrase "ce soir" is singular, so the structure is "C'est" ... que je pars; "Ce sont" is only for plural stressed nouns, and "Il est" does not form this cleft.
"mon frère" is the person who drives, so it is the subject of "conduit" and takes the subject pronoun "qui".

questions.prompt: Ce sont ces mots ___ m'ont blessé.
questions.explanation: "ces mots" is the subject of "m'ont blessé" (the words hurt me), so the subject pronoun "qui" follows "Ce sont".

questions.prompt: ___ pour cette raison que je suis venu.
questions.explanation: The stressed phrase "pour cette raison" is an adverbial complement, so it is introduced by "C'est" ... que; "Ce sont" needs a plural noun and "Il est" is not used for this emphasis.
questions.meaning: it is (stresses the phrase that follows)

questions.explanation: "ainsi" is an adverb, not the subject of "a commencé" (which already has "tout"), so the cleft takes "que", not "qui"; "dont" does not fit.

questions.prompt: Ce sont nos voisins ___ ont appelé.
questions.explanation: "nos voisins" is the subject of "ont appelé" (the neighbours called), so the subject pronoun "qui" is required.
With the stressed pronoun "toi" the cleft is "C'est" toi qui décides; "Ce sont" is only for plural third-person nouns, and "Il est" does not form the structure.
"cette idée" is the direct object of "je préfère" (I prefer this idea), so the object pronoun "que" is needed, not "qui".

questions.prompt: Ce sont les enfants ___ jouent dehors.
questions.explanation: "les enfants" is the subject of "jouent", so the subject pronoun "qui" follows "Ce sont".
The stressed word "maintenant" is an adverb of time, so the cleft is "C'est" maintenant que; "Ce sont" needs a plural noun and "Il est" is not used here.
questions.meaning: it is (stresses the word that follows)

questions.prompt: C'est ce professeur ___ enseigne le mieux.
questions.explanation: "ce professeur" is the subject of "enseigne" (he teaches best), so the subject pronoun "qui" is needed, not "que" or "dont".

questions.prompt: Ce sont ces raisons ___ expliquent son départ.
questions.explanation: In c'est/ce sont ... qui, the relative pronoun is the subject of "expliquent" (ces raisons explain his departure), so the subject form "qui" is needed; "que" would introduce an object.

units.title: Double Object Pronouns
units.description: Combining two pronouns — Combining two object pronouns in one sentence.

questions.explanation: When two pronouns combine, the direct object comes right after "te"; ce livre is masculine singular, so "le" is used: Je te le donne.
The direct object la lettre is feminine singular and replaced by the pronoun, which elides before the vowel of envoie: Il me "l'"envoie. "lui" is an indirect pronoun and cannot fill this slot.
questions.meaning: it, him, her (elided direct object pronoun)
questions.example: Il me l'envoie.

questions.explanation: Ces fleurs is a plural direct object, so the pronoun after "vous" is "les": Nous vous les offrons. "leur" is an indirect pronoun and would not stand for the flowers.
La photo is the feminine singular direct object, so the pronoun "l'" elides before a vowel, and the participle montrée agrees with it: Elle nous l'a montrée.

questions.prompt: Je le ___ ai déjà dit (à mon collègue).
questions.explanation: The indirect object à mon collègue (one person) is replaced by "lui", which follows le in the order le + lui: Je le lui ai déjà dit. "leur" would be plural.
questions.meaning: to him, to her (indirect object pronoun)

questions.explanation: Hier calls for the passé composé, and the subject tu takes avoir in the form "as dit": Tu me l'as dit hier. The l' (le) is masculine singular, so dit does not agree.
Hier requires the passé composé, and the preceding plural direct object les makes the participle agree, so "a envoyés" is needed: Il nous les a envoyés hier.
Demain calls for the future, and the subject je takes the ending -ai: "donnerai". The other forms belong to tu, il/elle or nous.
Hier needs the passé composé; the preceding direct object le is masculine singular, so the participle stays unchanged: "a expliqué" (Elle le leur a expliqué).
Ce matin points to the passé composé and the subject is nous, so avoir is conjugated "avons envoyé": Nous vous l'avons envoyé. The other options use the wrong person.
Hier soir needs the passé composé, and the preceding plural direct object les makes the participle agree: "a rendus" (Il me les a rendus).
The subject "Je" takes the first-person present ending, so the verb is "recommande"; the pronouns "vous la" come before it.
The subject "Tu" needs the passé composé of dire with avoir in the tu form, "as dit"; the pronouns "nous l'" sit before the auxiliary.
All the options are future forms, and "Elle" is third-person singular, so the verb takes the -a ending: "prêtera" (she will gladly lend it to you).
The subject "Ils" is third-person plural, so the present verb takes -ent: "parlent".
"Je" with "demain" calls for the future, first-person singular: "rendrai".
"Nous" with "bientôt" needs the future nous form, "montrerons".
"Il" is third-person singular and "ce soir" points to the future, so the verb is "apportera".

questions.prompt: Elle me l'___ (offrir) pour mon anniversaire.
questions.explanation: "Elle" takes avoir in the passé composé: "a offert"; the participle of offrir is "offert", and "me l'" comes before the auxiliary.
The subject "Tu" takes the present ending -es: "expliques".
The pronoun le becomes l' before a vowel, and with "je" the auxiliary avoir is ai, giving the passé composé "ai promis".
The subject "Nous" takes the -ons ending in the present: "souhaitons".

questions.prompt: Ils me l'___ (rendre ; l' = la clé) la semaine dernière.
questions.explanation: "la semaine dernière" needs the passé composé with avoir, and the preceding direct object "la" makes the participle agree in the feminine: "ont rendue".
questions.meaning: they gave back, they have returned
questions.example: Ils me l'ont rendue la semaine dernière.

questions.explanation: The subject "Elle" is third-person singular, so the present tense of envoyer takes "envoie"; the pronouns nous les come before the verb.
The subject "Je" takes the first-person singular present of confirmer, which is "confirme" (not -es, -ez or -ent); vous le sits before the verb.

units.title: Faire causatif
units.description: Faire + infinitive — The causative construction: having something done.

questions.explanation: After "fais" (faire causatif) the next verb stays in the infinitive, so the answer is "réparer", not a participle or conjugated form.
Faire causatif ("fait" + verb) means having something done by someone else, and the verb that follows is always an infinitive: "construire", not construit or construite.
After "fait" in the causative the verb stays in the infinitive, so "nettoyer" is correct; the participle nettoyé or the present nettoie would not work here.
Even though "faisons" is conjugated, the verb after it is not: faire causatif takes the bare infinitive "livrer" (we have the furniture delivered).

questions.prompt: Vous vous faites ___ (to cut) les cheveux.
questions.explanation: In the causative, the verb after faire stays in the infinitive, so it is "couper" (not "coupé"): someone else cuts your hair.
questions.example: Vous vous faites couper les cheveux.

questions.explanation: After faire, the second verb is always an infinitive, so it is "peindre": they have someone paint their house.

questions.prompt: Je me fais ___ (to cut) les cheveux.
questions.explanation: In 'se faire + infinitive', the second verb does not change form, so it is "couper": the hairdresser cuts my hair.

questions.prompt: Elle se fait ___ (to do) une manucure.
questions.explanation: The causative is faire + infinitive, even when the infinitive is faire itself, so it is "faire": she has a manicure done for her.
questions.meaning: to make, to do (faire faire: to have something done)

questions.prompt: Il fait ___ (to install) une nouvelle cuisine.
questions.explanation: After faire, the verb stays in the infinitive, so it is "installer" (not "installé"): he has a new kitchen fitted.
In the causative, the second verb is an infinitive, so it is "traduire": we have someone translate this document.
After faire, the verb stays in the infinitive, so it is "réviser": you have your car serviced.
The causative needs faire + infinitive, so it is "livrer" (not "livré"): they have the parcel delivered.

questions.prompt: Je fais ___ (to do) mes devoirs par mon frère.
questions.explanation: After faire comes an infinitive, even faire itself, so it is "faire": I have my brother do my homework.
questions.meaning: to make, to do (faire faire: to have something done)
