questions.example: Je fais faire des travaux dans ma cuisine.

questions.prompt: Elle fait ___ (to send) un cadeau à sa mère.
questions.explanation: In the causative, the second verb is an infinitive, so it is "envoyer": she has a present sent to her mother.

questions.prompt: Il fait ___ (to let know) la nouvelle à tout le monde.
questions.explanation: 'Faire savoir' means to let someone know, and the verb after faire stays in the infinitive, so it is "savoir".
questions.meaning: to know (faire savoir: to let know)
questions.example: Il a fait savoir à tout le monde qu'il démissionnait.

questions.explanation: After faire, the verb remains an infinitive, so it is "réparer" (not "réparé"): we have the roof repaired.
"Faites imprimer les documents" means to have the documents printed, so the infinitive "imprimer" follows faire; the other verbs do not match the meaning to print.
"Font agrandir leur maison" means they are having their house extended; faire causatif takes the infinitive "agrandir", which matches the clue 'to enlarge'.
questions.meaning: to enlarge, to extend (have it extended)

questions.prompt: Je fais ___ (to send for) le plombier.
questions.explanation: "Faire venir" is the set expression for sending for someone, so "venir" is right: I have the plumber come, whereas entrer, partir and travailler do not mean to send for.
questions.meaning: to come (faire venir: to send for)

questions.prompt: Elle fait ___ (to tour) la ville à ses invités.
questions.explanation: "Faire visiter" means to show someone around, so "visiter" fits la ville à ses invités; the other options do not make sense with this meaning.
questions.meaning: to visit (faire visiter: to show around)

questions.prompt: Il fait ___ (to laugh) tout le monde.
questions.explanation: "Faire rire quelqu'un" means to make someone laugh, so "rire" is the infinitive after fait; the other verbs do not mean to laugh.
questions.meaning: to laugh (faire rire: to make laugh)

questions.prompt: Nous faisons ___ (to understand) la situation à nos clients.
questions.explanation: "Faire comprendre quelque chose à quelqu'un" means to make someone understand it, so the infinitive "comprendre" follows faisons, matching the clue 'to understand'.
questions.meaning: to understand (faire comprendre: to make someone understand)
questions.example: Nous lui faisons comprendre la situation.

questions.explanation: "remarquer" is correct here. The causative construction: faire + infinitive.
questions.meaning: to notice (faire remarquer: to point out)
questions.example: Vous lui faites remarquer le problème.

questions.prompt: Ils font ___ (to pay) la note à leur client.
questions.explanation: "Faire payer la note à quelqu'un" is the causative meaning 'to make someone pay the bill', and the clue (to pay) plus "la note" points to "payer".
"Faire attendre quelqu'un" means 'to keep someone waiting', which matches the clue (to wait); after "faire" the verb stays in the infinitive: "attendre".

units.title: Formal Letter Writing Phrases
units.description: Professional correspondence — Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "Dear Sir or Madam" is…
questions.explanation: "Madame, Monsieur" is the standard opening salutation of a formal letter to someone whose name you don't know. The other options are closing formulas or polite phrases used later in the letter.

bank: je souhaite attirer votre attention sur
questions.explanation: Yours sincerely → Veuillez agréer mes salutations distinguées. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "I am writing to inform you" is…
choices: je vous écris pour vous informer
questions.explanation: "je vous écris pour vous informer" is the standard opening of a formal letter announcing information, literally "I am writing to you to inform you".

questions.prompt: The French for "please find attached" is… ___
bank: Je vous écris pour vous informer
questions.explanation: please find attached → veuillez trouver ci-joint. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "I look forward to hearing from you" is…
questions.explanation: I look forward to hearing from you → dans l'attente de votre réponse. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.
best regards → cordialement. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "with reference to" is…
choices: Je vous écris pour vous informer
questions.explanation: with reference to → en référence à. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "I would be grateful if you could" is… ___
questions.explanation: I would be grateful if you could → "je vous serais reconnaissant de" (+ infinitive); a woman writes "reconnaissante".

questions.prompt: The French for "please do not hesitate to contact me" is…
questions.explanation: "n'hésitez pas à me contacter" is the polite set phrase inviting the reader to get in touch. "Dans l'attente de votre réponse" means you are waiting for a reply, and the "ci-joint" phrases announce an attachment.

questions.prompt: The French for "I apologize for the inconvenience" is… ___
bank: je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée
questions.answer: je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée
questions.explanation: I apologize for the inconvenience → je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "following our conversation" is… ___
bank: Je vous écris pour vous informer
je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée
questions.explanation: following our conversation → suite à notre conversation. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "enclosed you will find" is…
questions.explanation: enclosed you will find → vous trouverez ci-joint. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "thank you for your understanding" is… ___
bank: je souhaite attirer votre attention sur
questions.explanation: thank you for your understanding → merci de votre compréhension. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

questions.prompt: The French for "I remain at your disposal" is…
questions.explanation: "je reste à votre disposition" is the standard closing line offering further help, built on the set expression être à la disposition de quelqu'un, with vous for formal letters.

questions.prompt: The French for "kindly note that" is… ___
questions.explanation: "veuillez noter que" uses veuillez, the polite imperative of vouloir, which French letters use for 'kindly' or 'please' requests.

questions.prompt: The French for "as per your request" is…
choices: je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée
je vous écris pour vous informer
questions.explanation: "conformément à votre demande" means 'in accordance with your request'; conformément à is the formal way to say 'as per'.

questions.prompt: The French for "in the meantime" is… ___
questions.explanation: "dans l'intervalle" literally means 'in the interval' and is a formal written way to say 'in the meantime', more elevated than en attendant.

questions.prompt: The French for "should you have any questions" is…
questions.explanation: French renders the English 'should you have' with a plain si + present tense, so "si vous avez des questions" is the natural formal equivalent.

questions.prompt: The French for "I would like to draw your attention to" is… ___
bank: je souhaite attirer votre attention sur
questions.answer: je souhaite attirer votre attention sur
questions.explanation: "je souhaite attirer votre attention sur" uses the fixed expression attirer l'attention de quelqu'un sur, 'to draw someone's attention to', with souhaiter as the polite 'would like'.
"respectueusement" is the adverb from respectueux, 'respectful'; the -ment ending works like English -ly.

questions.prompt: The French for "subject (of a letter)" is…
choices: je m'excuse pour la gêne occasionnée
Je vous écris pour vous informer
questions.explanation: subject (of a letter) → objet. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.
"le destinataire" is the person a letter or email is addressed to (destiné à, 'intended for'), the opposite of l'expéditeur.
"l'expéditeur" is the person who sends (expédier) a letter or parcel; le elides to l' before the vowel.
attachment → la pièce jointe. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.
signature → la signature. Set phrases for formal letters and emails.

units.title: Say It Your Way
units.description: Write the idea in French — Express nuanced or hypothetical ideas in your own words; more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say the project would have succeeded with more funding.
acceptableAnswers: Le projet aurait réussi avec plus de financement.
Avec davantage de fonds, le projet aurait abouti.
Le manque de financement a empêché la réussite du projet.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Le projet aurait réussi avec plus de financement." The past conditional "aurait réussi" expresses what would have happened if the condition had been met.

acceptableAnswers: Bon, d'accord, si tu insistes.
Je suppose que tu as raison.
Soit, allons-y, mais à contrecœur.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Bon, d'accord, si tu insistes." "Bon, d'accord" signals hesitation, and "si tu insistes" shows you are only giving in to your friend.

questions.prompt: Say you wish you had studied harder.
acceptableAnswers: J'aurais aimé étudier plus sérieusement.
Si seulement j'avais travaillé plus dur.
Je regrette de ne pas avoir étudié davantage.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'aurais aimé étudier plus sérieusement." The past conditional "j'aurais aimé" expresses a regret about the past, like "I wish I had".

questions.prompt: Argue that the policy is unfair.
acceptableAnswers: Cette politique me semble injuste.
Je trouve cette mesure injuste.
Cette politique désavantage clairement certains groupes.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cette politique me semble injuste." Using me semble or je trouve presents unfairness as your argued opinion rather than a bare fact.

acceptableAnswers: Le résultat a dépassé nos attentes.
On ne s'attendait pas à un si bon résultat.
C'est mieux que ce qu'on espérait.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Le résultat a dépassé nos attentes." The fixed phrase dépasser les attentes means 'to exceed expectations', in the passé composé for a completed outcome.

questions.prompt: Concede a point while maintaining your position.
acceptableAnswers: Certes, mais je maintiens mon point de vue.
C'est vrai, cependant je ne change pas d'avis.
J'admets ce fait, sans pour autant changer d'opinion.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Certes, mais je maintiens mon point de vue." Certes concedes the point, and mais je maintiens holds your position.

questions.prompt: Say you would reconsider under different circumstances.
acceptableAnswers: Je reconsidérerais ma position dans d'autres circonstances.
Dans d'autres circonstances, je reviendrais sur ma décision.
Je pourrais changer d'avis si la situation évoluait.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "Je reconsidérerais ma position dans d'autres circonstances." The conditional "reconsidérerais" makes it hypothetical; other conditional wordings such as "Je pourrais changer d'avis si la situation évoluait." are also right.

acceptableAnswers: Je reste sceptique face à cette affirmation.
Ça me semble difficile à croire.
J'ai du mal à croire cette version des faits.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "Je reste sceptique face à cette affirmation." "Rester sceptique face à" signals polite doubt; "J'ai du mal à croire…" works too.

questions.prompt: Say the negotiation reached an impasse.
acceptableAnswers: La négociation est dans une impasse.
Les discussions n'avancent plus.
On est bloqués, la négociation n'aboutit pas.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "La négociation est dans une impasse." "Être dans une impasse" is the set phrase for talks that are stuck; "Les discussions n'avancent plus." says the same thing more simply.

questions.prompt: Say you would have acted differently.
acceptableAnswers: J'aurais agi différemment.
À ta place, j'aurais fait autrement.
Je n'aurais pas procédé de cette façon.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'aurais agi différemment." The past conditional "j'aurais agi" describes what you would have done in a past situation.

questions.prompt: Point out an inconsistency in a friend's argument.
acceptableAnswers: Il y a une incohérence dans ton raisonnement.
Ton argument se contredit.
Je remarque une contradiction dans ce que tu dis.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Il y a une incohérence dans ton raisonnement." "Une incohérence" names the logical flaw directly but politely.

questions.prompt: Say the company is undergoing restructuring.
acceptableAnswers: L'entreprise traverse une restructuration.
La société est en pleine réorganisation.
L'entreprise revoit actuellement sa structure.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "L'entreprise traverse une restructuration." "Traverser" presents the restructuring as a phase the company is currently going through.

acceptableAnswers: Je suis prudemment optimiste.
J'ai bon espoir, sans trop m'avancer.
Je reste raisonnablement confiant.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je suis prudemment optimiste." The adverb "prudemment" tones down the optimism; "J'ai bon espoir, sans trop m'avancer" works too.

acceptableAnswers: Les preuves ne sont pas concluantes.
Rien ne permet de conclure avec certitude.
Les éléments recueillis restent insuffisants.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Les preuves ne sont pas concluantes." "Concluantes" means the evidence does not settle the question, and it agrees with the feminine plural "preuves".

acceptableAnswers: Peut-être devrions-nous chercher un compromis.
Il existe sûrement une solution intermédiaire.
Trouvons un juste milieu entre les deux positions.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Peut-être devrions-nous chercher un compromis." The conditional "devrions" makes the suggestion tentative, and "peut-être" at the start triggers the inversion "devrions-nous".

acceptableAnswers: Ce délai me semble irréaliste.
Ce délai n'est pas tenable.
Il sera difficile de respecter une échéance aussi serrée.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ce délai me semble irréaliste." "Me semble" presents the criticism as your opinion, which keeps it polite.

acceptableAnswers: Je dois avouer une certaine frustration.
Cette situation commence à m'agacer, je l'admets.
Je ne vais pas cacher que c'est frustrant.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je dois avouer une certaine frustration." "Avouer" and "une certaine" soften the complaint, so it stays diplomatic.

questions.prompt: Say the theory has since been disproven.
acceptableAnswers: Cette théorie a depuis été réfutée.
On a depuis démontré que cette théorie était fausse.
Cette théorie ne tient plus depuis de nouvelles découvertes.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cette théorie a depuis été réfutée." The passive "a été réfutée" agrees with "théorie", and "depuis" translates "since".

acceptableAnswers: C'était une erreur de ma part, je le reconnais.
J'admets m'être trompé.
J'admets m'être trompée.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "C'était une erreur de ma part, je le reconnais." It admits the mistake plainly without saying sorry over and over; "J'admets m'être trompé(e)" works too.

questions.prompt: Say the market has become increasingly competitive.
acceptableAnswers: Le marché est devenu de plus en plus concurrentiel.
La concurrence s'est nettement intensifiée.
Le secteur est aujourd'hui beaucoup plus compétitif.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Le marché est devenu de plus en plus concurrentiel." "De plus en plus" expresses "increasingly", and "devenir" takes "être" in the passé composé.

questions.prompt: Express that you are torn between two options.
acceptableAnswers: J'hésite entre les deux options.
Je suis partagé entre les deux choix.
Je suis partagée entre les deux choix.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'hésite entre les deux options." "Hésiter entre" expresses being torn; "Je suis partagé(e)" also works, and the adjective agrees with the speaker.

questions.prompt: Say the report raises more questions than it answers.
acceptableAnswers: Ce rapport soulève plus de questions qu'il n'en résout.
Ce rapport laisse plus de questions en suspens qu'il n'apporte de réponses.
Ce rapport suscite plus d'interrogations qu'il n'apporte de réponses.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ce rapport soulève plus de questions qu'il n'en résout." The comparison "plus de... que" uses the formal ne explétif, and "en" stands for "questions".

questions.prompt: Downplay the significance of an event.
acceptableAnswers: Ce n'est pas si grave que ça.
Il ne faut pas exagérer l'importance de cet événement.
Ça n'a pas tant d'importance, en fin de compte.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "Ce n'est pas si grave que ça." The structure "pas si… que ça" shrinks the importance of something; "Ça n'a pas tant d'importance" works the same way.

questions.prompt: Say the initiative fell short of its goals.
acceptableAnswers: L'initiative n'a pas atteint ses objectifs.
Les objectifs de cette initiative n'ont pas été atteints.
Cette initiative est restée en deçà de ses ambitions.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "L'initiative n'a pas atteint ses objectifs." "Atteindre ses objectifs" means to reach one's goals, so the negative says it fell short; "rester en deçà de" is a more formal option.

acceptableAnswers: J'admire sa résilience.
Sa capacité à tenir bon force le respect.
C'est vraiment impressionnant, sa résilience.
questions.explanation: One natural way: "J'admire sa résilience." "Admirer" takes a direct object, and "résilience" is the same idea as in English; "force le respect" is a stronger, more formal option.

questions.answer: Puisqu'il pleut, nous resterons à la maison.

questions.answer: Chaque fois que je le vois, il me parle de son travail.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Chaque fois que je le vois, il me parle de son travail." "Chaque fois que" (every time) introduces a repeated situation, with both clauses in the present.

questions.answer: Plus j'y pense, plus je suis convaincu.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Plus j'y pense, plus je suis convaincu." The pattern "plus… plus…" means "the more… the more…", and needs no article or "que".

questions.answer: Que tu le veuilles ou non, il faut le faire.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Que tu le veuilles ou non, il faut le faire." "Que… ou non" (whether or not) takes the subjunctive, so "vouloir" becomes "veuilles".

questions.answer: Bien que je sois occupé, je vais t'aider.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Bien que je sois occupé, je vais t'aider." "Bien que" (although) always takes the subjunctive, hence "sois" rather than "suis".

questions.answer: Une fois que ce sera fini, nous pourrons partir.
questions.explanation: Target phrase: "Une fois que ce sera fini, nous pourrons partir." After "une fois que", French uses the future "sera" when the main clause is in the future, where English uses the present.

units.title: Advanced Idioms & Nuance
units.description: Meaning match — C1-level idioms for nuanced, natural French.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre les points sur les i" roughly means… ___
bank: to have a dispute with someone
questions.explanation: Literally "to put the dots on the i's", "mettre les points sur les i" means "to clarify things precisely", leaving no room for misunderstanding.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir maille à partir avec quelqu'un" roughly means…
choices: to have a dispute with someone
to hit it off with someone
to put all one's eggs in one basket
questions.explanation: "Avoir maille à partir avec quelqu'un" comes from an old phrase about sharing a tiny coin (maille) that could not be split, so it means "to have a dispute with someone".

questions.prompt: The idiom "ne pas y aller par quatre chemins" roughly means… ___
bank: to get straight to the point
questions.answer: to get straight to the point
questions.explanation: Literally "not to go by four roads", "ne pas y aller par quatre chemins" means "to get straight to the point" without detours.

questions.prompt: The idiom "être pris la main dans le sac" roughly means…
choices: to be on the same wavelength
to hold a grudge against someone
questions.explanation: Literally "to be caught with one's hand in the bag", "être pris la main dans le sac" means "to be caught red-handed".

bank: to hold a grudge against someone
to give up, throw in the towel
to be on the same wavelength
questions.answer: to give up, throw in the towel
questions.explanation: "to give up, throw in the towel" is right because "jeter l'éponge" comes from boxing, where a trainer throws the sponge into the ring to concede the fight.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le vent en poupe" roughly means…
questions.explanation: "to be thriving, have momentum" is right because "avoir le vent en poupe" is a sailing image: the wind blows from behind (la poupe = the stern) and pushes you forward.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre du beurre dans les épinards" roughly means… ___
bank: to support each other, stick together
to improve one's financial situation slightly
questions.answer: to improve one's financial situation slightly
questions.explanation: Butter makes plain spinach richer, so "mettre du beurre dans les épinards" means "to improve one's financial situation slightly", for example with a small extra income.

questions.prompt: The idiom "ne pas être dans son assiette" roughly means…
choices: to get straight to the point
to make a big deal out of nothing
questions.explanation: Here "assiette" is an old word for one's normal balance or state, so not being "dans son assiette" means "to not feel well" or to feel out of sorts.

questions.prompt: The idiom "filer à l'anglaise" roughly means… ___
bank: to improve one's financial situation slightly
to have full freedom to act
to be on the same wavelength
questions.explanation: "Filer à l'anglaise" means "to leave without saying goodbye": you slip away quietly, the way English speakers say 'to take French leave'.

questions.prompt: The idiom "tirer les ficelles" roughly means…
choices: to pull the strings behind the scenes
to get straight to the point
questions.explanation: "Tirer les ficelles" is a puppeteer image, so it means "to pull the strings behind the scenes": someone secretly controls what happens.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la langue bien pendue" roughly means…
choices: to hold a grudge against someone
questions.explanation: "Avoir la langue bien pendue" pictures a tongue that hangs loose and is always ready to move, so it means "to be very talkative".

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre la main à la pâte" roughly means… ___
bank: to pull the strings behind the scenes
to make a big deal out of nothing
to have full freedom to act
questions.explanation: "Mettre la main à la pâte" literally means putting your hand in the dough, so it means "to get involved and help" with the work yourself.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir des atomes crochus avec quelqu'un" roughly means…
choices: to support each other, stick together
to hit it off with someone
questions.explanation: "Avoir des atomes crochus avec quelqu'un" pictures atoms that hook onto each other, so it means "to hit it off with someone" and click instantly.

questions.prompt: The idiom "ne pas mâcher ses mots" roughly means… ___
bank: to put all one's eggs in one basket
to have a dispute with someone
questions.explanation: "Ne pas mâcher ses mots" means not chewing your words to soften them, so it means "to speak bluntly".

questions.prompt: The idiom "être sur la même longueur d'onde" roughly means…
choices: to be on the same wavelength
to make a big deal out of nothing
to have full freedom to act
to improve one's financial situation slightly
questions.explanation: "Être sur la même longueur d'onde" uses the same radio image as English, so it means "to be on the same wavelength": two people think alike.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un poids sur la conscience" roughly means… ___
bank: to hit it off with someone
questions.explanation: "Avoir un poids sur la conscience" means carrying a weight on your conscience, so it means "to feel guilty about something".

questions.prompt: The idiom "prendre le taureau par les cornes" roughly means…
choices: to have a dispute with someone
to put all one's eggs in one basket
questions.explanation: "Prendre le taureau par les cornes" means grabbing the bull by the horns, so it means "to tackle a problem head-on" instead of avoiding it.

questions.prompt: The idiom "en faire tout un fromage" roughly means… ___
bank: to make a big deal out of nothing
to be on the same wavelength
to jump from one topic to another
questions.answer: to make a big deal out of nothing
questions.explanation: "En faire tout un fromage" means turning a small matter into a whole cheese, so it means "to make a big deal out of nothing".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le dernier mot" roughly means…
choices: to hit it off with someone
to get straight to the point
questions.explanation: "Avoir le dernier mot" works as in English and means "to have the last word": you end the argument and win it.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre tous ses œufs dans le même panier" roughly means… ___
bank: to put all one's eggs in one basket
to have a dispute with someone
questions.answer: to put all one's eggs in one basket
questions.explanation: "Mettre tous ses œufs dans le même panier" is the same image as English, so it means "to put all one's eggs in one basket": you risk everything on a single option.

questions.prompt: The idiom "c'est la goutte d'eau qui fait déborder le vase" roughly means… ___
bank: to be on the same wavelength
to jump from one topic to another
questions.explanation: Literally 'the drop of water that makes the vase overflow': one small final annoyance that makes everything spill over, so it means "it's the last straw".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir une dent contre quelqu'un" roughly means…
choices: to hold a grudge against someone
questions.explanation: Literally 'to have a tooth against someone': you keep wanting to bite them over an old offence, so it means "to hold a grudge against someone".

questions.prompt: The idiom "passer du coq à l'âne" roughly means… ___
bank: to hit it off with someone
to put all one's eggs in one basket
to jump from one topic to another
questions.answer: to jump from one topic to another
questions.explanation: Literally 'to go from the rooster to the donkey': you switch abruptly between unrelated things, so it means "to jump from one topic to another".

questions.prompt: The idiom "se serrer les coudes" roughly means…
choices: to have a dispute with someone
to support each other, stick together
questions.explanation: Literally 'to squeeze elbows together': people stand shoulder to shoulder to face a difficulty, so it means "to support each other, stick together".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir carte blanche" roughly means… ___
bank: to have full freedom to act
to have a dispute with someone
questions.answer: to have full freedom to act
questions.explanation: Literally 'to have a blank card': you are handed a signed blank page to fill in as you wish, so it means "to have full freedom to act".

units.title: Formal & Literary Register
units.description: High-register written French — C1-level formal and literary phrasing.

questions.prompt: Nonobstant les difficultés, il a ___ (reached) son objectif.
questions.explanation: "atteint" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ (to stress) que la situation est complexe.
questions.explanation: "Il convient de souligner que" is the formal way to stress a point ('it should be emphasised that'), and "souligner" introduces a "que" clause stating a fact.

questions.prompt: Force est de ___ que les résultats sont décevants.
questions.explanation: "Force est de constater que" is a fixed formal phrase meaning 'one must acknowledge that'; only "constater" completes it.

questions.prompt: Il n'en demeure pas moins que la question reste ___.
questions.explanation: The adjective after "reste" agrees with the feminine singular "la question", so "ouverte"; "la question reste ouverte" means it is still unresolved.

questions.prompt: En dépit des efforts consentis, le projet a ___.
questions.explanation: "échoué" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.

questions.prompt: Il s'agit là d'une problématique qui mérite d'être ___.
questions.explanation: After "mérite d'être" a past participle is needed, agreeing with the feminine "une problématique": "approfondie".

questions.prompt: Loin de moi l'idée de ___ vos compétences.
questions.explanation: "remettre en question" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.
questions.meaning: to call into question, to challenge

questions.prompt: Quoi qu'il en soit, la décision a été ___.
questions.explanation: In the passive "a été prise" the participle agrees with the feminine subject "la décision", so "prise".

questions.prompt: Il importe de ___ les enjeux avant d'agir.
questions.explanation: "Il importe de" is followed by an infinitive, and "cerner les enjeux" means to define the issues precisely before acting: "cerner".
questions.meaning: to pin down, to define precisely

questions.prompt: Cela étant dit, il convient de ___ prudemment.
questions.explanation: After "il convient de" you need an infinitive, and "procéder" means 'to go about it', so it works with just an adverb: "procéder prudemment".
questions.meaning: to proceed, to go about it

questions.prompt: Il n'est pas anodin de ___ que ce phénomène persiste.
questions.explanation: The structure "il n'est pas anodin de" must be followed by an infinitive, and "noter" (to note) takes the clause "que ce phénomène persiste"; the other forms are not infinitives.

questions.prompt: On ne saurait ___ l'importance de ce facteur.
questions.explanation: "On ne saurait" (one cannot) is followed by an infinitive, and "sous-estimer" (to underestimate) is the one that fits "l'importance de ce facteur".

questions.prompt: Il paraît opportun de ___ cette hypothèse.
questions.explanation: After "opportun de" you need an infinitive, and "explorer" is the only infinitive in the list; it also suits "cette hypothèse" (to look into a hypothesis).
questions.example: Il paraît opportun d'explorer cette hypothèse.

questions.prompt: Tout porte à croire que la tendance va se ___.
questions.explanation: "Va se" (is going to) needs an infinitive, and "poursuivre" gives the reflexive "se poursuivre", meaning 'to continue', which fits "la tendance".
"Il serait présomptueux de" takes an infinitive, and "affirmer" (to assert) with "en ... davantage" means 'to claim more about it'.

questions.prompt: Ceci étant, il convient de ___ nos attentes à la baisse.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "revoir à la baisse" (to scale down), so "revoir" fits "nos attentes à la baisse"; the other verbs do not combine with "à la baisse".

questions.prompt: Il va sans dire que cette approche ___ ses limites.
questions.explanation: The subject "cette approche" needs a conjugated verb, and "comporte" (involves, has) is the natural collocation with "ses limites".

questions.prompt: Il est indéniable que ce constat ___ la réflexion.
questions.explanation: "Susciter la réflexion" means 'to prompt reflection', so "suscite" is the verb that fits "ce constat" as subject; the other verbs make no sense with "la réflexion".

questions.prompt: Rien ne permet d'___ une telle conclusion (= l'appuyer par des preuves).
questions.explanation: The bracketed clue "l'appuyer par des preuves" (to back it up with evidence) is the meaning of "étayer"; the other verbs mean to dismiss, assert or disprove.

questions.prompt: Il conviendrait d'___ cette question plus avant.
questions.explanation: "examiner" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.
questions.example: Il conviendrait d'examiner cette question plus avant.

questions.prompt: Nul ne saurait ___ la portée de cet événement.
questions.explanation: "nier" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.

questions.prompt: Il est à ___ que peu de mesures aient été prises.
questions.explanation: "déplorer" is correct here. C1-level formal and literary phrasing.
questions.example: Il est à déplorer que peu de mesures aient été prises.

questions.prompt: Ainsi qu'il a été ___ précédemment, les résultats varient.
questions.explanation: "mentionné" is right because "ainsi qu'il a été mentionné précédemment" is the standard formal way to refer back to something already said; the other participles do not mean 'said earlier'.

questions.prompt: Il demeure difficile de ___ avec certitude.
questions.explanation: "conclure" fits because it can stand alone and pairs naturally with "avec certitude" (to reach a firm conclusion); survoler, détailler and parcourir all need a direct object, which this sentence does not have.

questions.prompt: Toutes choses étant égales par ailleurs, la situation devrait s'___ (= devenir meilleure).
questions.explanation: "améliorer" matches the clue "devenir meilleure" (become better) and fits the reflexive "s'améliorer"; "s'aggraver" and "s'envenimer" mean getting worse.
questions.example: Toutes choses égales par ailleurs, la situation devrait s'améliorer.

units.title: Nuanced Connectors
units.description: Advanced discourse markers — C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

bank: introduce a separate but related point
questions.explanation: néanmoins → introduce a contrast, similar to "nevertheless". C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

choices: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
questions.explanation: toutefois → introduce a formal contrast, "however". C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "cela dit" is used to… ___
bank: concede a point before continuing, "that said"
express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"
questions.answer: concede a point before continuing, "that said"
questions.explanation: "concede a point before continuing, "that said"" is right because "cela dit" accepts what was just said (cela) and then adds a reservation, like English "that said".

questions.prompt: The connector "en revanche" is used to…
choices: mark a strong contrast between two ideas
express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"
questions.explanation: en revanche → mark a strong contrast between two ideas. C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

bank: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
introduce a logical turning point in an argument
questions.answer: introduce a logical turning point in an argument
questions.explanation: or → introduce a logical turning point in an argument. C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "du reste" is used to…
questions.explanation: du reste → add a supporting remark, "moreover". C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "qui plus est" is used to… ___
bank: introduce a concession in everyday formal speech, "although" (+ subjunctive)
add emphasis to a preceding point
questions.answer: add emphasis to a preceding point
questions.explanation: qui plus est → add emphasis to a preceding point. C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "en outre" is used to…
choices: introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"
concede a point before continuing, "that said"
questions.explanation: en outre → add formal additional information. C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "de surcroît" is used to… ___
bank: express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"
explain a reason or condition, "insofar as"
questions.explanation: de surcroît → add extra formal emphasis. C1-level connectors for formal spoken and written French.

questions.prompt: The connector "par ailleurs" is used to…
choices: concede despite an obstacle, "the fact remains that"
introduce a separate but related point
introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
questions.explanation: "introduce a separate but related point" is right because "par ailleurs" literally means "elsewhere" and opens a different angle on the topic, like "furthermore" or "in other respects".

questions.prompt: The connector "dans la mesure où" is used to…
choices: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
explain a reason or condition, "insofar as"
introduce a logical turning point in an argument
questions.explanation: "explain a reason or condition, "insofar as"" is right because "dans la mesure où" (literally "in the measure where") limits or justifies a statement, as in "insofar as" or "since", and takes the indicative.

questions.prompt: The connector "étant donné que" is used to… ___
bank: mark a strong contrast between two ideas
questions.explanation: Étant donné que presents a known fact as the reason for what follows (Étant donné qu'il pleut, on reste à la maison), so the answer is "introduce a cause, "given that"".

questions.prompt: The connector "de sorte que" is used to…
choices: introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"
concede a point before continuing, "that said"
questions.explanation: "express a result, "so that"" is right because "de sorte que" + indicative states the outcome of an action ("so that"); with the subjunctive it expresses an intended purpose.

bank: introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
questions.answer: introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
questions.explanation: Quoique means "although", takes the subjunctive (quoiqu'il soit tard) and sounds a little more literary than bien que, so the answer is "introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)".

questions.prompt: The connector "bien que" is used to…
choices: explain a reason or condition, "insofar as"
introduce a concession in everyday formal speech, "although" (+ subjunctive)
questions.explanation: Bien que means "although" and must be followed by the subjunctive (Bien qu'il soit malade, il travaille), so the answer is "introduce a concession in everyday formal speech, "although" (+ subjunctive)".

questions.prompt: The connector "à moins que" is used to… ___
bank: add emphasis to a preceding point
introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
questions.explanation: "introduce an exception, "unless" (+ subjunctive)" is right because "à moins que" names the one case that would cancel the main clause, and it is followed by the subjunctive, often with a ne explétif (à moins qu'il ne pleuve).

questions.prompt: The connector "pourvu que" is used to…
choices: concede despite an obstacle, "the fact remains that"
questions.explanation: "express a condition, "provided that"" is right because "pourvu que" + subjunctive sets the condition the main clause depends on; on its own it can also express a hope ("Pourvu qu'il vienne !").

questions.prompt: The connector "de peur que" is used to… ___
bank: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
introduce a logical turning point in an argument
express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"
questions.answer: express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"
questions.explanation: "express a fear-based reason, "for fear that"" is right because "de peur que" + subjunctive gives the feared outcome that motivates the action, often with a ne explétif (de peur qu'il ne parte).

questions.prompt: The connector "si bien que" is used to…
choices: introduce a concession in a more literary register, "although" (+ subjunctive)
add emphasis to a preceding point
add a nuanced final remark, "moreover, besides"
questions.explanation: Si bien que introduces the result of the previous clause (Il a menti, si bien que personne ne le croit), so the answer is "show a natural consequence".

questions.prompt: The connector "faute de quoi" is used to… ___
bank: introduce a separate but related point
concede a point before continuing, "that said"
introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"
questions.explanation: "state a negative consequence, "failing which"" is right because "faute de quoi" (literally "for lack of which") announces what happens if the previous requirement is not met.

questions.prompt: The connector "quant à" is used to… ___
bank: introduce a concession in everyday formal speech, "although" (+ subjunctive)
introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"
introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
questions.answer: introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"
questions.explanation: "introduce a new topic in relation to, "as for"" is right because "quant à" shifts attention to a new person or thing in contrast to what came before (Quant à moi, je reste).

questions.prompt: The connector "au demeurant" is used to…
choices: add a nuanced final remark, "moreover, besides"
questions.explanation: Au demeurant adds a final point that rounds off the argument, much like "for that matter" (Il est, au demeurant, très compétent), so the answer is "add a nuanced final remark, "moreover, besides"".

questions.prompt: The connector "qui pis est" is used to… ___
bank: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
questions.answer: introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"
questions.explanation: Qui pis est adds a point that makes things even worse (Il est en retard et, qui pis est, il a oublié le dossier), so the answer is "introduce a worse consequence, "what is worse"".

questions.prompt: The connector "il n'empêche que" is used to…
choices: concede despite an obstacle, "the fact remains that"
add emphasis to a preceding point
questions.explanation: "concede despite an obstacle, "the fact remains that"" is right because "il n'empêche que" (literally "it does not prevent that") accepts an objection but insists the following fact still holds.

questions.prompt: The connector "tant et si bien que" is used to… ___
questions.explanation: Tant et si bien que stresses that something went on so far that a striking result followed (Il a tant insisté, tant et si bien qu'elle a cédé), so the answer is "emphasize an extreme resulting consequence".

units.title: Nominalisation
units.description: Turning verbs into abstract nouns — C1-level nominalisation, common in formal French writing.

questions.explanation: Décider forms its noun with the suffix -sion, as persuader gives persuasion, so the noun is "la décision".
The noun "l'analyse" is "analyser" without its final -r; the article elides to l' because the noun starts with a vowel.
Verbs ending in -clure form nouns in -clusion, so "conclure" gives "la conclusion" (like exclure → l'exclusion).
"Proposer" forms its noun with the -ition ending, giving "la proposition" (like composer → la composition).
Verbs ending in -uire form their noun in -uction, as produire gives production, so réduire becomes "la réduction".
Améliorer takes the feminine suffix -ation, with elision before the vowel, so the noun is "l'amélioration".
Développer takes the masculine suffix -ement, so the noun is "le développement".
Exiger forms its noun with the feminine suffix -ence, as in urgence, so the noun is "l'exigence".

questions.prompt: The noun form of "échouer" (to fail) is…
questions.explanation: The noun meaning "failure" is "l'échec", an irregular pair: you cannot build it from "échouer" with -tion or -ment.
"la réussite" is the noun of "réussir", formed with -ite rather than -tion. "la réunion" looks similar but comes from "réunir".
Verbs in -uire form nouns in -uction, so "produire" gives "la production". "la réduction" follows the same pattern but comes from "réduire".
Verbs in -aître form nouns in -aissance, and "reconnaître" keeps its prefix re-, giving "la reconnaissance". "la connaissance" comes from "connaître".
"résoudre" changes its stem to résol- in the noun, giving "la résolution". "la dissolution" follows the same pattern but comes from "dissoudre".
"interpréter" drops -er and adds -ation, giving "l'interprétation". The other inter- nouns come from "interrompre", "intervenir" and "interroger".
Verbs in -ifier form nouns in -ification, so "justifier" gives "la justification". "la justice" and "la justesse" come from the adjective "juste", not from the verb.
Verbs in -tenir form nouns in -tien, so "maintenir" gives "le maintien". "l'entretien" and "le soutien" come from "entretenir" and "soutenir".
Verbs in -ir like "établir" (nous établissons) form nouns in -issement, giving "l'établissement". "la stabilisation" comes from "stabiliser", and "l'étable" is a cowshed.
"expliquer" changes -quer to -cation, giving "l'explication". "l'explicitation" comes from "expliciter" instead.
The noun keeps the prefix sug- of "suggérer", giving "la suggestion"; "la digestion" and "la gestion" belong to "digérer" and "gérer", and "la congestion" means congestion.
"la découverte" comes from the past participle "découvert" plus -e, not from a -tion ending. "la couverture" and "l'ouverture" come from "couvrir" and "ouvrir".
Drop the -er ending of "augmenter" and add -ation to get "l'augmentation"; nouns in -ation are feminine, and the article elides to l' before a vowel.
The stem diminu- of "diminuer" takes the suffix -tion, giving "la diminution"; nouns in -tion are feminine.
Drop the -er of "créer" and add -ation to get "la création"; nouns in -ation are feminine.
Drop the -er of "transformer" and add -ation to get "la transformation"; nouns in -ation are feminine.
"Choisir" has an irregular, masculine noun form, "le choix", which is not built with a regular suffix.

units.title: Precision Vocabulary for Debate
units.description: Arguing and persuading in French — C1-level vocabulary for structured argument and debate.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ ce jugement trop tranché avant de conclure.
questions.explanation: "nuancer" is right because a judgment described as "trop tranché" (too clear-cut) needs to be qualified before concluding; "accentuer", "radicaliser" and "durcir" would make it more extreme.
questions.meaning: to qualify, to add nuance to

questions.prompt: Cet argument repose sur une ___ erronée (= point de départ du raisonnement).
questions.explanation: "prémisse" matches the clue "point de départ du raisonnement": an argument rests on a premise, and here that starting point is flawed; a conclusion is where reasoning ends.
questions.meaning: premise, assumption an argument is based on

questions.prompt: Il serait ___ de ne pas tenir compte de ce facteur. (= oversimplifying)
questions.explanation: "réducteur" matches the clue 'oversimplifying': ignoring a relevant factor makes the analysis too simple, and "il serait réducteur de" is the usual formal phrase for this criticism.
questions.example: Il serait réducteur de ne tenir compte que de ce facteur.

questions.prompt: Cette affirmation mérite d'être ___. (= put into perspective)
questions.explanation: "relativisée" matches the clue 'put into perspective' and is feminine to agree with "affirmation" after "d'être"; "réfutée" or "démontrée" would mean disproved or proved, not qualified.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ les avantages et les inconvénients. (= weigh up)
questions.explanation: "peser" matches the clue 'weigh up': one weighs advantages against disadvantages ("peser le pour et le contre"), whereas "réfuter" would mean to disprove them.
questions.meaning: to weigh up, to consider carefully

questions.prompt: Son raisonnement manque de ___. (= logical strictness)
questions.explanation: "rigueur" matches the clue 'logical strictness': reasoning that lacks rigueur is sloppy in its logic, whereas lacking "nuance" or "souplesse" would be about subtlety or flexibility.

questions.prompt: Il est essentiel de ___ les faits des opinions.
questions.explanation: "distinguer" is right because "distinguer A de B" means to tell A apart from B, here facts from opinions; vérifier, défendre and relativiser do not mean telling two things apart.

questions.prompt: Cette thèse repose sur des preuves si solides qu'elle est difficile à ___.
questions.explanation: "réfuter" matches the clue 'prove wrong': a thesis that is hard to refute is hard to show to be false, while "défendre" and "démontrer" mean supporting or proving it.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ cette hypothèse avec prudence. (= approach, tackle)
questions.explanation: The clue "approach, tackle" matches "aborder", and "aborder une hypothèse avec prudence" means to approach an idea carefully. The other verbs mean to refute, defend or reject it, which does not fit with caution.
questions.example: Il convient d'aborder cette hypothèse avec prudence.

questions.prompt: Son argumentation repose sur des ___ solides. (= evidence)
questions.explanation: The clue "evidence" points to "preuves": an argument rests on solid proof. "Prémisses" are starting premises, not evidence, and "opinions" are not solid support.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ la portée de cette déclaration. (= assess)
questions.explanation: The clue "assess" gives "évaluer": you assess the scope ("la portée") of a statement. "Nuancer" means to qualify it, "réfuter" to disprove it and "minimiser" to play it down, none of which means assess.

questions.prompt: Cette position est difficile à ___. (= argue in favour of)
questions.explanation: The clue "argue in favour of" gives "défendre": a position that is hard to defend. "Réfuter" means to argue against it, so it is the opposite of the clue.

questions.prompt: Il est nécessaire de ___ les contre-arguments. (= foresee)
questions.explanation: The clue "foresee" gives "anticiper": a good debater anticipates counter-arguments before they are raised. "Ignorer" and "réfuter" do not mean foresee.
questions.example: Il est nécessaire d'anticiper les contre-arguments.

questions.explanation: The clue "subtlety" gives "nuance": "manquer de nuance" means to lack subtlety. "Rigueur", "clarté" and "cohérence" are different qualities, not subtlety.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ les implications de cette décision.
questions.explanation: "considérer" is correct here. C1-level vocabulary for structured argument and debate.
questions.meaning: to consider, to take into account

questions.explanation: A conclusion follows logically ("découle logiquement") from the "prémisses", the premises of an argument. Objections, nuances and flaws do not give rise to a conclusion in this way.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ les biais possibles dans cette étude.
questions.explanation: Examining a study properly means pinpointing its possible biases, which is what "identifier" means here. "Favoriser", "défendre" and "renforcer" would mean encouraging or strengthening the biases, which makes no sense.

questions.prompt: Son point de vue mérite d'être ___.
questions.explanation: After "être" the passive needs a past participle, and "point de vue" is masculine singular, so "entendu" is right. "Entendue" and "entendus" do not agree, and "entendre" is an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Il est important de ___ les sources utilisées.
questions.explanation: Checking the sources used is basic good practice, so "vérifier" fits "il est important de". "Négliger" means the opposite, and "réfuter" and "nuancer" do not fit sources.
The adjective after "semble" agrees with "critique", which is feminine singular, so "infondée" is right. "Infondé" is masculine, and "infondées" and "infondés" are plural.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ la validité de cet argument. (= to call into question)
questions.explanation: After "Il convient de" French needs an infinitive, and "questionner" means to challenge the validity of an argument. The other forms are a participle or conjugated verbs and cannot follow "de".

"Mais contestable" sets up a contrast, so the first adjective must be positive: "cohérent". It is also masculine to agree with "raisonnement", unlike "cohérente", and "infondé" or "réducteur" are already negative.

questions.prompt: Il faut ___ les faits avant de juger.
questions.explanation: Before judging, you should look into the facts, which is what "examiner" means. "Ignorer", "favoriser" and "réfuter" do not make sense as a step before forming a judgment.
"Rester à" is followed by an infinitive, meaning something still has to be done: "démontrer". The other choices are participles or a conjugated form and cannot follow "à".

questions.prompt: Il est essentiel de ___ un débat constructif.
questions.explanation: Saying it is essential to do something for a "constructive debate" calls for a verb of encouragement, so "favoriser" (to promote) fits. "Empêcher" and "étouffer" work against a debate, and "réfuter" means to disprove.

units.title: Subjunctive Past
units.description: Le subjonctif passé — Past subjunctive after emotion, doubt, or judgment.

questions.prompt: Je suis content qu'il ___ (réussir) son examen.
questions.explanation: "Content que" expresses emotion and takes the subjunctive, and the success is already past, so the past subjunctive "ait réussi" is needed. It uses "ait" (subjunctive of avoir) to agree with "il", not "aie" or an indicative form.

questions.prompt: Il est possible qu'elle ___ (partir) avant notre arrivée.
questions.explanation: "Il est possible que" takes the subjunctive, and "partir" forms its past with être. The participle agrees with feminine "elle", giving "soit déjà partie".
questions.example: Il est possible qu'elle soit déjà partie.

questions.explanation: "Je doute que" requires the subjunctive, and the finishing precedes the doubt, so we use the past subjunctive. "Ils" needs the plural "aient fini", not singular "ait" or "aies".

questions.prompt: Il est dommage que tu ne ___ (pas venir) hier.
questions.explanation: "Il est dommage que" takes the subjunctive, and "venir" forms its past with être. With "tu" the subjunctive is "sois", so after "ne" we get "sois pas venu".

questions.prompt: Nous sommes surpris qu'elle ___ (accepter) cette offre.
questions.explanation: "Surpris que" expresses emotion and takes the subjunctive, and the acceptance is already past. "Accepter" uses avoir, so with "elle" we need "ait accepté", not "aies".

questions.prompt: Bien qu'il ___ (essayer), il n'a pas réussi.
questions.explanation: "Bien que" always takes the subjunctive, and the trying happened before the failure, so we use the past subjunctive "ait essayé". The participle does not agree because "essayer" takes avoir with no preceding object.

questions.prompt: Je regrette que vous ___ (ne pas pouvoir) venir.
questions.explanation: "Je regrette que" expresses emotion and takes the subjunctive, and the inability was in the past. With "vous" the subjunctive of avoir is "ayez", giving "n'ayez pas pu".
questions.meaning: that you could not, were not able to

questions.prompt: Il est étonnant qu'elles ___ (arriver) si tôt.
questions.explanation: After an expression of surprise ("Il est étonnant que") French uses the subjunctive, and the past form is "soient arrivées" because "arriver" takes être and agrees with feminine plural "elles".

questions.prompt: Je suis heureux que tu ___ (obtenir) ce poste.
questions.explanation: "Je suis heureux que" (emotion) takes the subjunctive, and the past form for "tu" is "aies obtenu": avoir in the subjunctive plus the participle.

questions.prompt: Il se peut qu'il ___ (oublier) son rendez-vous.
questions.explanation: "Il se peut que" expresses possibility and requires the subjunctive; the forgetting is already done, so the past subjunctive "ait oublié" (avoir, third person singular) is used.

questions.prompt: Nous sommes déçus qu'ils ___ (annuler) la réunion.
questions.explanation: "Nous sommes déçus que" (emotion) takes the subjunctive, and the cancelling came before, so the past subjunctive of "annuler" with avoir for "ils" is "aient annulé".

questions.prompt: C'est le meilleur film que j'___ (voir).
questions.explanation: A superlative ("le meilleur film que") triggers the subjunctive, and having already seen the film calls for the past form "aie vu"; the participle stays masculine "vu" because the object "film" is masculine.

questions.prompt: C'est la personne la plus gentille que je ___ (connaître).
questions.explanation: The superlative "la personne la plus gentille que" triggers the subjunctive, and since you still know this person, the present subjunctive "connaisse" is used, with the -e ending for "je".

questions.prompt: Je suis surpris qu'elle n'___ (rien dire).
questions.explanation: "Je suis surpris que" (emotion) takes the subjunctive, and the silence is past, so the past subjunctive for "elle" is "ait rien dit" with avoir, third person singular "ait".

questions.prompt: Il est possible que nous ___ (se tromper).
questions.explanation: "Il est possible que" takes the subjunctive; "se tromper" is reflexive so the past form uses être, "nous soyons trompés", with the participle agreeing with plural "nous".
questions.meaning: that we were mistaken, made a mistake

questions.prompt: Je suis désolé que tu ___ (perdre) ton travail.
questions.explanation: "Je suis désolé que" (emotion) takes the subjunctive, and the job was already lost, so the past subjunctive for "tu" is "aies perdu".

questions.prompt: Je suis surpris qu'il ___ (arriver) en retard hier.
questions.explanation: "Je suis surpris que" expresses an emotion and takes the subjunctive, and "arriver" uses être, so for masculine "il" and a past event the form is "soit arrivé".

questions.prompt: Je ne pense pas qu'elle ___ (mentir) hier.
questions.explanation: "Je ne pense pas que" (doubt) takes the subjunctive, and "hier" puts the lie in the past, so "mentir" (avoir) gives "ait menti" with an invariable participle.

questions.prompt: C'est dommage qu'ils ne ___ (pas venir) à la fête.
questions.explanation: "C'est dommage que" (regret) takes the subjunctive, and "venir" uses être, so the past form is "soient pas venus" (after the printed "ne"), with the participle agreeing with masculine plural "ils".

questions.prompt: Je suis ravi que vous ___ (réussir) votre projet.
questions.explanation: "ayez réussi" is the past subjunctive of réussir (avoir + participle), needed after the emotion "Je suis ravi que" for an action completed before now. "avez réussi" is indicative, and réussir takes avoir, not être.
questions.meaning: that you succeeded in, have succeeded in

questions.prompt: Il est possible que je me ___ (tromper) de date.
questions.explanation: "sois trompé" is right because se tromper is pronominal, so its past subjunctive uses être (je me sois trompé), and "Il est possible que" triggers the subjunctive. "aie trompé" wrongly uses avoir.
questions.meaning: that I was mistaken (used with me: que je me sois trompé, from se tromper)

questions.explanation: "ait guéri" is the past subjunctive (avoir + participle) after the emotion "contents que", and "elle" needs the third-person "ait". Guérir takes avoir here, so the participle does not agree (not "guérie").

questions.prompt: Il est peu probable qu'ils ___ (partir) sans nous prévenir.
questions.explanation: "soient partis" is correct because partir takes être and the plural subject "ils" makes the participle plural; "Il est peu probable que" requires the subjunctive. "aient partis" wrongly uses avoir.

questions.prompt: Je suis étonné que tu ___ (finir) si vite.
questions.explanation: "aies fini" is the past subjunctive for "tu" (aies + participle), required after the emotion "Je suis étonné que". "as fini" is indicative, and "aie"/"ait" do not match "tu".
"ait voyagé" is the past subjunctive after "Je suis fier que", with voyager taking avoir and the singular "il" needing "ait". "a voyagé" is indicative, and "soit voyagé" wrongly uses être.
questions.example: Je suis content qu'il ait voyagé seul.

units.title: Literary Tenses
units.description: Recognizing the passé simple — the past tense of literature and formal narration, rarely heard in everyday speech.

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il fut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il fut" is the passé simple of être, so it means "he was"; it is the literary equivalent of "il a été".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il eut" means…
questions.explanation: "Il eut" is the passé simple of avoir, so it means "he had"; it is the literary equivalent of "il a eu".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il fit" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il fit" is the passé simple of faire, so it means "he did/made"; don't confuse it with "il eut" (he had).

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il alla" means…
questions.explanation: "Il alla" is the passé simple of aller, so it means "he went"; it is the literary equivalent of "il est allé".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il vint" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il vint" is the passé simple of venir, so it means "he came"; "he became" would be "il devint".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il dit" means…
questions.explanation: "Il dit" is the passé simple of dire, so in a narrative it means "he said"; the same spelling is also the present tense "he says".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il vit" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il vit" is the passé simple of voir, so in a narrative it means "he saw"; the same spelling is also the present tense of vivre (he lives).

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il prit" means…
questions.explanation: "Il prit" is the passé simple of prendre, so it means "he took"; it is the literary equivalent of "il a pris".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il put" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il put" is the passé simple of pouvoir, so it means "he could" (he managed to); it is the literary equivalent of "il a pu".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il voulut" means…
questions.explanation: "Il voulut" is the passé simple of vouloir, so it means "he wanted"; it is the literary equivalent of "il a voulu".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il sut" means…
questions.explanation: "Il sut" is the passé simple of savoir, so it means "he knew" (often "he found out"); it is the literary equivalent of "il a su".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il crut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il crut" is the passé simple of croire, so it means "he believed"; "he knew/met" would be "il connut".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il naquit" means…
questions.explanation: "Il naquit" is the passé simple of naître (to be born), so it means "he was born"; the irregular stem naqu- makes it hard to recognise.

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il mourut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Mourut" is the passé simple of mourir (to die), so "il mourut" means "he died".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il devint" means…
questions.explanation: "Devint" is the passé simple of devenir (to become), so "il devint" means "he became".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il tint" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Tint" is the irregular passé simple of tenir (to hold), so "il tint" means "he held".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il écrivit" means…
questions.explanation: "Écrivit" is the passé simple of écrire (to write), so "il écrivit" means "he wrote".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il vécut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Vécut" is the irregular passé simple of vivre (to live), so "il vécut" means "he lived".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il partit" means…
questions.explanation: "Partit" is the passé simple of partir (to leave), so "il partit" means "he left".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il sortit" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Sortit" is the passé simple of sortir (to go out), so "il sortit" means "he went out".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il répondit" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Répondit" is the passé simple of répondre (to answer), so "il répondit" means "he answered".

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il perdit" means…
questions.explanation: "he lost": perdit is the passé simple of perdre (to lose); regular -re verbs like perdre end in -it in the il form, so il perdit means the same as il a perdu.

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il comprit" means… ___
questions.explanation: "he understood": comprit is the passé simple of comprendre, formed like prendre → il prit; in speech you would say il a compris.

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il reçut" means…
questions.explanation: "he received": reçut is the passé simple of recevoir, and its -ut ending echoes the past participle reçu (il a reçu).

questions.prompt: The passé simple form "il connut" means… ___
questions.explanation: "Il connut" is the passé simple of connaître, so it means "he knew/met"; as a one-off past event it usually means he met or got to know someone.

units.title: Philosophy & Abstract Concepts
units.description: Discussing abstract ideas — Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.

questions.explanation: truth → la vérité. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
knowledge → la connaissance. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
existence → l'existence. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
Consciousness (awareness of oneself) is "la conscience"; don't confuse it with la connaissance, which means knowledge.
reality → la réalité. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
ethics → l'éthique. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
Morality, the accepted rules of right and wrong, is "la morale"; l'éthique is the philosophical study of those rules.
freedom (philosophical) → la liberté. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
identity → l'identité. Vocabulary for philosophical and abstract discussion.
Meaning in the sense of significance is "le sens", as in le sens de la vie (the meaning of life); le concept means an idea, not a meaning.

"la raison" is reason, the faculty of thinking logically, as in « le siècle de la raison ». It is feminine, unlike « la morale » (morality) or « la perception » (perception), which name different ideas.
"la logique" is logic, the rules of valid reasoning; note the -ique ending for English -ic. Do not confuse it with « la raison » (reason, the faculty) or « la vérité » (truth).
"la croyance" is belief, something held to be true; it comes from the verb « croire » (to believe). It is not a cognate, so link it to « croire » to remember it.
"le doute" is the masculine noun from douter (to doubt), as in le doute cartésien, Descartes' method of doubting everything.
"la perception" is spelled exactly like the English word but is feminine, like most nouns ending in -tion. Do not confuse it with « la conscience » (consciousness, awareness).
"la sagesse" is wisdom; it comes from the adjective « sage » (wise). The other options mean argument, perception and reality.
"la vertu" is virtue, a moral quality; note the spelling with no final -e. Do not confuse it with « la sagesse » (wisdom) or « la connaissance » (knowledge).

questions.prompt: The French word for "justice (as a concept)" is…
questions.explanation: "la justice" is justice as an abstract idea, and it is feminine. The same word also means the justice system, as in « la justice française ».

questions.prompt: The French word for "the absolute" is… ___
questions.explanation: "l'absolu" is the adjective absolu used as a masculine noun for the absolute, as in la quête de l'absolu.

questions.prompt: The French word for "the relative" is…
questions.explanation: "le relatif" is the adjective relatif used as a masculine noun for the relative, the opposite of l'absolu.
"le paradoxe" is a paradox; note the -e ending and the masculine gender. « Le doute » means doubt and « le concept » means concept.
"le concept" is a concept, an abstract idea; it is spelled as in English and is masculine. « Le sens » means meaning or sense.
"l'argument" is an argument in the sense of a reason given to support a claim; it is masculine (« un argument »). A quarrel is « une dispute », not « un argument ».
"l'hypothèse" is a hypothesis; note the grave accent and the final -e. It is feminine: « une hypothèse ».
"la contradiction" is spelled exactly as in English and is feminine, like most nouns ending in -tion. It comes from « contredire » (to contradict).

units.title: Science & Technology, Advanced
units.description: Discussing research and innovation — Advanced science and technology vocabulary.

questions.prompt: The French word for "artificial intelligence" is… ___
questions.explanation: In "l'intelligence artificielle" the adjective follows the noun, and because "intelligence" is feminine, the adjective is spelled "artificielle".
algorithm → l'algorithme. Advanced science and technology vocabulary.
Research data is "les données", a feminine noun that comes from "donner" and is almost always used in the plural.
"la recherche" is the noun for research, as in "la recherche scientifique"; in everyday French it also means a search.
innovation → l'innovation. Advanced science and technology vocabulary.
A scientific experiment is "l'expérience"; the same word also means experience, so the context tells you which meaning is intended.
Hypothesis is "l'hypothèse", a feminine noun (une hypothèse) written with a grave accent on the è.
English "molecule" becomes "la molécule" in French: the word is feminine and takes an acute accent on the first e.
"le gène" is masculine and written with a grave accent; do not confuse it with la gêne, which means embarrassment.
"le laboratoire" is masculine, and the French spelling ends in -oire where English has -ory.
"la découverte" is the noun formed from the verb découvrir (to discover), so a scientific discovery is la découverte.
The field of robots is "la robotique", feminine like other -ique subject names such as l'informatique.
"quantique" is the adjective for "quantum", as in l'informatique quantique (quantum computing); numérique means digital and durable means sustainable.
"la biotechnologie" is the use of living organisms in technology; it is a feminine noun and, unlike English, takes an article.
"la nanotechnologie" is feminine, like most French nouns ending in -ie, and it needs the article la where English uses no article.
sustainability (economic) → la durabilité. Advanced science and technology vocabulary.

questions.prompt: The French word for "innovation hub" is…
questions.explanation: "le pôle d'innovation" uses pôle (centre, cluster) for English "hub": a place grouping companies, labs and universities.
"le brevet" is the legal document protecting an invention; to file a patent is déposer un brevet.
prototype → le prototype. Advanced science and technology vocabulary.
simulation → la simulation. Advanced science and technology vocabulary.
"l'automatisation" comes from the verb automatiser; note the French -isation ending where English says "automation".
"le chiffrement" comes from chiffrer (to encode) and is the standard French term for encryption; cryptage is common but less precise.

questions.prompt: The French word for "neural network" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le réseau de neurones" literally means "network of neurons": where English uses the adjective "neural", French uses réseau + de + a noun.
"la percée" literally means a breaking through, from percer, and is used figuratively for a scientific breakthrough, as in une percée médicale.
"l'évolutivité" is a system's ability to grow and handle more load; it comes from évoluer (to evolve), and the anglicism scalabilité is also heard.

units.title: Legal & Administrative French
units.description: Formal legal language — Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Le demandeur a déposé une ___ auprès du tribunal.
questions.explanation: "plainte" is correct because "déposer une plainte" is the set phrase for filing a formal complaint. A peine or sanction is imposed by a court, and an audience is held, not filed.
questions.example: La victime a déposé une plainte au commissariat.

questions.prompt: Le contrat entre en ___ dès sa signature.
questions.explanation: "vigueur" is correct because "entrer en vigueur" is the fixed phrase meaning to come into force. "rigueur" (strictness) looks similar but does not fit this expression.

questions.prompt: Il incombe à l'accusé de ___ son innocence.
questions.explanation: "prouver" is correct because "Il incombe à... de" means the burden lies on someone, and the burden here is to prove innocence. The look-alikes approuver, éprouver and réprouver mean approve, feel and condemn.
questions.example: Il incombe à l'accusation de prouver la culpabilité de l'accusé.

questions.prompt: Cette loi est en ___ depuis janvier.
questions.explanation: "vigueur" is correct because "être en vigueur" is the fixed phrase for a law being currently in force. "rigueur" (strictness) and "valeur" do not form this expression.

questions.prompt: Le tribunal a rendu son ___ hier.
questions.explanation: "jugement" is correct because a tribunal "rend" its ruling, as in "rendre un jugement". A procès is the trial itself, an appel is lodged by a party, and a serment is sworn.

questions.prompt: Les parties ont signé un ___ à l'amiable.
questions.explanation: "accord" is correct because "à l'amiable" means settled out of court, so the parties sign an agreement. A verdict, procès or appel belongs to court proceedings, not an amicable settlement.
A notary authenticates written papers, so "document" fits; a "litige" (dispute), a "délai" (time limit) and a "procès" (trial) cannot be authenticated.

questions.prompt: Il convient de respecter les ___ légales.
questions.explanation: You "respecter" legal "obligations" (duties imposed by law); "poursuites", "plaintes" and "peines" are things brought against or imposed on someone, not things you comply with.

questions.prompt: Le dossier a été soumis à l'___ du juge.
questions.explanation: "examen" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.
The subject "La procédure" is singular, so the verb is "dure" (not plural "durent"), and "durer" is the verb that takes a length of time like "plusieurs mois".

questions.prompt: Le prévenu a fait ___ de la décision.
questions.explanation: "appel" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Cette clause est ___ dans le contrat.
questions.explanation: The past participle agrees with the feminine singular subject "Cette clause", so it takes "-ée": "stipulée".

questions.prompt: Le ministère public a requis une ___ sévère.
questions.explanation: "peine" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Le tribunal administratif a statué en ___ instance.
questions.explanation: "première" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Les héritiers doivent régler les droits de ___.
questions.explanation: "succession" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.
"non-lieu" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.
questions.meaning: dismissal of a case, no grounds to prosecute

questions.prompt: Cette loi ___ les droits des consommateurs.
questions.explanation: The subject "Cette loi" is singular and needs a conjugated verb, so "protège" is right; "protéger" is an infinitive, "protégée" a participle and "protègent" plural.

questions.prompt: L'avocat a plaidé la ___ de son client.
questions.explanation: A lawyer argues his client's "défense" in court ("plaider"); a "plainte" is filed by a complainant, and a "peine" or "sentence" is handed down by the judge.
questions.example: L'avocat a assuré la défense de son client.

questions.prompt: Le contrat doit être ___ par les deux parties.
questions.explanation: After "être" in the passive, the participle agrees with the subject "Le contrat" (masculine singular), so "signé" is required, not the feminine, plural or infinitive form.

questions.prompt: La cour d'appel a annulé le ___ rendu en première instance.
questions.explanation: A court annuls a decision, and "jugement" is the only noun in the bank that names one; a witness, a clerk or a plaintiff is a person and cannot be annulled.

questions.prompt: Le fonctionnaire a délivré le ___ requis.
questions.explanation: An official "délivre" a document, and "certificat" is the only noun in the bank that is something issued; "litige", "témoin" and "plaignant" cannot be handed out.

questions.prompt: La demande a été ___ pour vice de forme.
questions.explanation: "rejetée" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Le litige a été réglé à l'___.
questions.explanation: "amiable" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.
questions.meaning: amicable; 'à l'amiable' means out of court

questions.prompt: Les témoins ont été ___ à comparaître.
questions.explanation: "convoqués" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.

questions.prompt: Le texte de loi a été ___ au parlement.
questions.explanation: "adopté" is correct here. Legal and administrative vocabulary in context.
questions.example: Le texte de loi a été adopté par le Parlement.

units.title: Diplomatic & Political Register
units.description: International relations vocabulary — Words for diplomacy, treaties and negotiation in a formal register.

questions.explanation: "le traité" is the French word for a treaty, a formal written agreement between states; it is masculine.
"la négociation" means negotiation, the process of discussing terms to reach an agreement; the noun is feminine.
"le sommet" is a summit, a high-level meeting between heads of state; it literally means "top" or "peak".
"l'ambassadeur" is the ambassador, the person who represents one country in another; the noun is masculine with an elided article.
"l'ambassade" is the embassy, the building and office of a country's mission abroad; the ambassador is "l'ambassadeur".
"l'alliance" is an alliance, a formal union between states acting together; the noun is feminine with an elided article.

questions.prompt: Which French word means "coercive measures imposed on a state"?
questions.explanation: "les sanctions" are coercive measures imposed on a state; the word is the same as in English and is usually plural.
"le cessez-le-feu" is built from the order cessez le feu (cease fire); it is masculine and stays the same in the plural.

questions.prompt: The French word for "diplomacy (in political discourse)" is…
questions.explanation: "la diplomatie" is the art and practice of conducting relations between states; "les relations diplomatiques" are the official ties between two countries, not diplomacy itself.
"la résolution" is the formal decision voted by an assembly such as the UN Security Council; it is feminine, like most nouns in -tion.
"la délégation" is the group of representatives a country sends to a negotiation or conference; an individual member is un délégué.

questions.prompt: The French word for "summit meeting" is…
questions.explanation: "la réunion au sommet" is a meeting of heads of state or government, often shortened to le sommet; "l'ambassade" is an embassy and "la médiation" is mediation.
