"bilatéral" describes something between exactly two parties, such as un accord bilatéral; "multilatéral" involves several and "unilatéral" only one.
"multilatéral" means involving several countries at once, as in une négociation multilatérale; "bilatéral" involves only two.
"l'accord" is a formal agreement between parties, as in un accord de paix; it is masculine, so the article elides before the vowel to l'.
"la médiation" is the intervention of a neutral third party to help two sides settle a conflict; the mediator is le médiateur.

questions.prompt: The French word for "sovereignty (in political discourse)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "la souveraineté" is a state's full authority over its own territory and affairs; note the spelling with -eraineté and the feminine article.

questions.prompt: The French word for "territorial integrity" is…
questions.explanation: "l'intégrité territoriale" is the principle that a state's borders must not be violated; in French the adjective territoriale follows the noun and agrees in the feminine.

questions.prompt: The French word for "international law" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le droit international" is the body of rules governing relations between states; in this sense le droit means 'law', not 'right'.

questions.prompt: The French word for "diplomatic relations" is…
questions.explanation: "les relations diplomatiques" are the official ties between two states, which they can establish or break off (rompre); the adjective follows the noun and agrees in the plural.

questions.prompt: Which French word means "general agreement reached without a formal vote or objection"?
questions.explanation: "le consensus" means general agreement reached without a formal vote or objection, while "l'accord" is a specific negotiated agreement between parties.

questions.prompt: Droit d'un membre permanent du Conseil de sécurité de bloquer seul une résolution : ___
questions.explanation: "le veto" is the right to block a decision on one's own; negotiation, diplomacy and mediation are ways to reach agreement, not to block it.
"l'envoyé" comes from the verb envoyer (to send) and means a person sent on a diplomatic mission, which is what "envoy" means.
"le protocole" is the set of formal rules of etiquette and procedure followed in diplomatic and official ceremonies; note the French spelling ends in -e.

questions.prompt: Déclaration officielle écrite remise à la presse :
questions.explanation: "le communiqué" is an official written statement released to the press; "le traité" is a written agreement between states, not a press release.

units.title: Rhetorical Devices & Style
units.description: Analyzing how texts are written — Vocabulary for literary and rhetorical analysis.

questions.prompt: Figure qui rapproche deux réalités sans outil de comparaison comme « comme » : ___
questions.explanation: "la métaphore" compares two things directly, with no linking word such as comme; a comparison that uses comme is a simile.
In French rhetoric a simile is called "la comparaison" because it compares with a linking word such as comme; without that word it becomes la métaphore.

questions.prompt: Figure qui consiste à dire le contraire de ce qu'on pense, souvent pour se moquer : ___
questions.explanation: "l'ironie" means saying the opposite of what you mean, often to mock; la litote, by contrast, says less in order to suggest more.

questions.prompt: Exagération volontaire de l'expression pour frapper l'esprit :
questions.explanation: "l'hyperbole" is deliberate exaggeration for effect, for example « je meurs de faim ».

questions.prompt: Figure qui atténue une réalité pénible ou choquante (ex. « il nous a quittés ») : ___
questions.explanation: "l'euphémisme" softens an unpleasant reality, as in « il nous a quittés » meaning « il est mort ».

questions.prompt: Répétition d'un même son consonantique dans des mots proches :
questions.explanation: "l'allitération" repeats a consonant sound, as in « Pour qui sont ces serpents qui sifflent sur vos têtes ? ».

questions.prompt: Question posée pour produire un effet, sans attendre de réponse : ___
questions.explanation: "la question rhétorique" is asked for effect, not to get an answer, for example « Qui pourrait nier cela ? ».

questions.prompt: Énoncé qui semble contradictoire mais exprime une vérité :
questions.explanation: "le paradoxe" is a statement that seems self-contradictory yet holds a truth, for example « Je sais que je ne sais rien ».
Giving human qualities to an object or idea is "la personnification" in French; note the double n, unlike English "personification".

questions.prompt: Placing two opposed ideas side by side, as in « Je vis, je meurs », is called…
questions.explanation: Setting two opposed ideas side by side is "l'antithèse" (feminine, with a grave accent), as in « Je vis, je meurs ».
"l'allégorie" is feminine (une allégorie): a story or image that stands for an abstract idea, like Plato's allégorie de la caverne.
"le ton" is masculine and means the tone of a text or a voice, as in un ton ironique; do not confuse it with le thon (tuna).

questions.prompt: The French word for "register (of speech)" is…
questions.explanation: "le registre" is the level of language a speaker or writer chooses (soutenu, courant, familier); note that the noun is masculine.
"le symbolisme" is the use of objects or images to stand for abstract ideas; like English "symbolism", it is masculine and ends in -isme.

questions.prompt: Using the same word or phrase again and again for effect is called…
questions.explanation: Using the same word or phrase again for effect is "la répétition"; note the two acute accents in the French spelling.
Saying less in order to suggest more, as in « Ce n'est pas mauvais » meaning "it's very good", is "la litote"; its opposite, exaggeration, is l'hyperbole.
"l'oxymore" (masculine) joins two contradictory words, as in Corneille's « cette obscure clarté ».
"l'analogie" (feminine) is a comparison between two things that share a relationship, used to explain or persuade.

questions.prompt: The French word for "imagery" (in a literary text) is…
questions.explanation: In literary analysis, a writer's imagery is usually called "les images", in the plural (for example, les images de la mer chez Hugo).
"le récit" is the narrative, the story of events as it is told; "la narration" refers rather to the act of telling it.

questions.prompt: The French word for "rhythm (of prose)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le rythme" is the flow of sentences created by their length and stresses; note the spelling with y and th, as in English.
emphasis → l'emphase. Vocabulary for literary and rhetorical analysis.

questions.prompt: Moving away from the main subject of a text or speech is called… ___
questions.explanation: Moving away from the main subject of a text or speech is "la digression", a feminine noun with the same spelling as in English.
A hint early in a story about what will happen later is called "l'annonce" in French narrative analysis (related terms: le présage, la prolepse for an actual flash-forward).

questions.prompt: The French word for "climax (of a story)" is… ___
questions.explanation: "le point culminant" is literally the highest point, the moment of greatest tension in a story.

units.title: Register Shifts
units.description: Familiar vs formal French — Everyday familiar register vs. its formal equivalent.

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bagnole" is…
questions.explanation: "Bagnole" is slang for a car, so its neutral, formal equivalent is "voiture".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bouffer" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Bouffer" is slang for eating, so the neutral verb is "manger" (not boire, which means to drink).

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "fric" is…
questions.explanation: "Fric" is slang for money, so its standard equivalent is "argent".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "mec" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Mec" is slang for a guy, a man, so the neutral equivalent is "homme".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bosser" is…
questions.explanation: "bosser" is everyday slang for working ("Je bosse demain"); the standard verb is "travailler".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "gosse" is… ___
questions.explanation: "gosse" is a familiar word for a kid; the standard word is "enfant".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bagarre" is…
questions.explanation: bagarre → dispute. Everyday familiar register vs. its formal equivalent.

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "flic" is… ___
questions.explanation: "flic" is slang for a police officer; the standard word is "policier".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bouquin" is…
questions.explanation: "bouquin" is a familiar word for a book; the standard word is "livre".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "piaule" is… ___
questions.explanation: "piaule" is slang for a room, especially the room where you sleep or live; the standard word is "chambre".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "taf" is… ___
questions.explanation: "taf" is slang for work or a job ("J'ai trouvé un taf"); the standard word is "travail".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "gars" is…
questions.explanation: "gars" is a familiar word for a guy or man; the standard word is "homme".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "truc" is… ___
questions.explanation: "truc" is a familiar word for 'thing', used when you don't name the object; the standard word is "chose".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "sympa" is…
questions.explanation: "sympa" is the familiar short form of 'nice' or 'pleasant'; in careful speech you say "agréable".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "nul" is… ___
questions.explanation: "nul" is a familiar way to call something useless or very bad; the more formal word is "médiocre".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "paumé" is…
questions.explanation: "paumé" is a familiar word for lost, whether you lost your way or feel confused; the standard word is "perdu".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "crevé" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Crevé" is familiar slang for completely worn out; in formal speech or writing you say "épuisé".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "chouette" is…
questions.explanation: "Chouette" is a familiar way to say something is great; the formal equivalent is "excellent".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar expression "foutre le camp" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Foutre le camp" is a crude, very familiar way to say "leave"; the neutral, formal verb is "partir".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "gueuler" is…
questions.explanation: "Gueuler" is familiar slang for shouting loudly; the standard, formal verb is "crier".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "rigoler" is…
questions.explanation: "Rigoler" is the everyday familiar verb for laughing; in formal French you use "rire".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "bête" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Bête" is the familiar way to call someone or something silly; the more formal adjective is "stupide".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "dingue" is…
questions.explanation: "Dingue" is familiar slang for crazy; the standard, more formal adjective is "fou".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "fauché" is… ___
questions.explanation: "Fauché" is familiar slang for having no money; a more formal way to say it is "sans le sou".

questions.prompt: The formal equivalent of the familiar word "la flemme" is…
questions.explanation: la flemme → le manque d'énergie. Everyday familiar register vs. its formal equivalent.

units.title: Advanced Collocations
units.description: Natural word combinations — Fixed verb-noun collocations common in formal French.

questions.explanation: Tenir compte de means "to take into account" (tenir compte de l'avis de chacun); do not confuse it with rendre compte de, which means to report on or account for.
Porter atteinte à means "to undermine/harm" something such as rights or a reputation, as in porter atteinte à la vie privée.
Faire face à means "to face up to" a difficulty, as in faire face à une crise.
Mettre en œuvre means "to implement", to put a plan or a measure into action, as in mettre en œuvre une réforme.
Prendre conscience de means "to become aware of" something, as in prendre conscience d'un problème.
"Tirer parti de" literally means to draw benefit from something, so it means "to take advantage of", as in tirer parti d'une situation.
"Donner lieu à" means to be the cause or occasion of something, so it means "to give rise to", as in cette décision a donné lieu à un débat.
"Avoir recours à" means turning to something as a means or last option, so it means "to resort to", as in avoir recours à la force.
"Faire preuve de" is followed by a quality, as in "faire preuve de courage", and means to display that quality, so it translates as "to demonstrate/show".
"Rendre compte de" means to report on or explain something, as in "rendre compte de ses actions", so the answer is "to account for"; with "se", "se rendre compte de" means to become aware of.
"Porter ses fruits" is used figuratively when efforts finally produce results, as in "nos efforts ont porté leurs fruits", just like English "to bear fruit".
"Jouer un rôle" works just like the English "to play a role": it means to have a part or a function in something, literally or figuratively.
"Susciter" means to arouse or provoke, and here what is aroused is "l'intérêt" (interest), so the phrase means "to spark interest".
"Soulever" literally means to lift up, so "soulever une question" means "to raise a question": to bring an issue up for discussion.
"Remettre en cause" means to challenge something that was taken for granted, which is "to call into question" in English.
"Mettre l'accent sur" literally means to put the stress on something, so it means "to emphasize" it.
"Prendre en compte" means to consider a factor when judging or deciding, which is "to take into account" in English.
"Faire l'objet de" means to be the object of a study, a measure or criticism, so it translates as "to be the subject of".
"Avoir tendance à" plus an infinitive describes a habitual inclination, just like the English "to tend to".
"Donner suite à" means to act on a request, a letter or a complaint, which is "to follow up on" in English.
French uses "tirer" (literally to pull) where English says draw, so "tirer des conclusions" means "to draw conclusions".
"Exercer" means to exert or exercise, so "exercer une influence" means "to exert an influence" on someone or something.
"Susciter" means to provoke or give rise to, so "susciter la controverse" means "to spark controversy".
"Faire figure de" means to appear as or pass for something, so it means "to be seen as": il fait figure de favori = he is seen as the favourite.
"Laisser entendre" means to let something be understood without saying it outright, so it means "to imply": il a laissé entendre qu'il partirait = he implied he would leave.

units.title: False Friends
units.description: Faux amis — Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "librairie" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: A librairie is a shop that sells books, hence "bookshop, not "library""; the place where you borrow books is a bibliothèque.

questions.prompt: The French word "attendre" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: Attendre means to wait (j'attends le bus), hence "to wait, not "to attend""; to attend an event is assister à.

questions.prompt: The French word "actuellement" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: Actuellement means at present (il travaille actuellement à Paris), hence "currently, not "actually""; 'actually' is en fait or en réalité.

questions.prompt: The French word "éventuellement" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: Éventuellement means if need be or possibly (je viendrai éventuellement), hence "possibly, not "eventually""; 'eventually' is finalement or à la longue.

questions.prompt: The French word "sensible" (a false friend) actually means…
choices: to insert, not just "to introduce" a person
questions.explanation: Sensible describes someone easily affected (elle est très sensible), hence "sensitive, not "sensible""; English 'sensible' is raisonnable or sensé.

questions.prompt: The French word "rester" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: Rester means to remain somewhere (je reste à la maison), hence "to stay, not "to rest""; to rest is se reposer.

questions.prompt: The French word "blesser" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: Blesser means to hurt or wound (il s'est blessé au genou), hence "to injure, not "to bless""; to bless is bénir.

questions.prompt: The French word "demander" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: Demander is a neutral request (je demande l'heure = I ask the time), hence "to ask, not "to demand""; to demand is exiger.

questions.prompt: The French word "assister à" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: Assister à means to be present at an event (j'assiste à un concert), hence "to attend, not "to assist""; to assist someone is aider.

questions.prompt: The French word "ignorer" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: Ignorer usually means not to be aware of something (j'ignore la réponse = I don't know the answer), hence "to not know, not "to ignore""; to ignore advice is ne pas tenir compte de.

questions.prompt: The French word "prétendre" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: prétendre → to claim, not "to pretend". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "introduire" (a false friend) actually means…
choices: to insert, not just "to introduce" a person
questions.explanation: introduire → to insert, not just "to introduce" a person. Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "large" (a false friend) actually means… ___
bank: to insert, not just "to introduce" a person
questions.explanation: large → wide, not "large" in general size. Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "journée" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: journée → day, not "journey". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "figure" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: figure → face, not "figure/number". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "monnaie" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: monnaie → change/currency, not "money" in general. Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "préservatif" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: préservatif → condom, not "preservative". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "crayon" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: French "crayon" is an ordinary pencil (un crayon de papier), so the answer is "pencil, not "crayon"". A wax crayon is "un crayon de cire".

questions.prompt: The French word "raisin" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: raisin → grape, not "raisin". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "coin" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: French "coin" is a corner (au coin de la rue), so the answer is "corner, not "coin"". A coin of money is "une pièce".

questions.prompt: The French word "location" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: French "location" means renting something (une location de voiture), so the answer is "rental, not "location/place"". A place is "un lieu" or "un endroit".

questions.prompt: The French word "formidable" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: formidable → great/wonderful, not "formidable". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "apologie" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: French "apologie" means defending or praising an idea (faire l'apologie de la violence), so the answer is "defense of an idea, not "apology"". An apology is "des excuses".

questions.prompt: The French word "déception" (a false friend) actually means… ___
questions.explanation: déception → disappointment, not "deception". Common French/English false friends.

questions.prompt: The French word "achever" (a false friend) actually means…
questions.explanation: French "achever" means bringing something to its end (achever un livre), so the answer is "to finish/complete, not "to achieve"". To achieve is "réaliser" or "accomplir".

units.title: Advanced Idioms III
units.description: Meaning match — More C1-level idioms.

questions.explanation: "mettre les voiles" is a sailing image (to hoist the sails and go), so it means "to leave abruptly", to clear off.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir du pain sur la planche" means…
choices: to have a lot of work to do
to have a clear field, free rein
questions.explanation: "avoir du pain sur la planche" literally means having bread on the board waiting to be worked, so it means "to have a lot of work to do".

questions.prompt: The idiom "être sur des charbons ardents" means… ___
questions.explanation: Sitting on burning coals is an image of restless, anxious waiting, so "être sur des charbons ardents" means "to be on tenterhooks".

choices: to put on the back burner
questions.explanation: A "pépin" is a fruit pip and, informally, a small hitch, so "avoir un pépin" means "to have a small problem".

bank: to have a lot of work to do
questions.explanation: Turning the page leaves a chapter behind you, so "tourner la page" means "to move on from something".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le compas dans l'œil" means…
choices: to struggle to make ends meet
to have a good eye for judging distances
questions.explanation: The image is an eye that measures like a pair of compasses, so "avoir le compas dans l'œil" means "to have a good eye for judging distances".

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre de l'eau dans son vin" means… ___
bank: to put on the back burner
questions.explanation: Adding water to wine makes it milder, so "mettre de l'eau dans son vin" means "to tone down one's demands" and compromise.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir des vues sur quelque chose" means…
questions.explanation: Here "vues" means aims or intentions, so "avoir des vues sur quelque chose" means "to have designs on something" you want to get.

questions.prompt: The idiom "tirer son épingle du jeu" means… ___
bank: to have a say in the matter
questions.explanation: Literally 'to pull your pin out of the game', "tirer son épingle du jeu" means "to come out ahead skillfully" from a tricky situation.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le champ libre" means…
choices: to have a clear field, free rein
questions.explanation: "avoir le champ libre" pictures an open field with nothing in the way, so it means "to have a clear field, free rein": no rival or obstacle stops you acting.

choices: to have a clear field, free rein
to put on the back burner
questions.explanation: "l'épreuve" is a trial or test, so "mettre à l'épreuve" means "to put to the test", as in mettre la patience de quelqu'un à l'épreuve.

questions.prompt: The idiom "jouer à pile ou face" means… ___
bank: to have a say in the matter
questions.explanation: "pile ou face" is heads or tails, so deciding by a coin toss means "to leave something to chance".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la main heureuse" means…
questions.explanation: Literally 'to have a happy hand', it means "to have a lucky touch": your choices or picks tend to turn out well.

questions.prompt: The idiom "mettre les pieds quelque part" means… ___
bank: to have a good business sense
to have a good eye for judging distances
to struggle to make ends meet
questions.explanation: Literally 'to put one's feet somewhere', it means "to set foot somewhere" and is often used in the negative: je n'y mettrai plus les pieds.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir voix au chapitre" means…
choices: to have a say in the matter
questions.explanation: The phrase comes from the voting voice of members of a monastery chapter, so "avoir voix au chapitre" means "to have a say in the matter".

questions.prompt: The idiom "tomber sous le sens" means… ___
questions.explanation: Something that 'falls under the senses' is plain for anyone to see, so "tomber sous le sens" means "to be obvious".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir le sens des affaires" means…
choices: to have a good business sense
to struggle to make ends meet
questions.explanation: "le sens des affaires" is a natural instinct for deals and money, so the phrase means "to have a good business sense".

bank: to put on the back burner
to have a clear field, free rein
questions.answer: to put on the back burner
questions.explanation: A "veilleuse" is a pilot light kept on low, so "mettre en veilleuse" a project means "to put on the back burner": it is put on hold for now.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir des hauts et des bas" means…
choices: to put on the back burner
questions.explanation: "Avoir des hauts et des bas" literally means having highs and lows, so it means "to have ups and downs", as in notre relation a des hauts et des bas.
"Tenir le coup" means withstanding a blow or a hard situation without giving in, so it means "to hold on, cope", as in malgré la fatigue, elle tient le coup.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir la tête froide" means… ___
bank: to have a say in the matter
questions.explanation: "Avoir la tête froide" (more often garder la tête froide) means staying calm and level-headed, so it means "to keep a cool head".

choices: to have a lot of work to do
questions.explanation: Literally 'to put on guard', "mettre en garde" means "to warn" someone about a risk, as in mettre quelqu'un en garde contre un danger.

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir un a priori" means… ___
bank: to have a good eye for judging distances
questions.explanation: "un a priori" (from Latin) is an opinion formed before knowing the facts, so "avoir un a priori" means "to have a preconception".

questions.prompt: The idiom "tirer le diable par la queue" means…
choices: to struggle to make ends meet
to have a good business sense
questions.explanation: "Tirer le diable par la queue" describes someone who barely gets by on very little money, so it means "to struggle to make ends meet".

questions.prompt: The idiom "avoir pignon sur rue" means… ___
bank: to have a lot of work to do
questions.explanation: "Avoir pignon sur rue" comes from owning a house whose gable faces the street, a sign of a solid trade, so it means "to be well-established (a business)".

units.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions
units.description: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics — Nuances of devoir, pouvoir, and other modal verbs.

lessons.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions 1
lessons.subtitle: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics

questions.prompt: Il ___ (devoir) être malade, il n'est pas venu.
questions.explanation: Here "devoir" expresses a probable guess (he must be ill, since he didn't come), and it agrees with "Il" as "doit"; "dois" is for je/tu and "dû" is only a participle.
"Devoir" expresses a probable estimate (she is probably about thirty), and with the third-person singular subject "Elle" the form is "doit".

questions.prompt: Tu ___ (devoir) partir maintenant, sinon tu seras en retard.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tu" takes "dois", and "devoir" here expresses obligation (you must leave now or you'll be late); "devez" would go with vous.
questions.meaning: must, have to (je/tu form: I/you must)

questions.explanation: The impersonal subject "Il" takes the third-person singular "peut", and "pouvoir" here expresses possibility (it may rain later).

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (pouvoir) très bien réussir si elle essaie.
questions.explanation: The subject "Elle" takes the third-person singular "peut", and "pouvoir très bien" expresses a real possibility (she may well succeed).

lessons.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions 2
lessons.subtitle: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics

questions.explanation: The subject "Ça" is third person singular, so pouvoir takes "peut"; the sense is 'it can wait until tomorrow'.
questions.meaning: can, is able to (it can wait)

questions.explanation: After "aurait" the verb needs the past participle of devoir, which is "dû" with a circumflex (without it, "du" means 'of the'); it expresses a reproach: he should have warned us.
The conditional perfect "n'aurais pas ..." requires the past participle "dû" (with the accent), meaning 'you should not have done that'.
The impersonal expression "il se peut que" ('it may be that') is always third person singular, so the verb is "peut"; it is followed by the subjunctive "ait".
With the subject "Elle" devoir takes the third person singular "doit", and "sûrement" shows it expresses probable inference: 'she must surely know already'.

lessons.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions 3
lessons.subtitle: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics

questions.explanation: "devez" is correct here. Nuances of devoir, pouvoir, and other modal verbs.
The subject "Il" is third person singular, so pouvoir takes "peut"; "ne ... pas avoir menti" then expresses impossibility: 'he cannot have lied'.
The subject "Elle" is third person singular, so devoir takes "doit"; "dois", "devons" and "doivent" belong to other subjects.
"devons" is correct here. Nuances of devoir, pouvoir, and other modal verbs.

questions.prompt: Cela ___ (pouvoir) sembler étrange, mais c'est vrai.
questions.explanation: The subject "Cela" is third person singular, so pouvoir takes "peut", meaning 'that may seem strange'.

lessons.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions 4
lessons.subtitle: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics

questions.explanation: Falloir is impersonal and used only with "il"; the present indicative is "faut", followed by "que" plus the subjunctive "vienne".

questions.prompt: Il se ___ (pouvoir) bien qu'il ait oublié.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression "il se peut que" ('it may be that') is always third person singular, so the verb is "peut", followed by the subjunctive "ait".
questions.meaning: it is possible, it may be (that)

questions.explanation: The subject is "Tu", so devoir takes the second-person singular present form "dois"; here it expresses a supposition, 'you must be mistaken'.
After "aurait" the verb needs a past participle, and the participle of pouvoir is "pu" with no accent, so 'n'aurait pas pu' means 'could not have'.
With the subject "Il", devoir takes the third-person singular form "doit"; it expresses a supposition, 'he must have his reasons'.

lessons.title: Nuanced Modal Expressions 5
lessons.subtitle: Devoir and pouvoir beyond the basics

questions.explanation: The subject is "Nous", so pouvoir takes the first-person plural ending "pouvons", giving 'we can always try'.
After "n'aurait pas" a past participle is needed, and the meaning 'should not have happened' calls for devoir's participle "dû" (with circumflex), not "pu".

questions.prompt: Il ___ (devoir) être fatigué après ce voyage.
questions.explanation: A conjugated verb is needed for the subject "Il", so devoir takes the form "doit", meaning 'must be' as a supposition: 'he must be tired after this trip'.
The subject "Elle" is third-person singular, so pouvoir takes "peut"; it expresses possibility, 'she may be right, after all'.

questions.prompt: Vous n'auriez pas ___ (devoir) partir sans prévenir.
questions.explanation: The conditional perfect "n'auriez pas ..." needs a past participle, and 'you should not have left without warning' uses devoir's participle "dû".

units.title: Etymology & Word Formation
units.description: Prefixes and suffixes — Common French prefixes and suffixes and what they signal.

bank: forms an abstract noun of quality
questions.explanation: The prefix "re-" means "again, back": refaire is to do again and revenir is to come back.
"dé-/dés-" signals "reversal, removal": défaire is to undo and désarmer is to disarm.

bank: forms a noun of action or result
questions.explanation: "in-/im-" means "not, opposite of": inutile is not useful and impossible is not possible.
"anti-" means "against": un antivol works against theft and un antibiotique fights bacteria.

bank: forms a noun for a person who does something
questions.explanation: "pré-" means "before": la préhistoire comes before written history, and prévoir is to see beforehand.
"post-" means "after": un post-scriptum is written after the letter, and postdater is to give a later date.
"sur-" means "over, above": survoler is to fly over and surpasser is to surpass.

choices: forms an abstract noun of quality
questions.explanation: "sous-" means "under, below": un sous-sol is a basement and un sous-marin is a submarine.
"co-" means "together, jointly": coopérer is to work together and un copropriétaire is a joint owner.
"inter-" means "between", as in "international" (between nations) or "interurbain" (between cities).
"trans-" means "across", as in "transatlantique" (across the Atlantic) or "transporter" (to carry across).
"auto-" means "self", as in "autobiographie" (a life written by oneself) or "autonome" (self-governing).
"bi-" means "two", as in "bilingue" (speaking two languages) or "bicyclette" (two wheels).
"mono-" means "one, single", as in "monologue" (one person speaking) or "monotone" (a single tone).
"multi-" means "many", as in "multicolore" (many colours) or "multinational" (involving many nations).
"extra-" means "beyond, extremely", as in "extraordinaire" (beyond the ordinary) or "extra-fin" (extremely fine).

choices: forms a noun of action or result
forms a noun for a person who does something
questions.explanation: "-tion" turns a verb into a noun, so it "forms a noun of action or result": "former" → "formation", "créer" → "création".

bank: forms an adverb, or a noun of action
forms a noun for a person who does something
questions.answer: forms an adverb, or a noun of action
questions.explanation: "-ment" "forms an adverb, or a noun of action": added to an adjective it gives an adverb ("lent" → "lentement"), and added to a verb stem it gives a noun ("changer" → "changement").

choices: forms a noun for a person who does something
forms a noun of action or result
forms an adverb, or a noun of action
questions.explanation: "-eur/-euse" "forms a noun for a person who does something": "vendre" → "vendeur/vendeuse", "danser" → "danseur/danseuse".

bank: forms an adverb, or a noun of action
forms a noun for a person who does something
forms a noun of action or result
questions.explanation: "-able/-ible" means "capable of being" done: "lisible" means it can be read, "faisable" means it can be done.

bank: forms a noun for a person who does something
forms an adverb, or a noun of action
questions.explanation: "-ique" means "relating to, forming an adjective": "histoire" → "historique" (relating to history), "économie" → "économique".

choices: forms an abstract noun of quality
forms a noun of action or result
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ité" "forms an abstract noun of quality" from an adjective, e.g. "rapide" → "rapidité", "réel" → "réalité".

bank: forms a noun of action or result
forms an abstract noun of quality
questions.explanation: "-if/-ive" "forms an adjective", often of tendency or function, e.g. "créer" → "créatif/créative", "sport" → "sportif/sportive".

choices: forms a noun for a person who does something
forms an abstract noun of quality
questions.explanation: "-iser" "forms a verb meaning "to make"", i.e. to make something have a quality, e.g. "moderne" → "moderniser", "central" → "centraliser".

bank: forms a noun of action or result
questions.answer: forms a noun of action or result
questions.explanation: "-age" "forms a noun of action or result" from a verb, e.g. "laver" → "lavage", "nettoyer" → "nettoyage".

units.title: Academic Writing Phrases
units.description: Structuring an academic essay — Set phrases for academic essays and structured argument.

questions.prompt: Cet essai a pour ___ d'examiner ce phénomène.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase "avoir pour objectif de" means 'to aim to', which fits an essay stating that it sets out to examine a phenomenon: "objectif".

questions.prompt: Il convient tout d'abord de ___ le contexte.
questions.explanation: "Situer le contexte" means 'to place the topic in its context', the usual opening move of an essay; the other verbs do not collocate with "contexte" here: "situer".

questions.prompt: Dans un premier temps, nous allons ___ les causes.
questions.explanation: 'Dans un premier temps' introduces the first step of a study, and examining "les causes" is done by "analyser"; 'combler' (fill) or 'corroborer' (back up) do not fit.

questions.prompt: Cette étude s'appuie sur des ___ empiriques.
questions.explanation: A study 'relies on' (s'appuie sur) evidence, and "données empiriques" is the standard collocation for 'empirical data': "données".

questions.prompt: Il est important de ___ ces résultats avec prudence.
questions.explanation: "interpréter" (to interpret) is what you do with results "avec prudence", because they can be read in more than one way. "Parvenir" and "aboutir" need "à" and take no direct object, and "combler" means to fill a gap.

questions.prompt: Nous nous proposons d'___ cette question sous un nouvel angle.
questions.explanation: "aborder" is the usual verb for approaching a question from a new angle, so "aborder cette question sous un nouvel angle" fits; "aboutir" takes no direct object, and "éluder" (avoid) and "exclure" (exclude) clash with "sous un nouvel angle".

questions.prompt: En ___, cette analyse montre que le phénomène est plus complexe qu'il n'y paraît.
questions.explanation: "conclusion" completes the set phrase "En conclusion,", which introduces the final point of an argument; an infinitive, a past participle or an adjective cannot follow "En" here.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ que ces résultats restent limités.
questions.explanation: "noter" completes the fixed formula "Il convient de noter que" (it should be noted that), used to draw attention to a point such as limited results.

questions.prompt: Cette recherche vise à ___ un vide dans la littérature.
questions.explanation: "combler" collocates with "un vide" (fill a gap), the standard way to say research fills a gap in the literature; "vérifier" or "corroborer" do not take "vide".
"révèlent" takes a direct object and means the data show or reveal a trend; the other verbs ("entrent", "contribuent", "s'inscrivent") need a preposition and cannot take "une tendance".

questions.prompt: Il est essentiel de ___ ces variables séparément.
questions.explanation: "considérer" takes a direct object and means to examine something, so "considérer ces variables séparément" fits; "contribuer" and "entrer" take no direct object, and "ressortir" (to take out again) makes no sense here.
"vérifier" fits "reste à ___ empiriquement": a hypothesis is something you verify by testing; the other options are intransitive and cannot take "cette hypothèse".

questions.prompt: Le présent travail s'inscrit dans la ___ de recherches antérieures.
questions.explanation: "continuité" forms the set phrase "s'inscrire dans la continuité de" (to follow on from earlier work); "méthode", "conclusion" and "preuve" are also feminine but do not form this phrase.

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ les limites de cette étude.
questions.explanation: "souligner" takes a direct object and means to highlight, so "Il convient de souligner les limites de cette étude" is the standard academic formula; the other verbs are intransitive.

questions.prompt: Ces résultats ___ largement les travaux existants.
questions.explanation: "corroborent" takes a direct object and means to confirm or support, so results "corroborent les travaux existants"; the other verbs need a preposition ("contribuent à", "s'inscrivent dans", "consistent en").

questions.prompt: Nous allons à présent ___ les implications pratiques.
questions.explanation: "examiner" (to examine) takes a direct object, so "examiner les implications pratiques" announces the next step of the analysis. "Parvenir" would need "à", "consister" needs "en" or "à", and "replacer" would need a phrase like "dans leur contexte".
questions.meaning: to examine, to look closely at

questions.prompt: Cette section a pour but de ___ le cadre théorique.
questions.explanation: "présenter" takes a direct object and means to set out, so "présenter le cadre théorique" describes what a section does; "contribuer", "consister" and "ressortir" cannot take a direct object.

questions.prompt: Il ressort de cette analyse que plusieurs facteurs ___ en jeu.
questions.explanation: "entrent" agrees with the plural subject "plusieurs facteurs" in the idiom "entrer en jeu" (to come into play); "mettre en jeu" would need a direct object, which this sentence lacks.
questions.meaning: they enter (entrer en jeu: to come into play)

questions.prompt: Ces travaux ont grandement ___ à notre compréhension du sujet.
questions.explanation: The verb "contribué" is the one that takes the preposition "à" (contribuer à = to contribute to); "apporter" and "enrichir" take a direct object instead.

questions.prompt: En définitive, cette étude ___ que d'autres recherches sont nécessaires.
questions.explanation: "suggère" takes a "que" clause and means the study points toward a conclusion; "contribue", "consiste" and "ressort" do not fit before "que d'autres recherches sont nécessaires".

questions.prompt: Il convient de ___ ces résultats à un échantillon plus large.
questions.explanation: "généraliser" takes a direct object plus "à" (généraliser ces résultats à un échantillon plus large = extend results to a wider sample); the other verbs cannot take "ces résultats" as object.
questions.meaning: to generalize, to extend more widely
questions.example: Il convient de rester prudent avant de généraliser ces résultats à l'ensemble de la population.

questions.prompt: Cette méthode présente plusieurs ___ par rapport aux approches précédentes.
questions.explanation: "plusieurs" requires a plural noun, so "avantages" fits; "avantage", "atout" and "intérêt" are singular.

questions.prompt: Les résultats obtenus nous ___ dans notre hypothèse de départ. (confirm)
questions.explanation: The subject "Les résultats" is plural and third person, so the verb takes the ending "confirment"; "confirme", "confirmons" and "confirmez" match other subjects.
questions.example: Les résultats obtenus confirment notre hypothèse de départ.

questions.prompt: Il est nécessaire de ___ ces conclusions dans un contexte plus large. (put back)
questions.explanation: "replacer" is correct here. Set phrases for academic essays and structured argument.
questions.meaning: to put back, to set in context

questions.prompt: Pour conclure, cette étude ___ un éclairage nouveau sur la question.
questions.explanation: The singular subject "cette étude" needs a present-tense third-person singular verb, so "apporte"; "apportent" is plural, and "apporter" and "apporté" are not finite forms.

units.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions
units.description: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de — Aspectual expressions for ongoing, just-finished, and about-to-happen actions.

lessons.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions 1
lessons.subtitle: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de

questions.prompt: Je ___ (être) en train de préparer le dîner.
questions.explanation: The subject "Je" takes "suis" in the construction "être en train de" (to be in the middle of doing).
"venir de" + infinitive means 'has just done'; with "Il" the verb is "vient".

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (être) sur le point de commencer.
questions.explanation: "sommes" is correct here. Aspectual expressions for ongoing, just-finished, and about-to-happen actions.
In "être en train de" (to be in the middle of doing), the subject "Elle" takes "est".
questions.meaning: is (in the middle of doing something)

questions.explanation: "venir de" + infinitive means 'have just done'; the plural subject "Ils" takes "viennent".

lessons.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions 2
lessons.subtitle: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de

questions.prompt: Tu ___ (être) sur le point de comprendre.
questions.explanation: "es" is the 'tu' form of être, which goes with 'tu' in the expression 'être sur le point de' (to be about to). 'Sommes', 'sont' and 'suis' belong to other subjects.
'Venir de' + infinitive means 'to have just done', and with 'je' venir becomes "viens". The other forms belong to different subjects.

questions.prompt: Elle ___ (être) en train de se préparer.
questions.explanation: 'Être en train de' (to be in the middle of doing something) needs être conjugated for 'elle', which is "est".
questions.meaning: is (in the middle of doing something)

questions.explanation: 'Venir de' + infinitive means 'to have just done', and with 'nous' venir becomes "venons".

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (être) sur le point de partir ?
questions.explanation: "êtes" is correct here. Aspectual expressions for ongoing, just-finished, and about-to-happen actions.

lessons.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions 3
lessons.subtitle: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de

questions.explanation: 'Être en train de' (to be in the middle of doing something) needs être conjugated for 'il', which is "est".
questions.meaning: is (in the middle of doing something)

questions.explanation: 'Venir de' + infinitive means 'to have just done', and with 'elles' (plural) venir becomes "viennent".

questions.prompt: Je ___ (être) sur le point de m'endormir.
questions.explanation: 'Être sur le point de' (to be about to) needs être conjugated for 'je', which is "suis".
'Venir de' + infinitive means 'to have just done', and with 'tu' venir becomes "viens".
'Être en train de' (to be in the middle of doing something) needs être conjugated for 'nous', which is "sommes".

lessons.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions 4
lessons.subtitle: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de

questions.prompt: Il ___ (être) sur le point de pleuvoir.
questions.explanation: The impersonal subject 'il' takes the third-person singular of être, "est", in 'être sur le point de' (to be about to).
questions.example: Le train est sur le point de partir.

questions.explanation: 'Venir de' + infinitive means 'to have just done', and with 'elle' venir becomes "vient".
The subject "Ils" is third-person plural, so "être" must be "sont" in the progressive "en train de" + infinitive ("are in the middle of eating").
questions.meaning: are (in the middle of doing something)

questions.prompt: Vous ___ (venir) de manquer une bonne occasion.
questions.explanation: With the subject "Vous", "venir" is conjugated "venez" in "venir de" + infinitive, which says the action has just happened ("you have just missed").

questions.prompt: Je ___ (être) en train d'apprendre le français.
questions.explanation: The subject "Je" takes "suis" in the ongoing-action structure "être en train de" + infinitive ("I am in the process of learning").

lessons.title: Nuanced Time & Aspect Expressions 5
lessons.subtitle: Être en train de, venir de, être sur le point de

questions.prompt: Nous ___ (être) sur le point de signer le contrat.
questions.explanation: The subject "Nous" takes "sommes" in "être sur le point de" + infinitive, which means "to be about to" do something ("we are about to sign").
The singular subject "Elle" takes "vient" in "venir de" + infinitive, which expresses a just-completed action ("she has just received").

questions.prompt: Il ___ (être) en train de travailler dur.
questions.explanation: The singular subject "Il" takes "est" in "être en train de" + infinitive, which describes an action in progress ("he is hard at work").

questions.prompt: Tu ___ (être) sur le point de réussir.
questions.explanation: The subject "Tu" takes "es" in "être sur le point de" + infinitive, which means you are on the verge of succeeding ("you are about to succeed").
The plural subject "Ils" takes "viennent" in "venir de" + infinitive, which says something has just happened ("they have just won the match").

units.title: Say It Your Way
units.description: Write the idea in French — Sophisticated and abstract ideas, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Argue that the reform is long overdue.
acceptableAnswers: Cette réforme est attendue depuis longtemps.
Il est grand temps que cette réforme voie le jour.
Cette réforme aurait dû être mise en œuvre depuis longtemps.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cette réforme est attendue depuis longtemps." "Depuis longtemps" with the present tense says it has been awaited for ages, while "Il est grand temps que… voie le jour" (subjunctive) says more forcefully that it is overdue.

questions.prompt: Express a nuanced position on a controversial topic.
acceptableAnswers: Ma position sur ce sujet est nuancée.
Je ne me range entièrement dans aucun des deux camps.
Ce sujet mérite une réflexion plus nuancée qu'un simple pour ou contre.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ma position sur ce sujet est nuancée." The adjective "nuancée" states a balanced view directly, and "Je ne me range entièrement dans aucun des deux camps" is another natural way to refuse to take sides.

questions.prompt: Say the findings warrant further investigation.
acceptableAnswers: Ces résultats méritent une enquête plus approfondie.
Il conviendrait d'approfondir ces recherches.
Ces conclusions appellent des investigations supplémentaires.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ces résultats méritent une enquête plus approfondie." Here mériter renders "warrant" and plus approfondie renders "further".

questions.prompt: Concede that the critics have a valid point.
acceptableAnswers: Il faut reconnaître que les critiques ne sont pas infondées.
Les détracteurs avancent un argument valable, je l'admets.
On ne peut pas balayer cette critique d'un revers de main.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Il faut reconnaître que les critiques ne sont pas infondées." Il faut reconnaître que signals the concession, and the litotes ne sont pas infondées means the critics have a point.

questions.prompt: Say the argument, while persuasive, overlooks key evidence.
acceptableAnswers: Cet argument, bien que convaincant, néglige des preuves essentielles.
Malgré sa force persuasive, cet argument omet des éléments cruciaux.
Convaincant en apparence, cet argument passe sous silence des faits déterminants.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cet argument, bien que convaincant, néglige des preuves essentielles." Bien que + adjective renders "while persuasive", and néglige renders "overlooks".

questions.prompt: Express reservations about a proposal without rejecting it outright.
acceptableAnswers: J'ai quelques réserves sur cette proposition.
Je ne rejette pas cette proposition, mais elle appelle des nuances.
Cette proposition mérite d'être examinée avec prudence.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "J'ai quelques réserves sur cette proposition." Avoir des réserves sur expresses doubts, and quelques softens them so the proposal is not rejected outright.

questions.prompt: Say the policy's long-term consequences remain uncertain.
acceptableAnswers: Les conséquences à long terme de cette politique restent incertaines.
On ignore encore les effets durables de cette mesure.
L'impact à long terme de cette politique demeure difficile à évaluer.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Les conséquences à long terme de cette politique restent incertaines." "Rester" (or "demeurer") translates "remain", and "incertaines" agrees with the feminine plural "conséquences".

questions.prompt: Articulate why consensus has proven elusive.
acceptableAnswers: Le consensus s'est révélé difficile à atteindre pour plusieurs raisons.
Divers facteurs expliquent l'absence de consensus.
Un accord général peine à se dégager, et ce, pour de bonnes raisons.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Le consensus s'est révélé difficile à atteindre pour plusieurs raisons." The verb "s'est révélé" renders 'has proven', and "difficile à atteindre" renders 'elusive'.

questions.prompt: Say the precedent set by this case is troubling.
acceptableAnswers: Le précédent créé par cette affaire est préoccupant.
Cette affaire établit un précédent inquiétant.
Le précédent qui en découle soulève de sérieuses inquiétudes.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Le précédent créé par cette affaire est préoccupant." A legal case is "une affaire", and "set a precedent" becomes "créer" or "établir un précédent".

questions.prompt: Suggest the debate has become needlessly polarized.
acceptableAnswers: Ce débat s'est polarisé de manière excessive.
La polarisation de ce débat me semble inutile.
Ce débat, à mon sens, s'est inutilement radicalisé.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ce débat s'est polarisé de manière excessive." Sophisticated and abstract ideas, and more than one wording is right.

questions.prompt: Say the data, though limited, points to a clear trend.
acceptableAnswers: Les données, bien que limitées, révèlent une tendance nette.
Malgré leur nombre restreint, les données indiquent une tendance claire.
Ces données, quoique partielles, dessinent une tendance évidente.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Les données, bien que limitées, révèlent une tendance nette." "Bien que" or "quoique" plus an adjective renders "though limited", and "données" is feminine plural, so the adjective is "limitées".

questions.prompt: Express that a compromise would satisfy no one.
acceptableAnswers: Un compromis ne satisferait personne dans ce cas.
Aucun compromis ne conviendrait vraiment ici.
Dans cette affaire, tout compromis laisserait les deux parties insatisfaites.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Un compromis ne satisferait personne dans ce cas." The conditional "satisferait" with "ne… personne" gives 'would satisfy no one'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say the institution has lost public trust.
acceptableAnswers: L'institution a perdu la confiance du public.
Le public ne fait plus confiance à cette institution.
Cette institution a vu sa crédibilité s'effriter aux yeux du public.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "L'institution a perdu la confiance du public." "Public trust" is "la confiance du public", and you can also turn it around with "ne fait plus confiance à".

questions.prompt: Argue for a more measured response.
acceptableAnswers: Je plaide pour une réponse plus mesurée.
Une réaction plus modérée serait préférable.
Il conviendrait d'adopter une approche plus mesurée.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je plaide pour une réponse plus mesurée." "Plaider pour" means "argue for", and the impersonal "il conviendrait de" makes the same point more formally.

questions.prompt: Say the proposal, however well-intentioned, is impractical.
acceptableAnswers: Cette proposition, bien qu'animée de bonnes intentions, est irréalisable.
Malgré de bonnes intentions, cette proposition reste peu pratique.
Aussi bien intentionnée soit-elle, cette proposition n'est guère applicable.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cette proposition, bien qu'animée de bonnes intentions, est irréalisable." "Bien que" carries the concession 'however well-intentioned' and "irréalisable" means 'impractical'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Express that the burden of proof lies elsewhere.
acceptableAnswers: La charge de la preuve incombe à l'autre partie.
Ce n'est pas à nous de prouver cela.
C'est à l'autre camp qu'il revient d'apporter la preuve.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "La charge de la preuve incombe à l'autre partie." "La charge de la preuve" is the fixed term for 'burden of proof', and "incomber à" means 'to lie with'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say the committee's recommendations were largely symbolic.
acceptableAnswers: Les recommandations du comité étaient surtout symboliques.
Le comité a formulé des recommandations essentiellement symboliques.
Ces recommandations relèvent davantage du symbole que de l'action concrète.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Les recommandations du comité étaient surtout symboliques." "Surtout" (or "essentiellement") renders 'largely'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Argue that correlation should not be mistaken for causation.
acceptableAnswers: Il ne faut pas confondre corrélation et causalité.
Une corrélation n'implique pas nécessairement une causalité.
Ce lien statistique ne prouve en rien une relation de cause à effet.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Il ne faut pas confondre corrélation et causalité." "Confondre A et B" expresses 'mistake A for B'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say the reform risks unintended consequences.
acceptableAnswers: Cette réforme risque d'entraîner des conséquences imprévues.
Il faut craindre des effets secondaires imprévus.
Cette réforme pourrait bien produire des effets contraires à ceux escomptés.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Cette réforme risque d'entraîner des conséquences imprévues." "Risquer de" + infinitive expresses 'risks', and "imprévues" means 'unintended'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Express that the evidence, on balance, supports the hypothesis.
acceptableAnswers: Dans l'ensemble, les preuves confirment cette hypothèse.
Les éléments recueillis, pris dans leur ensemble, étayent cette hypothèse.
Globalement, les faits vont dans le sens de cette hypothèse.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Dans l'ensemble, les preuves confirment cette hypothèse." "Dans l'ensemble" renders 'on balance'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say the debate ultimately hinges on differing values.
acceptableAnswers: Ce débat repose en définitive sur des valeurs divergentes.
Au fond, ce désaccord relève de valeurs différentes.
Ce sont des valeurs opposées qui sous-tendent ce débat.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Ce débat repose en définitive sur des valeurs divergentes." "Reposer sur" renders 'hinges on' and "en définitive" means 'ultimately'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Argue that transparency should take precedence over efficiency.
acceptableAnswers: La transparence devrait primer sur l'efficacité.
Je considère que la transparence doit l'emporter sur l'efficacité.
Mieux vaut privilégier la transparence, quitte à perdre en efficacité.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "La transparence devrait primer sur l'efficacité." "Primer sur" (or "l'emporter sur") means 'take precedence over'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say the assumption underlying the model is flawed.
acceptableAnswers: L'hypothèse sur laquelle repose ce modèle est erronée.
Ce modèle part d'un postulat discutable.
Le modèle repose sur une prémisse qui ne tient pas la route.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "L'hypothèse sur laquelle repose ce modèle est erronée." "Sur laquelle repose" renders 'underlying' and "erronée" means 'flawed'; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Express cautious support for an untested idea.
acceptableAnswers: Je soutiens cette idée, mais avec prudence.
Cette idée mérite d'être essayée, sous certaines réserves.
Je suis plutôt favorable, tout en restant prudent.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "Je soutiens cette idée, mais avec prudence." "Mais avec prudence" adds the caution to your support; other wordings are also accepted.

questions.prompt: Say history will be the ultimate judge.
acceptableAnswers: L'histoire jugera en dernier ressort.
Seule l'histoire pourra en juger.
C'est à l'histoire qu'il reviendra de trancher.
questions.explanation: One way to say it: "L'histoire jugera en dernier ressort." "En dernier ressort" means 'ultimately, as the final authority', so history is the ultimate judge; other wordings are also accepted.

units.title: Speaking: Idiomatic and Formal Phrasing
units.description: Say it out loud — Practise idiomatic and formal French by speaking full sentences aloud.

questions.answer: Il va sans dire que ce projet est important.
questions.explanation: "Il va sans dire que ce projet est important." means "It goes without saying that this project is important"; "il va sans dire que" is a formal way to introduce something obvious.
"Cela va de soi." means "That goes without saying" or "Of course"; it is a polished way to say something is self-evident.

questions.answer: Je vous prie de bien vouloir excuser ce contretemps.
questions.explanation: "Je vous prie de bien vouloir excuser ce contretemps." means "Please kindly excuse this setback"; "je vous prie de bien vouloir" is a very polite formula used with vous in formal speech and letters.

questions.answer: Nous avons le plaisir de vous informer de notre décision.
questions.explanation: "Nous avons le plaisir de vous informer de notre décision." means "We are pleased to inform you of our decision"; "avoir le plaisir de" is a standard formal opening in official messages.

questions.answer: Veuillez trouver ci-joint le document demandé.
questions.explanation: "Veuillez trouver ci-joint le document demandé." means "Please find attached the requested document"; "veuillez trouver ci-joint" is the fixed formal phrase used in emails and letters.

questions.answer: Dans la mesure du possible, nous ferons de notre mieux.
questions.explanation: "Dans la mesure du possible, nous ferons de notre mieux." means "As far as possible, we will do our best"; "dans la mesure du possible" politely limits a promise.

questions.answer: Quoi qu'il en soit, nous devons avancer.
questions.explanation: "Quoi qu'il en soit, nous devons avancer." means "Be that as it may, we must move forward"; "quoi qu'il en soit" sets aside what was said before.
"Cela ne fait aucun doute." means "There is no doubt about it"; it is a formal way to express certainty.

questions.answer: Il n'en demeure pas moins que le problème persiste.
questions.explanation: "Il n'en demeure pas moins que le problème persiste." means "The fact remains that the problem persists"; "il n'en demeure pas moins que" is a formal way to say "nevertheless".

questions.answer: À vrai dire, je n'en sais rien.
questions.explanation: "À vrai dire, je n'en sais rien." means "To tell the truth, I have no idea"; "à vrai dire" introduces a frank admission, and "en" stands for "about it".

questions.answer: Tout compte fait, c'était une bonne décision.
questions.explanation: "Tout compte fait, c'était une bonne décision." means "All things considered, it was a good decision"; "tout compte fait" introduces a final judgement after weighing everything.

questions.answer: En fin de compte, cela n'a pas d'importance.
questions.explanation: "En fin de compte, cela n'a pas d'importance." means "In the end, it doesn't matter"; "en fin de compte" sums up a conclusion.
"Cela va sans dire." means "That goes without saying." It is a polished way to stress that something is obvious; "Ça va sans dire" is the everyday spoken form.

questions.answer: Je tiens à vous remercier de votre confiance.
questions.explanation: "Je tiens à vous remercier de votre confiance." means "I'd like to thank you for your trust." "Tenir à" + infinitive means "to be keen to", and "remercier de" introduces what you thank someone for, as in formal speeches and letters.

questions.answer: Nous restons à votre entière disposition.
questions.explanation: "Nous restons à votre entière disposition." means "We remain entirely at your service." It is a standard formal closing in business emails and letters.

questions.answer: C'est une question de bon sens.
questions.explanation: "C'est une question de bon sens." means "It's a matter of common sense." "Bon sens" is the French for common sense, and "une question de" means "a matter of".

questions.answer: Cela dit, il faut rester prudent.
questions.explanation: "Cela dit, il faut rester prudent." means "That said, we must remain cautious." "Cela dit" introduces a contrast or reservation after a point you have just made.

questions.answer: Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu.
questions.explanation: "Il n'y a pas de fumée sans feu." is the French version of "There's no smoke without fire." It suggests a rumour probably has some truth behind it; note "pas de" after the negative.
"Mieux vaut tard que jamais." means "Better late than never." The inverted "mieux vaut" (rather than "il vaut mieux") is typical of proverbs.
"Chaque chose en son temps." means "All in good time" or "One thing at a time." People use it to tell someone not to rush ahead.

questions.answer: Cela va de mal en pis.
questions.explanation: "Cela va de mal en pis." means "Things are going from bad to worse." "Pis" is an old comparative of "mal" that survives in this fixed expression.

questions.answer: Je vous saurais gré de bien vouloir répondre rapidement.
questions.explanation: "Je vous saurais gré de bien vouloir répondre rapidement." is a very polite formula for formal letters and emails; "je vous saurais gré de" means "I would be grateful if you would".

questions.answer: Nous vous prions de nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée.
questions.explanation: "Nous vous prions de nous excuser pour la gêne occasionnée." means "We apologise for any inconvenience caused." It is the standard formal apology in announcements and customer messages.
"C'est le monde à l'envers." literally means "It's the world upside down." You say it when something is absurd or the opposite of how it should be, like "What is the world coming to?"

questions.answer: En un mot, tout va bien.
questions.explanation: "En un mot, tout va bien." uses the idiom "en un mot" (in a word, in short) to sum up a situation briefly.
